[302] Ministry of Defence St.prop

[303] No. 48 (2007–

[304] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values Recommendation from the Ministry of Defense of March 28, 2008, approved by the Cabinet the same day

[305] Stoltenberg II Government

[306] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values ​​1.1 The purpose and function of the defense forces

[307] The military is the state's power apparatus to be able to defend itself

[308] Norway's security against external threats

[309] Military power is one of several instruments a sovereign state has to protect its interests, ensure national independence and political freedom of action

[310] The basic function of the Armed Forces is to protect and safeguard Norway's security, interests and values

[311] This means that the Armed Forces must be able to carry out a wide range of tasks in a credible manner

[312] The Armed Forces, together with our allies, shall contribute to defending Norway's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and to defending and enforcing Norway's sovereign rights

[313] The Armed Forces shall exercise Norwegian authority within defined areas, and contribute to preventing and handling episodes and security policy crises in Norway and its surrounding areas

[314] Furthermore, the Armed Forces shall contribute to collective defense and multinational crisis management, and to the work for international peace and security within the framework of international law and the UN Charter

[315] The Armed Forces must also contribute to safeguarding societal security, which has become increasingly important with a changing threat landscape

[316] Norway needs a defense force to help fulfill the fundamental and timeless responsibility of creating security for the state, the population and society

[317] Norwegian security and defense policy must also be based on the values and interests we wish to secure

[318] These values ​​mean that the state and its citizens can further develop the rule of law, democracy and ensure law and order, human rights and security

[319] Society must be able to safeguard and protect itself against serious threats to these values

[320] The most central role of the Armed Forces is to help prevent and handle security challenges against Norway and in Norwegian areas, and thereby help ensure stability and development in line with Norwegian interests

[321] In a globalized world, the Armed Forces must carry out this work both at home and abroad

[322] The continuation of a well-functioning democratic society, as well as the ability to create sustainable and environmentally conscious value, requires stable and peaceful development

[323] A credible defense is the state's most fundamental instrument for ensuring peace and stability

[324] A changed threat landscape has not changed this fundamental situation

[325] Despite the fact that the answer has been subject to significant changes, Norway still needs a relevant and finds 10 St.prp

[326] No. 48 2007–

[327] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values, a military defense adapted to a new era with new challenges

[328] Norway, as an integrated part of the international community, is obliged to safeguard its interests in cooperation with others, in a larger whole

[329] Norwegian security is strongly influenced by developments in our surroundings, regionally and globally

[330] Solutions to the vast majority of security challenges can only be created through close collaboration with others

[331] The value of being able to live in peace and freedom is the starting point for our desire to contribute actively to maintaining and developing an international legal order, defending human rights and strengthening intergovernmental cooperation

[332] In this perspective too, the Norwegian Defence Forces play a central role

[333] Both as a means of underpinning Norway's credibility by helping to meet common challenges faced by the international community, but also to ensure Norway's influence, political room for manoeuvre and support from others should the need arise

[334] A modern and flexible operational defense that helps meet common challenges internationally also underpins Norway's credibility and impact and power in other areas and in a broader perspective, and as a relevant actor internationally

[335] Credible and relevant contributions of force, not least for smaller countries like Norway, also provide leverage in international politics

[336] In a globalized world, clear contributions to the work for international peace and security, made visible through solidarity, burden-sharing and the ability to meet our obligations, are therefore not a supplement to national security and defense policy

[337] It is a crucial prerequisite for protecting important values, while safeguarding Norwegian interests in a comprehensive and effective manner

[338] The state has many instruments to secure Norwegian values ​​and interests

[339] Different challenges require different instruments

[340] In the work for international peace and security, political, military, developmental and humanitarian instruments are necessary

[341] To safeguard Norwegian security interests and international peace and stability, the Armed Forces must therefore be seen and used in close conjunction with other security policy instruments

[342] Good utilization of society's resources requires close cooperation between the military and civilian sides

[343] In many cases, the Armed Forces will not have the dominant role, but will still be an important player

[344] The armed forces must be integrated into Norwegian society

[345] This is important to ensure broad support and contribute to predictability of the Armed Forces' activities

[346] Society must have confidence that resources within the defense sector are used for the good of the community

[347] The government emphasizes that the role of military power is primarily to help create a foundation for establishing and implementing political solutions

[348] The government's political platform reflects a long-term ambition related to the development of the Defence Strategy in a bigger picture, where increased emphasis on societal security and the need to see the use of military force in the context of other instruments is central

[349] Within this framework, the government will emphasize further developing a modern and flexible operational defense that can safeguard Norway's security, interests and values' in a changing world

[350] The modernization of the Armed Forces

[351] The modernization of the defense sector has been absolutely necessary to ensure Norway has a timely and effective defense

[352] Since the end of the Cold War, the Norwegian Armed Forces have undergone significant development in line with a changing threat landscape and changes in the Armed Forces' other framework conditions

[353] Deconstruction and conversion attempts

[354] In light of, among other things, the recommendations from the Defence Commission of 1990, work was begun on significant changes to the structure and organisation of the Armed Forces

[355] This work continued throughout the 1990s, with a focus on reductions in the Armed Forces' structure, changes in organizational and management forms, and savings in operations and maintenance

[356] At the end of the decade, it was nevertheless clear that the Armed Forces were facing two fundamental imbalances

[357] between resource needs and resource supply and between the organization of the response and the tasks

[358] The defense was supposed to solve

[359] This was the background for the restructuring and modernization process that was initiated by the Stoltenberg I government in 2001, with a focus on changing the basic structure of the Armed Forces and creating a more sustainable long-term balance between tasks, level of ambition and access to resources

[360] Restructuring and modernization Since 2001, when the Stoltenberg I government presented the St.prp

[361] the Armed Forces have undergone an extensive restructuring and modernization process that is still ongoing

[362] Through this process, major changes have occurred, both in the tasks, structure and organization of the Armed Forces

[363] The restructuring has been challenging, both for the sector 11 2007–2008 St.prop

[364] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values as a whole and for its personnel

[365] At the same time, For the answer's operational ability and relevance have been improved

[366] The answer has been to develop relevant force contributions that meet a high international standard

[367] A better balance has been created between the Defence's tasks, structure and resource level

[368] A number of new military capabilities have been added to the defense structure

[369] This has provided an increased ability to carry out assignments both at home and abroad

[370] A wide range of organizational changes have been implemented that have contributed to more efficient operations

[371] The Armed Forces' property stock has been significantly reduced in size

[372] The personnel structure has undergone and is undergoing significant changes, both in terms of expertise and staffing

[373] In sum, this has enabled stronger prioritization of operational activities and the supply of new and modern equipment to the defense structure

[374] At the same time, major reforms have been carried out in the personnel area, with the introduction of the departmental officer system, calls for voluntary service for women, changes in the duty to order, and new educational systems better adapted to the civilian education system

[375] Significant reforms have also been implemented in the areas of administration, accounting and governance

[376] The main objectives have been to strengthen the defense sector's ability for comprehensive and long-term management, and to implement and follow up on political decisions

[377] Establishing integrated strategic management and introducing new management systems and tools have been key measures in this work

[378] These measures have yielded good results

[389] The army is under reconstruction after several years of extensive changes and the dismantling of the mobilization-based structure

[390] Extensive investments have been made in the naval defense structure, and with the new frigates in place, among other things, the Norwegian Navy will have a very high quality

[391] The significant modernization of the F-16 fighter jets and associated systems in recent years means that the combat air force today is very modern

[392] At the same time, in the medium term, the fighter fleet will reach the end of its service life and be ripe for replacement

[393] The Home Guard's comprehensive quality reform has contributed to the Home Guard being highly competent and well-equipped to carry out its tasks

[394] Emphasis has been placed on further developing a personnel structure with a more appropriate competence, rank and age profile, better adapted to the needs of the Armed Forces

[407] Consequences for the period 2009-2012 and in the longer term

[408] The restructuring of the defense sector from 2001 to the present day has created a good foundation for further developing the Forsvaret, both in the period 2009-2012 and in the longer term

[409] With this long-term plan, the transition is brought into a new phase with an emphasis on continuous 12 St.prop

[410] No. 48 2007–

[411] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values, development and adaptation to changes in needs and framework conditions

[412] Although much has been achieved in the work to modernize the Armed Forces, demanding challenges still remain, not least in a long-term perspective

[413] This applies above all to the need to ensure and further strengthen the balance between the Agency's tasks, structure and access to resources, as well as the need to create the most predictable and robust framework possible for the Agency's further development

[414] Several of the Armed Forces' central materiel systems will reach the end of their operational lifespan in the period to

[415] This involves necessary prioritization and major investments

[416] At the same time, the Armed Forces will be faced with increased demands and challenges related to the sum of the tasks that must be solved at home and abroad

[417] Strengthening the Armed Forces' ability to continuously improve and develop is therefore important

[418] Another key challenge is the ability to recruit and retain sufficient personnel with the right skills

[419] This is a crucial prerequisite for the defense sector to be able to solve assigned tasks in an efficient and credible manner, and for the organization to have the necessary flexibility to adapt to changes in a changing world

[420] The further development of the defense sector must therefore be a continuous process

[421] This will be crucial to ensure that Norway has a defense that is best adapted to the prevailing security environment and that is also designed to take into account new developments in a long-term perspective

[422] The Government's main priorities for the period 2009-2012 and beyond The Government wishes to continue the development of the Armed Forces based on the overall main defence policy priorities on which there has been broad political agreement in the Storting and the priorities that are based on the Soria Moria Declaration

[423] Defence capability and the High North

[424] The government places emphasis on strengthening the Armed Forces' ability to carry out basic national tasks, with a focus on presence and assertion of sovereignty in the North

[425] The government sees the highlands as Norway's most important strategic focus area in the years to come

[426] This should also be reflected in the further development of the Armed Forces

[427] Norway has a clear and concrete need for a credible defense and crisis management capability, which is also adapted to and underpins NATO's ability to safeguard our fundamental security

[428] The need arises from Norway's geopolitical location and strategic interests related to resource management in our local areas

[429] This dimension of our security situation distinguishes us from many of our allies and partners, who can largely refine their defenses against international intervention

[430] The conflict prevention role of the armed forces

[431] The Government places great emphasis on the Norwegian Armed Forces' conflict prevention role

[432] The armed forces shall be a means of contributing to stable and peaceful development both nationally and internationally

[433] The armed forces will in many cases be a means of helping to maintain stability and contribute to Norway's security policy framework developing in a desirable direction

[434] This will often be the primary purpose of using military forces, whether it concerns the exercise of authority, the assertion of sovereignty or incident and crisis management at home and abroad

[435] Relevant military presence to safeguard political freedom of action, which does not contribute to unintended escalation and which at the same time creates a sufficient conflict prevention effect, is central in this regard

[436] International cooperation on peace, security and defense National needs, and NATO's fundamental common needs related to the defense of the member states, must be the starting point for the development of the Norwegian Armed Forces' military capabilities

[437] At the same time, efforts must be made to ensure that the defense structure that is developed is relevant and applicable internationally

[438] Norway has neither the ability nor the goal to be able to defend itself alone against more extensive threats to its own security

[439] Norway's defense and crisis management capabilities depend on support from allies if the situation were to escalate to a level we cannot handle ourselves

[440] In a changed security picture, national security interests are also safeguarded through multinational crisis management and military efforts far from Norwegian areas

[441] An essential element in meeting Norway's national security needs is therefore to contribute to meeting NATO's basic common needs, and to contribute relevant and sought-after capabilities to the UN

[442] The government therefore places emphasis on strengthening Norwegian participation in the UN's peacekeeping operations, and on establishing a holistic approach to the work with 13 2007–2008 St.prop

[443] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values and to meet international challenges where political, military, humanitarian and development instruments are seen in context

[444] Multinational defense cooperation will become even more important in the future with a view to maintaining a sustainable and robust national defense capability

[445] Such cooperation will be especially important for smaller nations like Norway

[446] The Government therefore wants to have an active and broad approach to the work of further developing concrete collaborative solutions with close allies and partners

[447] Effective civil-military cooperation in the work of preventing and meeting the security challenges that Norway may face, a holistic approach to the use of military and civilian instruments must be sought

[448] A clear understanding of roles in which the various instruments are seen in context is important in this regard

[449] Furthermore, an approach must be sought where contributions from different authorities are mutually reinforcing elements in a combined effort

[450] The Government places increased emphasis on societal security, and will work to ensure that the Armed Forces, as one of several security policy instruments, are as relevant as possible in relation to the real security challenges Norway may face in the future

[451] Popular support, defense capability and will to defend

[452] The government wants a defense force with solid roots in society

[453] The organization and activities of the Armed Forces are in a mutually influencing relationship with developments in and expectations from civil society

[454] This must be reflected in the further development of the Armed Forces

[455] In this regard, defensive capability and will to defend are closely linked

[456] The armed forces must be perceived as relevant and credible, both by Norway's surroundings and by Norwegian society

[457] There is broad support among the population for Norway to have a military defense

[458] This support must be continuously confirmed and maintained by ensuring a broad anchoring of the Armed Forces as an integrated part of society and by creating confidence that resources are used for the good of the community

[459] This places high demands on the further development and modernization of the Armed Forces, and on communication, dialogue and transparency regarding the Armed Forces' activities

[460] Conscription as a foundation for the Armed Forces

[461] The Government will maintain the general duty of protection as a foundation for the Armed Forces' activities, adapted to a new era and the needs of the Armed Forces

[462] The duty to protect must constitute an important premise for the further development of the Armed Forces

[463] In addition to helping to ensure the necessary anchoring of the Armed Forces in the Norwegian population, conscription is crucial for ensuring that the Armed Forces have personnel with the right expertise

[464] The first-time service must therefore be developed continuously so that it has high quality and meaningful content

[465] It is therefore crucial that initial service plays a central role beyond ensuring recruitment to the Armed Forces

[466] Diversity and competence

[467] The Armed Forces shall be an inclusive workplace that reflects the diversity that characterizes Norwegian society in general

[468] The Armed Forces are also a competence-intensive organization

[469] A key challenge is therefore to recruit and retain sufficient personnel with the right expertise for civilian and military positions from all parts of the population

[470] This is especially true in today's tight job market

[471] The Government therefore places particular emphasis on measures that can help safeguard and further develop the crucial resource that the defence sector's personnel represent

[472] The personnel policy dimension must constitute a central part of long-term planning

[473] The Government also places great emphasis on increasing the proportion of women in the Armed Forces

[474] National and international industrial cooperation

[475] The Government will work based on the objective of developing cooperation between the Armed Forces and industry, in light of the emphasis the Government places on national and international defence materiel cooperation

[476] Based on the Armed Forces' needs and the strategy for industrial policy aspects of the Armed Forces' procurement, the government will facilitate a strengthened strategic partnership between the Armed Forces and industry

[477] Continued modernization The government wants a modern defense with the ability to meet new security challenges

[478] Developments in Norway's security policy environment underscore the need for a modern and flexible defence force that can help handle a wide range of different tasks, both at home and abroad

[479] Continuous development and adaptability

[480] It must be emphasized that the Armed Forces are capable of change and adaptability, and can continuously adapt to changes in the environment

[481] This will be a prerequisite for Norway to be able to meet future security and defense policy challenges in a credible and effective manner

[482] No. 48 2007–

[483] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values A holistic and long-term perspective

[484] A holistic and long-term perspective on the development of the Armed Forces must be established

[485] Given the long lead times associated with the Armed Forces' materiel investments and the production of military expertise, it is neither possible, appropriate nor desirable to implement sweeping changes in the Armed Forces based on short-term priorities

[486] A modern military defense requires highly specialized expertise and advanced equipment in many areas and levels

[487] A modern defense can only be maintained through continuous investments in expertise and materiel

[488] In a long-term perspective, it is crucial to have a defense structure that can provide a robust starting point for adapting to alternative development directions

[489] Predictability around the overarching political objectives and framework for the defense sector's activities is therefore crucial

[490] The Government emphasizes that the best possible consistency between the tasks should be created and maintained

[491] The Armed Forces are required to resolve and meet the conditions given

[492] This is both good defense policy and good economics

[493] The ability of the armed forces to carry out their tasks is crucial to whether Norway has an effective and good defense

[494] The Armed Forces' main deliverable is operational capability

[495] The Government's main objective for the further development of the Armed Forces is therefore to maintain and further develop the Armed Forces' operational capability, so that the Armed Forces' tasks are carried out in the best possible way

[496] This requires a defense that has relevant military capabilities with sufficient reaction capability, combat power, availability and endurance, and that is able to cooperate effectively with civilian actors, allies and partners

[497] In addition, the Armed Forces must appear as an attractive and exciting workplace

[498] The long-term plan for the period 2009-2012 and beyond St.prop

[499] No. 48 (2007-2008) contains the government's priorities and recommendations for the further development of the defense sector in the period 2009-2012 and beyond

[500] The proposal takes a holistic approach to future development, and sets out the main objectives and framework for the activities

[501] In working on the proposal, the recommendations from the Defence Policy Committee, cf. NOU 2007:15, with representatives from all the political parties in the Storting, and the Chief of Defence's Defence Study 07 have been drawn upon

[502] In the work on the proposition, great emphasis has been placed on broad inclusion and open debate, with extensive dialogue to promote the most democratic process possible linked to the further development of the Armed Forces

[503] The Ministry of Defence has received input and views from many quarters in the preparatory work, including by obtaining a broad range of views on the recommendations from the Defence Policy Committee and the Defence Study

[504] Furthermore, mayors from affected municipalities were invited to a dialogue conference, and the entire population was invited to present their views through an electronic consultation – forsvarsdialog.no – on the internet

[505] Based on this starting point, the government has placed emphasis on setting a main direction for the further development of the defence sector that reflects the objectives and priorities in the government's political platform, as set out in the Soria Moria Declaration

[506] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values

[507] In an increasingly volatile world, the main rationale for the Armed Forces must be to contribute to the fundamental and timeless responsibility of creating security for the state, the population and society, as well as to protect and promote our interests and values

[508] The armed forces are one of the state's most fundamental instruments in this context

[509] Norway's position in today's global security picture is primarily linked to two dimensions, both of great international, regional and national importance

[510] – Globalization challenges and new geopolitical developments that emphasize Norway's central position in relation to the strategically important high north, which in recent years has received increased international attention, politically, economically and environmentally

[511] – Regional resource management where Norway has a central position with regard to both energy and fishery resources, and which in the resource area means that we have far greater strategic weight than the country's size and population would otherwise indicate

[512] Norway's geopolitical location and strategic resource interests mean that we face increasing challenges in our immediate areas

[513] This dimension of our security policy situation distinguishes us from many of our allies

[514] For this reason, the High North is the government's most important strategic focus area

[515] This should also be reflected in the further development of the Armed Forces

[516] The most central role of the Armed Forces is to help ensure Norwegian sovereignty and prevent and handle security challenges in our immediate areas, thereby contributing to safeguarding our security, interests, values ​​and regional stability

[517] This also indicates an emphasis on national tasks such as asserting sovereignty and crisis management, through military presence

[518] The challenges of globalization are also the clearest expression of the fact that Norwegian security could be strongly influenced by international developments

[519] As an integrated part of the international community, Norway must safeguard its interests in close cooperation with others

[520] Norway also has many interests that we share with others, including actively contributing to promoting a UN-led world order, ensuring respect for human rights and strengthening intergovernmental cooperation

[521] In a globalized world, contributions to the work for international peace and security are therefore not a supplement to our national security, but a prerequisite for safeguarding it

[522] The safeguarding of our shared interests and values therefore takes place today through the active participation of the Armed Forces both at home and abroad, and there is no contradiction in this

[523] The Government's main priorities In the Soria Moria Declaration, the Government based itself on a number of priorities that are in line with the most fundamental and partly timeless Norwegian interests

[524] This concerns the High North as Norway's most important strategic focus area, the importance of a UN-led world order, contributions to the development of NATO, and an active European policy

[525] The Government also emphasizes that the Armed Forces should be developed as a modern, flexible and alliance-adapted security policy instrument, with a balance between tasks, structure and access to resources

[526] The Government therefore recommends a significant financial boost for the Armed Forces

[527] Today's challenges, both regionally and internationally, emphasize the need for a credible military defense as one of the key instruments for protecting Norway's security, interests and values, which may come under increasing pressure in the years ahead

[528] The role of military power is to create a basis for political solutions

[529] The military as a political instrument is fundamentally intended to prevent war, not wage war

[530] The use of military force must have legitimacy both nationally and internationally, and the Armed Forces must, not least, have solid support among the population

[531] The Government places great emphasis on the Norwegian Armed Forces' conflict prevention role

[532] This applies both nationally, where the Armed Forces contribute to regional stability and predictability through their presence and routine activities, and in connection with 16 St.prop

[533] No. 48 2007–

[534] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values, military participation abroad, as a contribution to stable and peaceful development internationally

[535] Today's security challenges are complex, and the Armed Forces will in many cases be only one of several instruments

[536] This requires a more holistic approach where military instruments are seen in conjunction with other efforts, with the aim of optimal use of the combined resources

[537] This applies both in connection with participation in peacekeeping operations abroad, and as part of the Armed Forces' role in contributing to societal security at home

[538] The Government places emphasis on societal security, and will work to ensure that the Armed Forces, as one of several security policy instruments, are as relevant as possible in relation to the challenges Norway may face in the future

[539] An approach must be sought in which contributions from different sectors of society emerge as mutually reinforcing elements in a joint effort

[540] The Armed Forces' main deliverable is operational capability

[541] The decisive factor in whether Norway has an effective Norwegian defense is therefore that the Armed Forces have the real ability to carry out their tasks

[542] National needs and NATO's

[543] Fundamental common needs must be the starting point for the development of the Armed Forces' military capabilities

[544] General conscription shall continue to be a foundation for the defense structure, and is at the same time an important link between the Armed Forces and the people

[545] The government plans to continue conscription at a robust level, with a clear operational justification

[546] Conscripts in their first year of service shall continue to have a central place in the operational units of the defense branches

[547] Defensive ability and defensive will are closely related

[548] The defense must be perceived as relevant and credible, both by Norway's surroundings and by Norwegian society

[549] There is broad support and enthusiasm among the Norwegian people for the Armed Forces

[550] This support must be maintained by ensuring a strong anchoring of the Armed Forces in the population – as an integrated part of society

[551] Therefore, it is also important that the Defence can recruit workers from the entire population to a greater extent than today

[552] Gradual change in the security policy environment

[553] Globally, we are faced with a complex security policy picture, which also has several worrying features

[554] The most important new thing is a gradual, but still fundamental, change in the geopolitical picture

[555] Developments in countries such as China, India and Russia are moving us from a unipolar to a more multipolar world order

[556] As a result, we see an increasing tendency towards great power rivalry

[557] The territorial state and state security also seem to be gaining in importance, with consequences also in our immediate vicinity, both in the political, resource-related and military areas

[558] At the same time, the challenges of globalization related to global poverty and environmental challenges, increased competition for strategic raw materials, international terrorism and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction continue and are partly intensified

[559] This can also lead to security policy challenges in various ways, locally, regionally and internationally

[560] For Norway, this is primarily a threat to societal security, but potentially also to our national security

[561] Internal and cross-border conflicts also have serious consequences, both locally and regionally, not least for human rights, regional stability and local social development

[562] International developments emphasize that Norway continues to benefit from challenges being resolved on the basis of international law and multilateral security arrangements, above all the UN

[563] Furthermore, an effective and credible NATO, based on the collective security guarantee and adapted to current challenges, remains a cornerstone of Norwegian security policy

[564] Norway therefore has a vital interest in helping NATO remain relevant and strengthen its role as the primary framework for transatlantic security cooperation

[565] The challenges in our local areas are partly a function of the global challenges, and as such can only be solved within a broad multilateral framework

[566] At the same time, Norway is facing challenges in the north that must mainly be resolved nationally, related to ongoing resource management and unresolved jurisdictional issues

[567] Potential conflicts of interest in the resource area mean that we cannot rule out the possibility that situations with security policy aspects may arise

[568] The strategic importance of the High North, both economically, environmentally and militarily, combined with uncertainty related to developments in Russia, indicates that this is an area that must have high priority, also within security and defense policy

[569] Future challenges to Norwegian security will primarily be various forms of political pressure, or through violations and episodes that challenge Norwegian sovereignty

[570] These will most likely be of limited military scope, but could arise quickly, requiring rapid handling

[571] This requires military forces with high operational quality, sufficient responsiveness and endurance, extensive strategic and tactical mobility, and the necessary self-protection

[572] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values

[573] Taken together, the challenges require that the Norwegian Defence Force must be able to solve tasks both at home and abroad

[574] This indicates further development of a modern and flexible emergency defense that can help handle a wide range of tasks

[575] Today's complex security policy challenges also place higher demands than before on a comprehensive policy from the Norwegian side, where security and defense policy must in many cases be seen in close connection with foreign policy, economic, industrial, development and environmental aspects

[576] Security and defense policy goals Developments in the environment indicate that the current main security policy goals should remain unchanged

[577] Maintaining Norway's sovereignty, territorial integrity and political freedom of action is a fundamental security interest, which is not least expressed through the comprehensive High North initiative

[578] Another fundamental security interest is to contribute to a multilateral world order under the leadership of the UN, with an emphasis on international law and universal human rights, as an expression of international solidarity and strengthening of the UN

[579] Norway also has a vital interest in maintaining and strengthening the transatlantic security community through NATO

[580] – To prevent war and the emergence of various threats to Norwegian and collective security

[581] – To contribute to peace, stability and the further development of a UN-led international legal order

[582] – To safeguard Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights, interests and values and protect Norwegian freedom of action against political, military and other pressure

[583] – Together with our allies, defend Norway and NATO against attacks and threats

[584] – To secure society against attacks and threats from state and non-state actors

[585] Based on these objectives, the government's main defense policy goal is to further develop a defense that is capable of adapting to developments and meeting the challenges of rapidly changing environments, in order to protect Norway's security, interests and values

[586] This requires a modern and flexible operational defense force, which can participate in the full range of operations, at home and abroad

[587] The defense policy goals are closely linked to the tasks of the Armed Forces

[588] The Norwegian Armed Forces shall, within its area of responsibility and in cooperation with other national authorities, contribute to fulfilling these objectives

[589] Defence policy objectives: – Alone and together with allies, secure Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights, interests and values, and preserve Norwegian freedom of action against military and other pressure

[590] – Through participation in multinational peace operations anchored in a clear and unambiguous international legal basis and international defense cooperation, contribute to peace, stability, enforcement of international law and respect for human rights, as well as prevent the use of force by states and non-state actors against Norwegian and international security

[591] – Together with allies, contribute to the collective defense of Norway and other allies in accordance with our alliance commitments, and to meet various types of attacks and threats to ensure Norwegian and collective security

[592] – Contribute to safeguarding Norwegian societal security, saving lives and limiting the consequences of accidents, disasters, attacks and attacks from state and non-state actors

[593] The operationalization of the defense policy goals occurs through the defense concept, which sets out the fundamental principles for the structure, organization and activities of the Armed Forces

[594] The defence concept emphasises the importance of developing the defence as a modern, flexible and alliance-adapted security policy instrument, where a balance is sought between tasks, structure and access to resources, and where activities are based on close cooperation with civilian authorities and on conscription

[595] Defence policy development in a holistic and long-term perspective

[596] Defence policy shall lay the foundation for the development of the Armed Forces' structure and capabilities, as well as for the development and composition of expertise

[597] It is therefore crucial to establish a holistic and long-term perspective on development

[598] A holistic perspective requires that defense policy is based on the sum of the overall strategic trends and challenges that characterize the Armed Forces' environment, and the main security policy priorities that are based on these

[599] It further emphasizes the need to 18 St.prop

[601] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values sees the Armed Forces' efforts in close connection with other instruments, and to see the Armed Forces' activities at home and abroad as two sides of the same coin

[603] At the same time, it must be taken into account that the future is characterized by uncertainty and unpredictability, and that the Defence must be able to adapt to the greatest possible extent to the various and most likely developments that could affect the environment in the longer term

[604] In other words, the defense must be as scenario-robust and threat-independent as possible

[605] Participation in peace-support operations abroad is a contribution to international peace and security, which in our globalized world is increasingly determining our national security

[607] Multinational cooperation is becoming increasingly important as a prerequisite for military cooperation with allies and partners, and for maintaining robust and sustainable national defense structures

[608] The government wants a clear focus on multi-national cooperation, with both allies and partners, as a means of contributing to long-term balanced defense development

[609] The Armed Forces' level of ambition and tasks

[610] The Armed Forces shall carry out the tasks assigned to it by the country's political authorities at any given time, within the defined level of ambition and the established framework

[611] The ability to solve both routine and more demanding and varied individual assignments, using a significantly smaller structure than previously, requires a clarified and realistic level of ambition

[612] This places high demands on the consistency between political expectations and military capability, which in turn requires a balance between given tasks and allocated resources

[613] The essence of defense policy and defense planning, and the entire alignment of the Armed Forces, was long based on a known threat and an identified enemy

[614] Faced with today's threat landscape, the defense policy approach is rather the opposite

[615] That Norway has values to protect and interests to defend, in principle regardless of what or who one might have to defend these against

[616] This is also fundamental to how the Armed Forces should be developed

[617] The defense policy ambition is a dimension for what kind of military defense Norway should have, in the same way that the ambition is determined based on what the nation believes it should possess in terms of military power, in terms of defense capability

[620] Furthermore, the Armed Forces must be sufficiently threat-independent

[621] The defense must be flexible enough to be able to handle various challenges and missions, within a clarified framework of ambition, based on an inherent ability for rapid change and adaptation

[622] The main task of the Armed Forces is to develop and apply military power, to deliver operational capability

[643] Effective and integrated management

[644] The top leadership of the Armed Forces has undergone major changes, and today's integrated model has contributed to significant improvements within the areas that the Storting based on when the model was adopted

[645] The government plans to strengthen those parts of the model that have worked well, while also initiating certain measures to improve the management apparatus in areas where challenges have been identified

[646] The strategic leadership is gathered in the joint leadership building at Akershus Fortress, with the Chief of Defence and his military strategic functions integrated into the Ministry of Defence

[647] The government wishes to continue the main features of the existing management model, with some changes

[648] These changes are primarily aimed at improving the Ministry's ability to address the need for comprehensive strategic planning and effective management of the sector

[649] In order to facilitate strengthened strategic follow-up, leadership and control in the defence branches, as well as establish a clearer management structure in the Defence, the Inspectors General and their staff functions, which are currently located in the Defence Staff, will be located at the respective centres of gravity for their activities

[650] Together with functions and expertise that are currently organized at the underlying levels in the defense branches, a robust and clear level of management for force production in the respective defense branches is hereby established

[651] To also strengthen operational management, the current two operational headquarters are being merged into one, where management resources on the operational side are being pooled into one robust environment

[652] The headquarters will be located at Reitan near Bodø, thereby also contributing to strengthening the military presence and leadership in the north

[653] A relevant operational structure

[654] The challenges in our local areas appear to be greater than previously thought

[655] When designing the operational structure of the Armed Forces, great emphasis must therefore be placed on national needs and tasks

[656] For Norway to have a credible ability to carry out these tasks, a sufficient breadth of capabilities is required

[657] At the same time, Norway's contribution to international crisis management through the UN and NATO remains of fundamental importance

[658] Alliance affiliation must therefore also be reflected in the force structure, by basing Norwegian forces on NATO standards to the greatest extent possible, with the aim of being able to operate closely with allies across the entire spectrum of conflicts

[659] This requires forces with sufficient quality, responsiveness, endurance, strategic and tactical mobility, as well as self-protection and training standards

[660] The challenges both at home and abroad underscore the importance of forces that are capable of responding at short notice, with high mobility and deployability

[661] At the same time, our forces must have sufficient endurance to be able to contribute abroad together with allies and partners over time

[662] The government places emphasis on developing an operational structure with the best possible balance between responsiveness and resilience

[663] The Armed Forces must have the ability to effectively handle national tasks – both ongoing and those that may arise – while the Armed Forces are engaged in operations abroad

[664] The structure must therefore not only have sufficient breadth, but within relevant capacities also sufficient depth to ensure the ability to operate simultaneously at home and abroad

[665] With the current task portfolio and the determined level of ambition, the government's recommendation is to – in the main – continue the current structure and 2008 parliamentary proposals

[679] An appropriate base and support structure

[680] The Armed Forces' base and support structure must primarily contribute to ensuring that the Armed Forces can carry out its tasks in the most efficient manner possible, and must be based on the needs associated with operational activities

[681] It is an overarching goal for the government to further develop the Armed Forces' base and support structure so that it best supports the operational structure and the Armed Forces' operations

[736] The basis for a relevant defense

[737] The entirety of the measures proposed in this proposal will contribute to ensuring a modern and flexible operational defence, adapted to the need to protect Norway's security, interests and values, and with the ability to adapt to a changing world

[738] It is a robust defense system designed to handle a wide range of different tasks, both nationally and internationally

[739] The Government is continuing its work to fulfill the level of ambition set out in the Soria Moria Declaration and the initiatives set out therein

[740] The Armed Forces must have military capabilities with the necessary reaction and response capabilities, availability and endurance, with conscription and popular support as the foundation, and effective cooperation with civilians, allies and partners as a prerequisite – to provide Norway with the military defense, with the operational capability, that our society needs

[741] This foundation is strengthened through this proposition

[742] The primary goal of this long-term plan is to continue and further develop the Armed Forces' operational structure and capabilities

[743] To contribute to this, changes are planned related to support activities and the base structure, as well as to leadership, management, personnel and expertise in the defense sector

[744] The sum of the recommended measures, changes and frameworks described here will bring the Armed Forces a long step towards the stated ambition and goal, and create a solid starting point for continuous further development

[745] This does not mean that the modernization of the Defence Force has been completed, but that efforts should be made to bring the development of the Defence Force onto a more stable and predictable track

[746] The goal is to create a situation where development occurs more through gradual adjustments within the framework of long-term goals, rather than through frequent and all-encompassing reforms

[747] It has therefore been crucial for the government to lay the foundation for sustainability in the defence sector by continuing and further developing what has been achieved through modernisation since 2001, as a basis for further strengthening the Defence Forces

[748] The Government therefore recommends a significant financial boost for the Armed Forces

[749] Such sustainable development, which can help ensure a long-term balance between the Armed Forces' tasks, structure and access to resources, however, requires that the assumptions on which the proposals are based are actively followed up

[750] On the one hand, this is about creating predictability regarding the financial basis for the further development of the Armed Forces, and on the other hand, it is also largely about the sector's own responsibility for using allocated funds in an efficient and responsible manner – for the good of the community

[751] –2008 St.prop

[752] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values Security policy framework 3.1 Security in a global world

[753] Norwegian security policy is shaped in the span between our fundamental security policy interests and objectives, our security policy environment, and the security policy instruments we have at our disposal to safeguard our interests

[754] In this respect, the military is a crucial instrument

[755] Norway's fundamental security policy interests and objectives reflect Norway's position as a small state with a strategic location, a Euro-Atlantic anchorage and a clear emphasis on multilateral security arrangements and international solidarity

[756] These interests are reflected in the government's political platform, the Soria Moria Declaration, and are of an overarching and partly timeless nature

[757] The safeguarding of Norwegian security interests must also be seen in light of the security policy environment

[758] The international community today faces a broad spectrum of security challenges, which are constantly changing

[759] Internationally, it concerns both new geopolitical developments and ongoing globalization challenges

[760] At the same time, Norway faces significant regional challenges related to resource management, military strategic issues and the environment

[761] Norway's security policy situation is also characterized by the fact that we are located in a strategically sensitive area, with NATO, the EU and Russia as key players

[762] Developments among these key players – as well as in the UN and the Nordic countries – constitute important premises for Norwegian security policy

[763] We are facing gradual, but nonetheless fundamental changes in the international landscape

[764] The main international development is not necessarily negative

[765] However, it is characterized by several worrying features with consequences for, among other things, the role of the territorial state and the UN, key arms control regimes, and with possible consequences for Western security cooperation

[766] In addition, there are security challenges in our immediate areas, which place increased demands on Norway as a regional player

[767] The spectrum of challenges places great demands on a comprehensive policy from the Norwegian side that not only encompasses security and defense policy aspects, but also elements of a foreign policy, economic, industrial development and environmental nature

[768] In relation to the overall challenges, the Armed Forces also play an important role

[769] It is important that there is a connection between security policy, defense policy and the alignment of the Armed Forces' structure

[770] This is a prerequisite for strengthening the long-term balance between the Armed Forces' tasks, structure and access to resources

[771] Norway's security policy interests and objectives The main objective of security policy is to safeguard Norway's fundamental security interests and objectives

[772] In the Soria Moria Declaration, the government established priorities that confirm that several of these interests are safeguarded through the government's most important areas of focus, including the High North, the importance of a UN-led world order, contributions to the development of NATO and an active European policy

[773] Developments have shown that all of these priorities were correct

[774] Safeguarding our sovereignty, territorial integrity and political freedom of action is a fundamental security interest that is expressed through the government's High North initiative

[775] Another fundamental security interest is to contribute to a multilateral world order under the UN with an emphasis on international law and human rights

[776] This is an expression of international solidarity, but also an expression that it is in the interest of small states to establish international rules of engagement, including for the use of military force

[777] The government has taken the consequences of this by actively working to strengthen the UN's role in conflict resolution, and by increasing our contributions to UN-led operations

[778] Norway also has a vital interest in maintaining and strengthening the transatlantic security community through NATO

[779] The alliance constitutes a cornerstone of Norwegian security policy, through collective defense and cooperation with close allies

[780] This is demonstrated by the emphasis we place on maintaining NATO's traditional role linked to the response of member states, and also by the fact that NATO's main commitment, International Security Assistance 24 St.prp

[781] No. 48 2007–

[782] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values. Stance Force (ISAF) is Norway's main international commitment

[783] An increasing scope of cross-border threats means that Norway's security interests today must also be safeguarded by contributing to stability outside the Euro-Atlantic area

[784] Persistent challenges related to regional conflicts, resulting in human rights violations, can in many cases only be resolved through direct intervention by the international community

[785] The same applies to cross-border global security challenges related to international terrorism and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction

[786] Norway's military engagements abroad are geographically wide-ranging and currently extend from Afghanistan across the Middle East and to Africa

[787] Finally, as a result of our location, Norway has a fundamental security interest in helping Russia cooperate well with the Western community

[788] This is important both for international development in general, and for stability in our immediate areas in particular

[789] Cooperation eastwards is an integral part of the government's High North policy

[790] Based on our fundamental security policy interests, Norway's main security policy objectives today can be listed as follows

[791] – To prevent war and the emergence of various threats to Norwegian and collective security

[792] – To contribute to peace, stability and the further development of a UN-led international legal order

[793] – To safeguard Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights, interests and values and protect Norwegian freedom of action against political, military and other pressure

[794] – Together with our allies, defend Norway and NATO against attacks and threats

[795] – To secure society against attacks and threats from state and non-state actors

[796] In achieving these objectives, the Armed Forces will be one of several key security policy instruments available to the Norwegian authorities

[797] also chapter

[798] The design of Norwegian security policy must be based on the fact that the concept of security itself has acquired a broader and more complex content

[799] It no longer encompasses only state security, but also societal security and human security

[800] The most important perception of the purpose of security policy has been and continues to be state security, as the fundamental security need related to the existence, sovereignty and integrity of the state

[801] While state security in our part of the world before 1990 was linked to the threat of invasion, the situation after 1990 has been primarily characterized by the danger of various forms of political and military pressure, and limited episodes, crises and attacks

[802] At the same time, the spread and use of weapons of mass destruction can ultimately lead to such extensive damage that the vital interests or existence of the state are threatened

[803] The emergence of new security challenges has also resulted in the very structure of society becoming a target for attacks by non-state actors

[804] A consequence of this is the need for increased emphasis on social security

[805] This is about safeguarding the safety of the civilian population and securing central societal functions and important infrastructure against attack and other damage, but without threatening the existence of the state

[806] International developments since 1990 have also led to more attention being paid to human security

[807] This is about protecting the individual, where human rights and the right to life and personal security are at the center

[808] Consideration of human security is essential to the developments we have seen in recent years, where the international community has felt compelled to intervene, including with military means

[809] Norway's security policy environment – ​​a changing world

[810] New geopolitical developments

[811] The first decade after the Cold War was a period in which the most important challenges were related to conflicts within states, human rights violations and regional instability

[812] With September 11, 2001, asymmetric threats in the form of international terrorism were further accentuated as a threat to the international community

[813] Throughout the period, however, the Western countries, led by the United States, emerged as the global center of gravity

[814] Today – just over 15 years after the Cold War – this picture is also ripe for revision

[815] We are now witnessing the emergence of new great powers such as China and India with regional and to some extent global ambitions, and at the same time the revitalization of former great powers such as Russia

[816] This reflects new geopolitical developments, which may lead to changes in the global balance of power itself

[817] The United States is still the world's most influential country, by virtue of its economy, and not least militarily, where the United States will continue to have superior capabilities

[818] At the same time, we see a gradual reduction in the United States' relative power and influence

[819] The 25th 2007–2008 St.prop

[820] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values is partly due to the emergence of new global players such as China and India, developments in Russia, but also ongoing American military engagements, including in Iraq, which tie up large resources

[821] Developments in and around Iraq have created a new situation in this region, with a strengthened Iran and a shift in the balance of power in an area of ​​great importance for the world's energy supply

[822] The most important feature in the international picture is the development in China

[823] With a background of strong economic development, China already constitutes the world's fourth largest economy, and at the current rate of development, it will be able to overtake the United States and become the world's leading economy in a few decades

[824] The country's foreign policy is characterized by responsibility, but at the same time with the goal of increasing its influence globally

[825] It will take many decades before China eventually has the military capability of the United States globally

[826] However, in the long term and by virtue of its economic weight, China may have the potential to become a global player on par with the United States

[827] China already has a major impact on global economic cycles and environmental issues, political and economic developments in Africa and Asia, and efforts to prevent the spread of weapons of mass destruction

[828] Russia is also back on the international stage

[829] The country is outwardly characterized by economic freedom of action and great power ambitions

[830] Internally, we have seen a development towards centralization of power and nationalist rhetoric

[831] Today's main trend will likely persist

[832] Internal developments are combined with a more strained relationship between Russia and important Western countries

[833] This comes to the surface in a number of issues such as the question of Kosovo's status, missile defense, arms control agreements, further NATO expansion, and more

[834] Compared to the United States and China, Russia will primarily be a regional power

[835] However, Russia, by virtue of its territory, raw materials and partly military capability, will be able to play a significant role, both in relation to the Caucasus, Central Asia and Europe, including the Nordic countries

[836] The EU's role as a more independent actor will create increased interdependence and will initially have a positive and stabilizing effect in relation to other major actors

[837] The EU has maximized its influence through the design of an international rules-based system where multilateralism and human rights are central, and these are principles that are also central to Norway

[838] At the same time, we cannot rule out that greater equality between the EU and other major players could lead to increased tension, both internally on the Western side and in relation to Russia

[839] Global security challenges

[840] We are also in the global age

[841] The impacts of the globalization process are partly positive, in the form of increased flow of information, technology and labor, increased trade, less poverty and more prosperity, as well as a general increasing international interdependence

[842] However, it also brings challenges

[843] National authorities have had reduced control over their own social development

[844] Less developed countries will be less able to benefit from the benefits of globalization than well-organized countries, with the consequent risk of economic and political instability and, in the worst case, state collapse

[845] Globalization and more open borders have also contributed to intensifying serious challenges in the area of security policy, in the form of threats related to international terrorism, the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and ballistic weapon technology, and information warfare

[846] The challenges are often asymmetrical, in that militarily inferior actors are given the opportunity to strike their opponents in areas other than where they are militarily superior

[847] The challenges are more complex, and the transition between peace, crisis and war correspondingly vague

[848] The threats can arise quickly, are cross-border and have consequences far beyond their place of origin

[849] International terrorism as a result of extreme political Islamism affects both Muslim and Western countries, and most often the civilian population

[850] Terrorism finds its roots in what still characterizes many areas of the world, namely a lack of political, economic and social development, and is also often associated with weakly founded states and crime

[851] This means that we are facing a long-term challenge, with potential security policy consequences both regionally and in relation to our own country

[852] The spread of weapons of mass destruction and ballistic weapon technology to new states poses a growing threat

[853] It also appears particularly worrying that such weapons could in the future also be spread to and used by non-state actors

[854] The entire non-proliferation regime is under pressure, and the next five to ten years will likely be decisive for the direction in which developments take place

[855] It cannot be ruled out that the current development with spread to new states will continue

[856] Should the non-proliferation regime collapse, it could have very serious consequences for stability both regionally and globally

[857] In the future, we may experience weapons of mass destruction in the hands of regimes with a declared adversarial relationship with Europe and the United States, and where traditional deterrence will not necessarily have an effect

[867] Early in the 21st century, developments are characterized by increased global competition for a number of important strategic raw materials such as minerals, grain and rice, fish and fossil energy in the form of oil and gas

[868] Competition is intensified by strong economic growth in large countries such as China and India, which has led to increased commodity prices and intensified exploitation of resources both on land and at sea

[936] NATO has shown great ability to adapt and has gradually adapted to a changing security policy situation

[1064] Security policy consequences for Norway As described above, we are today faced with a complex security policy picture with several worrying features

[1065] The overall challenges include new geopolitical developments, ongoing globalization challenges related to terrorism and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, increasing global environmental challenges and competition for strategic resources, combined with significant national resource challenges in our own areas

[1066] All of the challenges will affect Norway and Norwegian interests in different ways, while our opportunities to influence some of the challenges alone will be very limited

[1067] The spectrum of challenges means that high demands must be made on a comprehensive policy from the Norwegian side that not only encompasses security and defense policy in the traditional sense, but where foreign policy, economics, industry, development and environmental policy will also play an important role

[1296] In the area of resources, there is even the potential for Norway and some allies to have conflicting interests

[1298] In addition, this underlines the importance of prioritizing bilateral cooperation with close allies such as the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany and the Netherlands

[1302] There are requirements that Norway contribute relevant and visible forces to any allied operation in Norway, including credible host country and reception arrangements

[1304] A number of the challenges in the North, especially in the area of resources, are also of such a nature that they must mainly be handled with national resources

[1306] This is crucial for national control over development in the area

[1310] Asserting sovereignty, as well as the ability to handle incidents and crises, is also becoming important and requires forces with high responsiveness, mobility and a flexible range of instruments

[1311] The challenges in our immediate area appear likely to become greater rather than less, and this must be reflected in our security and defense policy

[1312] Our ability to assert our sovereignty and to manage episodes and crises in our immediate areas is fundamental here

[1313] This is not about going back to Cold War defense, or about significantly raising the level of ambition for the tasks handled nationally

[1317] The fact that the Armed Forces can assist the civilian sector in an effective manner in relevant situations is also of great importance both from a societal perspective and for the legitimacy of the Armed Forces

[1318] Norway's overall challenges in the North underline the importance of military presence, both in the form of national and allied training and exercises, its own operations in peacetime, and permanent installations and infrastructure with fixed activity

[1319] The Armed Forces currently conduct 24/7 operations in the North related to surveillance, assertion of sovereignty and exercise of authority, and a relevant military presence is a prerequisite for being able to carry out these tasks in a credible manner

[1320] Presence also strengthens the ability to prevent and handle incidents and crises up to a certain level without requiring the deployment of additional capacities, and as such is conflict prevention

[1321] The main challenges in the North are largely related to the sea areas, but also affect the land and air territory

[1322] This requires a regular Norwegian military presence in and over these sea areas, with an emphasis on areas where Norwegian jurisdiction is disputed

[1323] We must also have the ability to quickly assert sovereignty over the airspace, as a prerequisite for the Armed Forces' ability to contribute to crisis management and to ensure national freedom of action

[1324] The probability of extensive violations of Norwegian land territory is assumed to be far less, but there is still a need for a relevant military presence here as well

[1326] Norway therefore has a fundamental interest in continuing and intensifying the work towards a trusting relationship between our two countries, both bilaterally and through institutions such as the NATO-Russia Council (NRC
