[1329] The Armed Forces as a security policy instrument

[1330] Holistic approach to the use of security policy instruments International developments since 1990 have had consequences for the view on the use of military force as a security policy instrument

[1331] On the one hand, the risk of extensive military conflicts has been greatly reduced

[1332] On the other hand, the emergence of regional conflicts with gross violations of human rights has led to increased international acceptance of intervention by the international community towards sovereign states

[1333] As a result, the use of military force has become more visible

[1334] Use of military 39 2007–2008 St.prop

[1335] A defense force to protect Norway's security, interests and values may be relevant both to prevent potential crises and in connection with long-term stabilization of the situation in a conflict area

[1336] We must assume that the reality of the future will also be characterized by conflicts, war and emergency situations where the use of military force will be necessary

[1337] This means that the Armed Forces will be an important foreign and security policy instrument

[1338] However, in dealing with future security challenges, military capabilities will often not be the dominant security policy instrument

[1339] Military instruments will often have a suppressive function

[1340] Active use of military force must be a last resort, after other means have been tried, or as an integrated part of a comprehensive approach that also includes other means

[1341] The purpose of such use of force will in all cases be to achieve political objectives

[1342] In general, it will only be appropriate for Norway to use military means of force nationally in connection with limited situations related to the assertion of Norwegian sovereignty, the exercise of authority and contributions to crisis management

[1343] In all other situations, the Armed Forces will operate within a multinational framework, in or outside Norway

[1344] The framework for Norwegian use of military power

[1345] The framework for Norway's use of military force dictates that this must always be anchored in international law, either through consent from the parties, through the right to individual or collective self-defense pursuant to Article 51 of the UN Charter, or through a mandate from the UN Security Council pursuant to Chapter VI or VII of the UN Charter

[1346] In today's operations, situations may also arise where parties to a conflict deliberately violate principles related to proportionality and the protection of non-combatants

[1347] This will place great demands on the Armed Forces' ability to deal with difficult situations under international law, and must therefore be reflected in training and education

[1348] Total defence and civil-military cooperation

[1349] The changing risk picture and increased emphasis on societal security have also led to a changed pattern of civil-military cooperation, within the framework of a changed total defense concept

[1350] This involves mutual support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society on both prevention, emergency planning and operational matters

[1351] In addition to situations where the Armed Forces will have primary responsibility, cf. chapter 5.5, the Armed Forces may be able to make military resources available to help solve tasks that civilian institutions do not have the resources to solve alone

[1352] It is a prerequisite that the Norwegian Defence contributes based on available capacities, expertise and resources that have been established to solve the primary tasks

[1353] The Armed Forces' support to civil society is broad-ranging, and includes search and rescue both at sea and on land, assistance in connection with major accidents, crises and natural disasters, other assistance to the police in accordance with the assistance directive, as well as the decontamination and removal of explosives

[1354] In addition, the Intelligence Service and the National Security Authority have tasks for civil society, as well as the special and ongoing responsibility

[1355] The Coast Guard and Border Guard have to exercise Norwegian authority in delimited areas

[1356] Furthermore, the agreement with the Norwegian Coastal Administration on coastal preparedness and action management (Coastal Preparedness and Action Management) gives the Armed Forces the authority to implement measures and lead efforts in crisis situations at sea and along the coast, until the agency with primary responsibility can take over

[1357] Reference is made to a more detailed discussion of the Total Defence Force and civil-military cooperation in Chapter

[1358] Crisis situations requiring close coordination between the military and civilian sectors

[1359] The need for cooperation between the civilian and military sectors is reinforced by the fact that in today's international threat landscape, undesirable events that can be defined in the area between crime and armed attack cannot be ruled out

[1360] The clearest example of this may be terrorist attacks, which often have an international dimension, may be of a magnitude that exceeds what the civilian sector can handle alone, and whose main aim is to influence or pressure the country's political authorities

[1361] In these cases, in extraordinary situations, one may be faced with a security crisis, even if one is not dealing with an armed attack in the traditional sense

[1362] Such a crisis situation will require efforts and close cooperation between civilian and military resources to prevent threats, combat them and reduce any harmful effects

[1363] Summary and security policy implications for defense policy

[1364] The security policy situation – summary

[1365] Today we are faced with a complex security policy picture that simultaneously presents several worrying features, encompassing both new geopolitical developments, persistent and partly increasing globalization, and challenges

[1366] No. 48 2007–

[1367] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values challenges, and significant national resource challenges in our own areas

[1368] The challenges in total place high demands on a comprehensive policy from the Norwegian side, where security and defense policy must in many cases be seen in close connection with foreign policy, economic, industrial, development and environmental aspects

[1369] The most important feature of today's security policy situation is a gradual but nonetheless fundamental change in the geopolitical picture

[1370] The United States is no longer as dominant in international politics, and emerging powers, such as China, India and Russia, are gaining increasing influence

[1371] We are moving from a unipolar to a more multipolar world

[1372] As a result of greater equality, we also see signs of increased great power rivalry

[1373] This has, among other things, contributed to an increased focus on the territorial state and state security – something we are also seeing the consequences of in our own local areas

[1374] Norwegian security is also characterized by the increasing influence of global challenges, including international terrorism, the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, environmental destruction and the struggle for strategic raw materials

[1375] These challenges, however, are different from challenges to traditional state security; the threat is directed as much at the vulnerability of open modern societies as it is at our military forces

[1376] At the same time, regional and ethnic conflicts continue, with serious consequences, both in the areas concerned and more generally in relation to respect for human rights and regional stability

[1377] At the same time, Norway is facing challenges in our immediate areas

[1378] The region's international importance in terms of resources means that more and more countries are turning their attention to the area

[1379] Among these countries is also Russia, which has significant strategic interests in the area

[1380] Norway's relationship with Russia is good today

[1381] The country has nevertheless undergone significant changes since the 1990s, with an increased degree of centralization of power and renewed great power ambitions

[1382] On the military side, this is expressed through more modern forces with high responsiveness and great mobility, as well as through increased military activity

[1383] The Kola Peninsula also constitutes the most important base area for Russia's sea-based strategic nuclear weapons

[1384] The Barents Sea's importance as an exercise and testing area is therefore great, and increasing

[1385] This contributes to the fact that our focus area in the north also has significant military strategic importance for our neighbor to the east

[1386] It cannot be ruled out that conflicts of interest between Norway and other states, especially in the area of resources, could have security and defense policy consequences

[1387] The most likely, direct challenges will be various forms of political pressure, through, for example, offenses, episodes and minor incidents that challenge Norwegian sovereignty

[1388] Militarily, the challenges will be of a different nature than during the Cold War

[1389] On the other hand, they could arise quickly, which places high demands on rapid handling on the Norwegian side

[1390] Many of today's challenges are cross-border and complex

[1391] Norwegian security is increasingly linked to international security and international cooperation, and the UN is therefore the most important organization for global security and stability

[1392] This is primarily because smaller states are dependent on linking their own security challenges to international agreements

[1393] By extension, the UN also legitimizes the use of military force on behalf of the international community

[1394] However, we see signs that multilateralism is under pressure, and that there are still challenges associated with the international community's ability and willingness to intervene even when basic human rights are threatened

[1395] The future of key arms control and disarmament agreements is also uncertain

[1396] Norway continues to benefit from international security challenges being resolved on the basis of international law and multilateral security arrangements

[1397] No other organization possesses the same range of instruments and the same global legitimacy as the UN

[1398] An important goal for the government is therefore to strengthen the UN's role in the world

[1399] Norway has taken on a leadership role in this work, including by helping to strengthen the UN's role in multidimensional crisis management so that the resources of the international community are utilized as effectively as possible

[1400] At the same time, NATO remains a cornerstone of Norwegian security policy

[1401] The solidarity enshrined in the alliance's collective and mutual defense obligations (Article 5) highlights values and interests that are important to Norway

[1402] Today, we see renewed attention to the alliance's traditional tasks related to the defense of member countries, and it is in Norway's interest to support this

[1403] At the same time, it is clear that a great deal of the Alliance's attention in the years ahead will also be directed towards urgent challenges outside the traditional areas of responsibility of NATO countries

[1404] It is important to emphasize that there is a close connection between safeguarding Norwegian security interests at home and abroad

[1405] Collective defense today is largely a question of burden sharing

[1406] Significant participation in peace-support operations will therefore continue to be a central element in Norwegian security and defense policy in the future, with the UN and NATO as the primary anchor points

[1407] Emphasis should be placed on Norway contributing at a level that reflects 41 2007–2008 St.prop

[1408] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values, a reasonable burden sharing in relation to allied countries

[1409] Relations across the Atlantic are improving and are characterized by more equality

[1410] Nevertheless, there is still a potential for internal tensions, particularly in relation to how global security challenges should be resolved

[1411] Norway therefore has a great interest in contributing actively to NATO; partly to influence developments in line with Norwegian interests, but also because NATO is the only organization with the capacity to safeguard Norwegian security in the event of a major crisis

[1412] Priority must therefore continue to be given to cooperation with close allies, primarily the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany and the Netherlands

[1413] The Government will also place emphasis on further developing practical Nordic defense cooperation

[1414] This cooperation will supplement and not replace the commitments and close cooperation Norway has with NATO allies

[1415] Implications for defense policy

[1416] The analysis of the security policy environment sets out the overall political guidelines for the use of Norwegian military power, and thus also provides guidelines for the development of defense policy

[1417] The following frameworks and guidelines must be central in this regard

[1418] – The diversity of challenges at home and abroad means that the Armed Forces must be aligned with the sum of the trends that characterize our surroundings

[1419] Security challenges dictate that the defense reforms that were initiated by the Stoltenberg I government in 2001, and that the Bondevik II government continued, must continue

[1420] The main goal of a modern and flexible operational defense remains unchanged

[1421] – Defense policy must facilitate an operational structure characterized by jointly trained elements that, within a joint operational framework, can solve missions across the entire spectrum of conflicts

[1422] This requires military forces with sufficient quality, responsiveness, strategic and tactical mobility, self-protection and endurance

[1423] – Sufficient endurance must be given considerable weight

[1424] This is because national crisis management requires ongoing access to available response forces, but also to be able to solve long-term missions at home or abroad

[1425] – General conscription is crucial both to give the Armed Forces a necessary anchoring in society, and to ensure access to enough departments that can share operational burdens

[1426] Sufficient endurance through military service is also crucial for the availability of forces that are ready for rapid deployment in national and allied emergencies

[1427] – The Armed Forces must, within the framework of the total defence concept, be able to cooperate with the civilian sector and also contribute to the civilian part of societal security work

[1428] – The challenges in our immediate areas indicate that the Norwegian Defence Force, with support from society's other resources, must be able to independently solve tasks related to surveillance and intelligence in Norwegian areas of interest and assertion of sovereignty

[1429] The Armed Forces must also be able to contribute to incident and crisis management in a credible manner

[1430] This requires a range of military capabilities that provide opportunities for adapted response methods that can be applied quickly

[1431] – The challenges in our immediate areas also emphasize the vital importance of the defense of Norway being linked to a larger community with anchorage to the west

[1432] We must therefore contribute to strengthening NATO's connection to our area, through, among other things, regular allied exercises and training on Norwegian soil, permanent allied presence, credible host country and reception arrangements for allied forces, and by Norway being able to contribute its own forces to a possible allied operation in Norway

[1433] – The defense must be based on NATO standards to the greatest extent possible, so that it can function within an allied framework across the entire spectrum of conflicts, both in connection with collective defense at home and abroad and in connection with participation in NATO-led peace operations

[1434] – Active participation in UN and NATO peace support operations must be of great importance for the Armed Forces' organization

[1435] Norwegian forces must only participate substantially in the entire spectrum of peace support operations, from preventive, through peacekeeping and to peacemaking operations

[1436] In this regard, Norwegian forces must be able to cooperate closely with forces from allies and partner countries

[1437] – Long-term balance between the Armed Forces' tasks, structure and access to resources is crucial to success

[1438] This requires predictability in resource access and comprehensive solutions

[1442] Societal developments

[1443] The development of the Armed Forces is in a mutually influencing relationship with developments in civil society

[1444] This relationship is reflected in many different dimensions

[1445] The armed forces must be able to meet the demands of modern conflicts and security challenges

[1446] This has consequences for the Armed Forces' tasks, orientation and competence, as well as for doctrines and concepts, materiel and organization

[1447] The security picture that forms the basis for defense planning is characterized, among other things, by the fact that threats and risks are of a more limited scope, but more complex than previously

[1448] In a crisis situation, nationally or internationally, the expectation in civil society will largely be that society will function as normally as possible while at the same time handling crises, if necessary using military means

[1449] This places great demands on the Armed Forces

[1450] The result is that the distinction between peace, crisis and war has become more blurred

[1451] The defense must base its orientation and activities on this

[1452] Together with other changes and trends in society, this means that the framework conditions for the Armed Forces' activities have changed significantly

[1453] The defense must still be dimensioned and trained for its primary task – the use of military power, but in a relevant and changed context

[1454] Dependence between civilian and military actors – at home and abroad

[1455] The interdependence between military and civilian actors in the work of meeting modern security challenges has increased

[1458] Civil-military cooperation will also significantly influence the way operations are carried out

[1459] In many situations, effective cooperation will be a critical factor for the progress of operations, in addition to mutual understanding and respect for the roles that civilian and military actors must fulfill

[1460] This development has had important consequences for cooperation between military and civilian actors nationally

[1461] The task of safeguarding societal security has become increasingly important given the vulnerability of modern society

[1462] Modern society's critical dependence on information and communication technology brings new security challenges

[1463] Centralization creates large and vulnerable concentrations of people and resources

[1464] The interdependence between various societal functions and in their relationship with the outside world increases the risk of ripple effects from events that may initially be limited or isolated

[1465] This may mean that incidents reach such a scale that the Armed Forces must be prepared to support civilian actors with available and relevant resources

[1466] Ultimately, this could mean that challenges to societal security develop into a security-political dimension

[1467] On the other hand, developments have led to the Armed Forces becoming more dependent on civil society in several areas

[1468] This applies, among other things, to competence development, deliveries of goods and services, security of supply and technology

[1469] In sum, this has led to changes in the approach to civil-military cooperation and total defense, where mutual support across the entire spectrum of crises has become the underlying principle

[1471] At the same time, the interaction between civilian and military instruments has become increasingly visible internationally in the work to create peace, stability and development in conflict-ridden areas

[1472] This requires a long-term and holistic approach, where military instruments alone will not constitute a sufficient

[1473] A defense that protects Norway's security, interests and values ​​is a prerequisite for achieving desired results

[1474] However, the use of military force and military means will in many cases be a necessary step in order to create the stability and security required for civilian actors to be able to carry out their tasks

[1475] Furthermore, military efforts could play an important role in the longer-term reconstruction efforts in conflict-torn societies

[1503] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values

[1504] Changed media reality Another key development is that the Armed Forces' activities take place in a completely different media reality than before

[1505] The demand for, and availability of, information has increased significantly

[1506] This has implications for preparedness, security, recruitment, competence and the ability to handle the information aspect within the framework of the requirements set by the operational activities

[1507] In modern conflicts, there is an expectation of access to updated information about the situation in general and Norwegian forces in particular

[1508] This is also important for the legitimacy of the operations

[1509] A critical press is a central part of a democratic society

[1510] The media must be expected to play an active and critical role in all future conflicts

[1511] The media will report on the progress and consequences of the operations at close range, and will help influence public opinion's perception of the situation in the area where the crisis is unfolding

[1512] Increased emphasis on human security The international media's focus on conflicts and conflict areas also contributes to increased attention to the humanitarian consequences of conflicts

[1513] This is a result of the value placed on human security, which entails a limited acceptance of the loss of human life, both civilian and military

[1514] During the Cold War, it was tacitly accepted that a total war would lead to huge losses, which is no longer the case

[1515] This has major implications for operational conditions, and places changed demands on the Armed Forces' capacities and expertise

[1516] Great emphasis must be placed on protecting our own forces, both in the form of modern equipment and the way operations are planned and carried out

[1517] Avoiding unnecessary and unintended harm to civilian communities during operations will also be crucial

[1518] In addition, military force must be used within the rules of international law, and within politically defined boundaries and conditions

[1519] Furthermore, it is important that military forces are given the necessary powers and freedom of action so that missions can be carried out effectively without excessive risk

[1520] This requires a high standard of training and the necessary competence to assess complex situations

[1521] Sociocultural and demographic conditions

[1522] The military is also influenced by socio-cultural and demographic trends

[1523] Over time, social development has been characterized by an increasing degree of individualization, which has led to individuals placing greater demands on efficiency and material goods, with less focus on the collective as a value in itself

[1524] This is a development that could, in the long term, have consequences for support for conscription and for the Armed Forces' social standing

[1525] It is therefore important that the Armed Forces meet society's expectations and carry out assigned tasks in an efficient manner

[1526] Furthermore, developments in the composition of the population are of importance to the Armed Forces

[1527] Changes in settlement, work and family patterns, as well as the development towards a more multicultural society, create opportunities for the Armed Forces

[1528] This also places new demands on the organisation, both in terms of recruitment, equality, diversity and family policy measures

[1529] Technological developments

[1530] Technological developments are helping to change weapons, equipment and the way modern military forces operate

[1531] One of the most important developments today is the opportunities that information technology provides for interaction in networks, both within and between organizations and across levels and cultural divides

[1532] This makes resource utilization more flexible and coordinated, which creates increased efficiency

[1533] The concept of network-based defense (NbF) is made possible by this development

[1534] This will continue to be central to the development of the Armed Forces in the period 2009-2012, and beyond

[1535] Technological developments have a crucial impact on how military forces are assembled, on how military operations are carried out, and not least on the ability of military forces to carry out their tasks in different situations

[1536] The rapid technological development places great demands on updated expertise regarding the possibilities and challenges that technology represents, and must therefore be reflected in the Armed Forces' education

[1537] The technology also has significant implications for the safety of personnel participating in operations, both in the form of new opportunities for more effective protection, but also in the form of new vulnerabilities

[1538] New technology in itself does not reduce the requirement for protection of one's own forces, but can be used as one of several means to make protection more effective

[1539] Therefore, the ability to understand, utilize and shape technological developments is of central importance, both in military operations and in long-term defense planning

[1540] Technological developments also have important consequences for cost developments

[1541] Price rise 45 2007–2008 St.prp

[1542] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values. The lack of military materiel and equipment creates pressure on the Armed Forces' finances and uncertainty in defense planning

[1543] The development of technology is increasingly led by civilian, commercial actors

[1544] This means that modern technology is often more readily available and more affordable

[1545] Nevertheless, in many cases it turns out that adapting and applying technology for military purposes is costly

[1546] Furthermore, the unit costs of some types of modern defense equipment tend to increase significantly from one generation to the next

[1547] This is a development we have little influence over, because it is largely driven by the demand of the major nations

[1548] The pace and extent of this type of cost growth is difficult to predict accurately, especially in a longer-term perspective

[1549] The risk picture and technological developments thus point in the same direction with regard to the specific design of the Armed Forces

[1550] A relevant defense must have a technological standard that makes it possible to operate effectively, alone and together with allied forces, inside and outside Norway and across the entire spectrum of conflicts

[1551] This does not mean that the Armed Forces must have an identical technological level with all allies in all areas, but that there must be a necessary and broad ability to cooperate between our own and allied military forces

[1552] Economic framework conditions

[1554] Defence budgets have developed relatively stably in fixed kroner from 1990 to the present day

[1555] The defense budget's share of gross domestic product (GDP) has decreased from approximately 3% to approximately 1.6% during the same period, and as a share of the state budget from over 6% to under 3% during the same period

[1556] During the same period, GDP has increased by about 65%, measured in constant kroner

[1559] There has been a significant increase in employment and a significantly increased level of activity in business and mainland industry

[1560] The positive development has continued throughout

[1561] In the future, the Norwegian economy is still expected to face significant challenges

[1562] The long-term trends show that there is a need for adjustments in economic policy to ensure long-term sustainability of public finances

[1563] In the longer term, oil and gas production will decline

[1564] The growth potential of the mainland economy will thus be decisive for future economic growth in Norway

[1565] At the same time, the Generation Account, cf. Report to the Storting, shows

[1566] that expenditure on pensions and health and care must be expected to increase significantly

[1584] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values, and to develop and maintain military capabilities

[1585] Such cooperation can provide increased operational capability and flexibility nationally as well as internationally

[1586] Multinational cooperation is also a prerequisite for maintaining and further developing the ability to cooperate militarily with allies and other cooperation partners

[1587] Cooperation can span a wide range of areas, from operations, training and exercises, development, acquisition and maintenance of military capabilities, expertise and education, to the establishment of integrated military units

[1588] There are also large variations in the depth and degree of commitment associated with different forms of multinational cooperation

[1589] In the further development of multinational defense cooperation, greater emphasis will be placed on developing integrated force production solutions in line with the principle of mutually reinforcing defense structures

[1590] This helps to support the international community's (NATO/EU/UN) ability to handle new challenges, while enabling the continuation of a national operational breadth and depth in the defense structure that corresponds to the needs of the individual country

[1591] Central parts of traditional multinational cooperation have been concentrated on operational force cooperation

[1592] This cooperation is essential for the ability to work together in operations and contributes to increased efficiency and interoperability

[1593] However, operational force cooperation must be supplemented by increased focus on cooperation on force production in a broad sense

[1594] It is primarily in this area that collaboration can provide major savings and contribute to increased operational effectiveness

[1595] The effects that can be achieved from multinational cooperation depend on the breadth and depth of the cooperation

[1596] The greatest effect will be achieved if the countries develop their respective operational capacities/units towards system similarity

[1597] System similarity means cooperation that is based on the same type of platform or weapons system and encompasses all stages of force production

[1598] Developing system similarity could also provide positive operational effects, increased flexibility and greater endurance

[1599] This way, the capacities can be used both in joint operations, but also on an independent national basis

[1600] It is in this light that the Norwegian-Swedish feasibility study, which was initiated by the Norwegian and Swedish Chiefs of Defence, on mutually reinforcing cooperation must be understood, cf. box

[1601] A number of projects have been identified in this study as feasible within a bilateral framework

[1602] The purpose of the collaboration is to exploit the countries' comparative advantages, streamline operations and create economies of scale within force production, logistics and other support activities

[1603] In this way, savings are achieved that put both countries in a better position to maintain the breadth and quality of the defense structure and at the same time contribute to ensuring that a larger part of the structure is available for operational use

[1604] The countries retain the necessary discretion over the use of their own operational forces, but cooperate on support functions

[1605] Box 4.2 Norwegian-Swedish feasibility study

[1606] In the autumn of 2007, the Chiefs of Defence of Norway and Sweden submitted a joint study that highlights how the defence structures in Norway and Sweden can be organised in a mutually reinforcing manner within force production, logistics and operational structure

[1607] The study has, among other things, conducted a review of existing material plans in a 20-year perspective

[1608] The purpose of the study has been to clarify the scope for enhanced cooperation, with a main focus on the planning period 2009-2012, with a horizon of

[1609] A large number of possible areas of cooperation have been identified, and 18 current areas of cooperation within the Army, Navy, Air Force, expertise and personnel, logistics, analysis and development have been described in more detail

[1610] The greatest potential for military, economic and political gains lies primarily in the coordinated development of the countries' structural plans in the longer term

[1611] This will make it possible to achieve coordinated procurement of future equipment for the Armed Forces, in addition to a more rational utilization of support activities

[1612] In addition, the feasibility study has highlighted areas of collaboration that can be realized in the shorter term

[1613] These are further assessed by the Ministry of Defense in collaboration with the Swedish authorities

[1614] The study's main conclusion is that current response planning should be changed with the aim of making concrete multinational cooperation an integrated part of long-term development

[1615] The Ministry of Defence is working to assess, further develop and further specify the Chiefs of Defence's recommendations, in collaboration with Sweden

[1616] Finland has been involved in the follow-up to the feasibility study, by initiating a trilateral feasibility study

[1617] The enhanced military cooperation is open to participation by all Nordic countries, and Denmark and Iceland are also invited to participate

[1619] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values 4.5 Trends in multinational materiel cooperation

[1620] Multinational cooperation on the acquisition and development of defense equipment is becoming increasingly important for smaller countries and their defense industries

[1621] The globalization of security policy challenges, combined with significant cost growth in several areas for advanced military equipment, means that multinational materiel cooperation will gain increased importance in the future

[1622] This is particularly true for small and medium-sized countries, where developments clearly point to multinational cooperation becoming an important prerequisite for maintaining national defense in long-term economic balance

[1623] High technological and competence requirements, rising costs for selected types of military equipment and continuous pressure on defense budgets, contribute to the fact that European countries must increasingly cooperate more closely on the development, acquisition, operation and maintenance of defense equipment

[1624] The development is reinforced by increased demands for operational cooperation in foreign operations and emergency forces, with requirements for compatible equipment and materiel, and an increased need for expanded cooperation between involved authorities and industry

[1625] Overall, international materiel cooperation can provide significant economic savings as well as competence-related and other positive effects for the parties

[1626] This requires the right framework conditions and agreement on operational and technical requirements

[1627] This development will also affect the Norwegian defense

[1628] Norway participates in international material cooperation in both bilateral and multilateral contexts

[1629] Within NATO, the CNAD (Conference of National Armaments Directors) plays a significant role as a facilitator and arena for material cooperation between the allies

[1630] This applies particularly to projects that are so costly and demanding that they require the participation of the largest member states in the alliance in order to be realized, such as strategic airlift, airborne ground surveillance systems and protection of deployed military forces against missiles

[1631] Within the NATO framework, Norway has bilateral agreements and material projects with selected allied partner countries, of which the United States and the North Sea countries are the most important

[1632] The Ministry of Defence has initiated work to assess how the NATO Supply and Maintenance Organisation (NAMSA) can be used more effectively by Norway in connection with the organisation of procurement, resupply and maintenance services

[1633] With the establishment of the European Defence Agency (EDA), significant dynamics have recently been witnessed within European materiel cooperation

[1634] EDA is an intergovernmental EU agency for the harmonisation and development of military capabilities, research and technology development, material procurement, as well as defence industrial and market development

[1635] Norway has, as the only third country so far, entered into a cooperation agreement with EDA

[1636] It is too early to draw final conclusions regarding experiences from the collaboration with EDA

[1637] The cooperation agreement gives Norway a necessary and important opportunity to participate in concrete initiatives for military capacity development in collaboration with close partners in Europe

[1638] EDA will be the central forum for such work, but has so far been most successful in the research and technology area, partly based on the legacy

[1639] from the former Western

[1640] European Armaments Group (WEAG

[1641] Consequently, it is in this area that the agreement has had the most impact for Norway, even though the rights are fewer and Norway's participation is less extensive than in WEAG

[1642] In this sense, the transfer of this cooperation from the WEU to the EU led to a weakening of Norway's participation rights

[1643] It is a clear challenge that Norway is not represented in EDA's governing bodies

[1644] In addition to the research and technology projects, EDA has taken several initiatives that could eventually lead to joint procurement of materiel, closer industrial cooperation and more extensive multinational military cooperation in line with Norwegian needs and interests

[1645] In the coming period, the Government will continue to work to ensure that the limitations resulting from Norway's status in relation to the EDA can be compensated for through the best possible mutual cooperation based on an active attitude and constructive contributions from the Norwegian side

[1646] In the Nordic region, cooperation takes place within Nordic

[1647] Armaments Cooperation (NORDAC

[1648] Nordic defense cooperation is constantly increasing in scope and importance

[1649] The Norwegian-Swedish cooperation that has been initiated is a concrete example of this, and also includes the material area

[1650] This planning collaboration is open to the other Nordic countries, and has already added new content to the collaboration in NORDAC

[1651] Developments within NATO and the EU, in addition to an increasing focus on multinational material cooperation, have significant consequences for Norway

[1652] Norwegian policy must be adapted to the need to play an active role in seeking cooperation, both in the allied framework, but also in relation to EDA and in a Nordic and bilateral context

[1653] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values 4.6 Cooperation on military capabilities in NATO and the EU Over the past ten years, NATO countries have carried out some radical restructuring of their own defense structures to adapt to today's challenges and needs

[1654] The work to transform the Alliance's military capabilities has been expanded to an increasing number of areas

[1655] Some significant results have been achieved, including through the establishment of NATO

[1656] Response Force (NRF), and multinational cooperation projects within, among other things, strategic air and sea transport

[1657] This work is both challenging and demanding

[1658] The Alliance's overall challenges, including the operations in Afghanistan, Kosovo and the issue of further expansion of the Alliance, require both attention and resources

[1659] The ability and willingness to launch new transformation initiatives is thus put under pressure

[1660] Progress remains limited in a number of critical areas, including air-to-air refueling and airborne ground surveillance (AGS

[1661] The NRF, which constitutes NATO's rapid reaction capability, has also proven difficult to realize according to original ambition

[1662] Today's practice of the concept helps to tie up forces that could have been used in ongoing operations

[1663] This contributes to a significant gap between established force requirements and the contributions actually made available from member states, both in the NRF context and in ongoing operations

[1664] Work is underway to further develop the NRF to create a better match between ambitions and resources

[1665] Norway actively supports this work

[1666] For Norway, the capacity development taking place in NATO will continue to be of great importance

[1667] The design of the Norwegian defense will largely be based on the standards that NATO and our allies also base their work on

[1668] At the same time, there is an increasing trend in which two or more allies join forces to provide military capabilities or solve specific operational missions

[1669] In this context, cooperation with countries such as the United Kingdom, Germany, the Netherlands and Denmark forms an important framework for multinational cooperation

[1670] This connects us to our closest and most important European allies

[1671] Another example is the strengthened defense cooperation with Sweden, which will be developed further in the future

[1672] Within the EU framework, it is the EDA that is currently the central driving force for the development of military capabilities in EU member states

[1673] The work in EDA is still characterized by the fact that this is a new organization, and it takes time to initiate the planned projects

[1674] Developments in recent years nevertheless indicate that the EU will take a more prominent place in the European development of military capabilities

[1675] Actual cooperation between NATO and the EU in this area is currently modest, beyond the exchange of information

[1676] This is also worrying from a Norwegian perspective

[1677] Norway has a great interest in the strategic cooperation between NATO and the EU taking shape as quickly as possible, and that this becomes a complementary and mutually reinforcing relationship, also with regard to the development of military capabilities

[1678] Developments in military operations

[1679] The assumptions, approaches and instruments that underpin the way military forces carry out their tasks are in continuous development

[1680] Only since the end of the Cold War have the changes been significant

[1681] The changes within military operations are, on the one hand, a consequence of other types of developments, including political, economic, technological and cultural conditions

[1682] On the other hand, developments within military operations affect the environment

[1683] At the same time, military operations have a significant dynamic of their own through the lessons and experiences that are continuously collected and analyzed

[1684] A number of overarching trends contribute to shaping developments within military operations

[1685] There will be fewer large accumulations of soldiers and equipment

[1686] At the same time, military operations are increasingly taking place in densely populated areas

[1687] In many operations, an adversary may be technologically inferior and choose to use means and methods that may include terror, guerrilla tactics, acts of sabotage and improvised mines and weapons

[1688] These are examples of asymmetric warfare, and contribute to presenting conventional military forces with significant challenges

[1689] At the same time, collateral damage from combat actions becomes less acceptable

[1690] Military forces are expected to use force in a proportionate and highly targeted manner to avoid unintended harm, and must place emphasis on leaving an area of operations free of munitions and other debris that could harm civilians

[1691] Long-range, high-precision weapon systems are becoming more accessible and cost-effective

[1692] These are used to combat targets at long distances

[1693] This also has consequences for military forces' operational patterns

[1694] Operations will continue to take place at great speed

[1695] On the one hand, developments are moving towards increased emphasis on mobility and lighter military units

[1696] No. 48 2007–

[1697] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values

[1698] At the same time, in several operational areas, increasing demands are being made for armor and personal protection to ensure the safety of personnel

[1699] Another key development is that major military operations are increasingly dependent on close cooperation with non-military actors to succeed

[1700] The operations will increasingly be carried out in an integrated manner, where political, military, developmental and humanitarian instruments are seen in context

[1701] In sum, developments within military operations place changed and new demands on education and competence, training and exercises, military materiel, the ability to cooperate with allies, partners and civilians, and the way operations are planned, led and carried out

[1702] The development of the security policy framework conditions described in Chapter 3, and the conditions described in this chapter, together form the overall framework for the Armed Forces' orientation, tasks and structure, including both the operational structure, the personnel structure and the support and logistics structure

[1703] This is described in more detail in the following chapters

[1704] –2008 St.prop

[1705] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values Defense policy framework, guidelines and priorities

[1706] A holistic and long-term perspective

[1707] The defense policy defines the framework, guidelines and priorities that will form the basis for the further development of the Armed Forces

[1708] Defence policy is the link between the overall security policy interests and objectives, and the specific design of the Armed Forces' structure, organisation and activities

[1709] The main elements of defense policy are the defense policy goals, the defense concept and the tasks of the Armed Forces

[1710] It is crucial to establish a holistic and long-term perspective on the further development of Forsvaret

[1711] A holistic perspective requires that defense policy is based on the sum of the overall strategic trends and challenges that characterize the Armed Forces' environment, and the main security policy priorities that are based on these

[1712] It further emphasizes the need to view the Armed Forces' efforts in close connection with other instruments, and to view the Armed Forces' activities at home and abroad as two sides of the same coin

[1713] A long-term perspective requires that predictability be created regarding the most fundamental priorities and frameworks for the Armed Forces' activities

[1714] At the same time, it must be taken into account that the future will continue to be characterized by uncertainty and unpredictability

[1715] The Armed Forces must be able to adapt to the greatest extent possible to the various and most likely developments that will affect the environment in the longer term

[1716] In other words, the defense must be as scenario-robust as possible

[1717] In short, defense policy must lay the foundation for a modern and flexible defense effort that can safeguard Norway's security, interests and values in a changing world

[1718] The Armed Forces must be able to handle a wide range of different tasks both at home and abroad, through close and mutual cooperation with allies, partners and civilian actors

[1719] This must form the basis for the development of the Norwegian Defence Force's structure and capabilities, as well as for competence and personnel composition

[1720] Defence policy goals

[1721] The Government believes that the main content of the existing defence policy objectives should be continued, with some minor clarifications that emphasize the anchoring in international law and the close connection between Norwegian and international security

[1722] The defense policy goals reflect that the Armed Forces, within its area of responsibility and in cooperation with other national authorities where this is natural, shall contribute to fulfilling these goals

[1723] – Alone and together with allies, secure Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights, interests and values, and preserve Norwegian freedom of action against military and other pressure

[1724] – Through participation in multinational peace operations anchored in a clear and unambiguous international legal basis and international defense cooperation, contribute to peace, stability, enforcement of international law and respect for human rights, as well as prevent the use of force by states and non-state actors against Norwegian and international security

[1725] – Together with allies, contribute to the collective defense of Norway and other allies in accordance with our alliance commitments, and to meet various types of attacks and threats to ensure Norwegian and collective security

[1726] – Contribute to safeguarding Norwegian societal security, saving lives and limiting the consequences of accidents, disasters, attacks and attacks from state and non-state actors

[1727] In order to provide guidance in the specific design of the Armed Forces' structure and activities, the defense policy goals must be operationalized

[1728] This is done in the defence concept, which sets out the fundamental principles for the development of the structure, organisation and activities of the Armed Forces, as well as through the description of the Armed Forces' tasks and associated level of ambition, cf. chapters 5.3 and

[1729] No. 48 2007–

[1730] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values 5.3 The defense concept and the fundamental principles for the organization and activities of the Armed Forces The defense concept describes how the Armed Forces should be organized to best be able to solve its defined tasks, and thereby also contribute to realizing the security and defense policy goals

[1731] With this as a starting point, the defense concept sets out the fundamental orientation of the Armed Forces, as well as the overarching principles that will form the basis for the Armed Forces' future development and activities

[1732] Through the processing of the Recommendation

[1733] S. no. 234 (2003-2004), cf. St.prp

[1734] No. 42 (2003-2004), the Storting agreed to a defense concept with the following wording

[1735] The Armed Forces shall be developed as a modern, flexible and alliance-adapted security policy instrument, striving for a balance between the Armed Forces' tasks, structure and access to resources

[1736] The activities will be based on close cooperation with relevant civilian authorities and on conscription that is practiced in line with the needs of the Armed Forces

[1737] The focus will be on securing and promoting Norwegian interests, through being able to handle a broad range of challenges both nationally and internationally

[1738] The Government assumes that the underlying principles of the defense concept are still valid, and that these should be continued as a basis for the further development of the Armed Forces

[1739] At the same time, it is crucial that the interpretation of, and the content of, the various main elements of the defense concept are continuously updated in line with developments and the overall security and defense policy priorities

[1740] In this regard, the government adopts the following approach to the various main elements of the defense concept

[1741] The further development of a modern and flexible operational defence The armed forces must be adapted to the new security challenges that characterise our surroundings

[1742] These environments are today characterized by a complex threat and risk picture

[1743] The most likely direct threat to Norwegian territory today could materialize in the form of episodes and minor attacks, which could occur quickly

[1744] In addition, there are the challenges that arise from Norway's desire to contribute to international peace and stability, including through participation in peace-support operations

[1745] In relation to these main challenges, the goal must be to further develop a dedicated defense that can solve tasks both at home and abroad

[1746] By operational defence is meant a defence that is quickly and flexibly capable of solving tasks that must primarily be handled nationally, and which can also operate together with allies both in connection with peace-support operations and in connection with collective defence of one's own territory and that of other allies

[1747] This not only means that the Armed Forces must have a sufficiently high quality in terms of expertise and materiel, but must also be able to meet the demands for attitudes, ethics and leadership that characterize a modern society

[1748] Norwegian forces must be able to operate effectively in a modern combat environment, handle complex situations and have a technological standard that is sufficient to carry out the tasks and ensure the necessary self-protection

[1749] At the same time, the Armed Forces must be organized so that it has the necessary flexibility to adapt to changes in the environment over time

[1750] This is primarily about maintaining and further developing competence, but also about establishing organizational structures that are sufficiently dynamic

[1751] Furthermore, it is important to take a long-term perspective, especially in relation to investment planning

[1752] An alliance-adapted defense. NATO continues to be a cornerstone of Norwegian security

[1753] This applies to the defense of Norwegian territory, where our general dependence on NATO will be at least as great as during the Cold War

[1754] This also applies to Norwegian participation in peace support operations abroad, where NATO, together with the UN, forms the primary multilateral framework

[1755] The Armed Forces must therefore be able to operate effectively with allies, both in terms of being able to meet any challenges in our immediate areas, and in order to be able to make a significant contribution to peace-support operations

[1756] Our ability to collaborate with allies must be reflected in terms of material, expertise and culture

[1757] This does not mean that the Armed Forces must have an identical technological level with allies in all areas, but that it must have the ability to cooperate with allied military forces

[1758] This is also a prerequisite for establishing effective multinational cooperation solutions with other nations

[1759] An alliance-adapted defense also means that the Armed Forces must be organized to contribute actively to solving NATO's collective tasks, based on reasonable burden sharing with other allies

[1760] Long-term balance between the Armed Forces' tasks, structure and access to resources The Armed Forces must be further developed within the framework of a long-term perspective, where the financial assumptions reflect the tasks and the ambition 53 2007–2008 St.prop

[1761] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values at the level that the Armed Forces are expected to handle

[1762] It is crucial to ensure stability and predictability in the Armed Forces' framework conditions, including ensuring consistency between the ambitions and resources that form the basis for development

[1763] Greater predictability provides better conditions for avoiding wrong investments, allows for more rational utilization of public resources and increases the operational capability of the capabilities the Armed Forces invests in

[1764] However, this also assumes that the Armed Forces organize and carry out their activities as cost-effectively as possible, that resources are prioritized to the greatest extent possible towards supporting the Armed Forces' operational deliveries, and that the scope of the logistics and support structure is best aligned to meet the needs of the operational structure

[1765] Close cooperation between military and civilian authorities

[1766] Emphasis must be placed on continuously further developing cooperation between the Armed Forces and civilian actors in order to meet changing and new security challenges, not least in relation to societal security

[1767] Many of the challenges that Norway faces today have a catchment area that affects an increasing number of agencies and sectors of society

[1768] In line with the changes in the total defence concept, the Armed Forces, based on the expertise, capacities and resources established to solve the primary tasks, shall be able to support civilian authorities across the entire spectrum of crises

[1769] Cooperation between military and civilian actors is also becoming increasingly important in connection with the Norwegian Defence Force's international activities, including in terms of education, planning and implementation

[1770] Greater emphasis must be placed on utilizing and further developing arrangements and mechanisms within total defense, which can contribute to more coordinated and mutually reinforcing cooperation across the entire crisis spectrum

[1771] Conscription shall be continued as a foundation for the Armed Forces' activities, based on the Armed Forces' needs and adapted to a new era

[1772] Conscription must constitute an important premise for the further development of the Armed Forces

[1773] Conscription will continue to have a strong operational justification

[1774] Conscripts should therefore continue to have a central place in the operational structures of the defense branches

[1775] Conscription is crucial to providing the Armed Forces with a steady supply of motivated and qualified personnel

[1776] The initial service will thus continue to be the central recruitment and selection mechanism for commanders and enlisted personnel, both for operational tasks in Norway and for participation in operations abroad

[1777] In addition, conscription helps to give the Armed Forces a necessary foothold in society, and to give the population a relationship with the Armed Forces

[1778] Because military service is so important to the Armed Forces, it is a clear goal that those who serve their first term of service should experience it as positive, educational and meaningful to the greatest extent possible

[1779] The first-time service should have substantial content that helps make the service attractive and rewarding for the individual

[1780] The Armed Forces' ability to handle challenges nationally and internationally

[1781] There is a close connection between national tasks and tasks that must be solved in cooperation with allies and partners

[1782] Participation in peace-support operations abroad is a contribution to international peace and security, which in our globalized world is increasingly determining our national security

[1783] Within a limited response structure, the key word must be synergy, meaning that great emphasis must be placed on prioritizing capacities that can be used both at home and abroad

[1784] A number of challenges must be considered national and must initially be solved nationally, such as surveillance, the exercise of authority and the assertion of sovereignty, contributions to societal security and national incident and crisis management

[1785] This requires a defense structure that, with the right capabilities, can be in the right place at the right time

[1786] This requires military forces with a range of capabilities of sufficient quality, responsiveness, mobility and self-protection, and which are capable of graded response methods across the entire spectrum of conflicts

[1787] The forces must also have sufficient endurance, and this places demands on both volume, support and logistics

[1788] It also requires a command and control system with the ability to lead joint operations, and which, within the framework of the total defense concept, can operate in cooperation with the civilian sector

[1789] Other challenges must be resolved in close cooperation with allies, such as participation in peace-support operations and collective defense of Norwegian or allied territory

[1790] Participation in collective defense and peace support operations requires forces that can operate closely with allies and other partners across the entire spectrum of conflicts, and this also requires flexible forces with high responsiveness, self-protection and firepower

[1791] At the same time, the forces must have sufficient endurance to stand with the same allies and partners in an area over time

[1792] Of particular importance for participating in operations 54 St.prop

[1793] No

[1794] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values far from Norway also requires the ability for strategic mobility – under national or multinational auspices

[1795] The tasks of the Armed Forces

[1796] The Armed Forces' tasks are divided into national tasks that must in principle be able to be solved nationally and without allied participation, tasks that are solved in cooperation with allies and other partners, and other tasks where other authorities have primary responsibility and the Armed Forces in principle have a supporting role

[1797] The tasks of the Armed Forces and the associated level of ambition must reflect the security and defense policy goals

[1798] The tasks also constitute the concrete framework for designing the Armed Forces' activities, capacities, structure and expertise

[1799] Based on the political priorities described above, the government's view is that all tasks in the current task spectrum are important and should be continued in the next long-term planning period

[1800] At the same time, some adjustments have been made to the task formulations to highlight priorities in relation to new security policy challenges

[1801] It is the Armed Forces' ability to solve the sum of the dimensioning tasks that must govern the composition and alignment of the defence structure

[1802] The basic function of the Armed Forces is to protect and safeguard Norway's security, interests and values

[1803] The High North is the government's most important strategic focus area, and the security and defense policy challenges in the area are increasing

[1804] The Government is therefore of the opinion that tasks related to Norway's territorial waters must be given considerable importance, and that our ability for surveillance and intelligence, assertion of sovereignty, and incident and crisis management is fundamental

[1805] The ability to contribute to collective defense at home and abroad and participate in peace-support operations is of great importance, and must therefore also be a determining factor in the design of the defense structure

[1806] These priorities do not mean that other types of tasks, including the Armed Forces' contribution to societal security and the exercise of authority, are not important

[1807] However, such tasks must mainly be solved on the basis of the structure that has been established to carry out the Armed Forces' dimensioning tasks

[1808] Such prioritization is also in line with the recommendations from the Defence Policy Committee, which assumes that the tasks of the Armed Forces must reflect the fundamental and timeless responsibility to contribute to creating security for the state, the population and society, and to promote national values ​​and interests

[1809] Within the framework of available resources, the committee points out the need for clearer prioritization between tasks, and in this context refers to the need to prioritize national crisis management and collective defense as the highest priority

[1810] In the committee's view, this will also create a good basis for solving tasks related to sovereignty, participation in foreign operations and international emergency forces

[1811] At the same time, the committee emphasizes the fundamental importance that the ability to conduct effective surveillance and intelligence will continue to have in order to be able to solve other tasks

[1812] The committee further finds that the tasks related to the exercise of authority and support for civil society are being handled in a good manner today, and therefore should not be given higher priority

[1813] However, effective exercise of authority will continue to be an important task for relevant parts of the structure

[1814] National tasks

[1815] A number of the Armed Forces' tasks arise from a national responsibility and interests in Norway and its surrounding areas

[1816] These tasks must therefore be able to be solved with national resources, and in principle without ongoing allied participation

[1817] This requires military presence, as well as military capabilities with high responsiveness and availability under national control

[1818] To ensure a national decision-making basis through timely surveillance and intelligence

[1819] A main task for the Armed Forces is to have the ability to monitor Norwegian land, air and sea territory, and selected sea areas where Norway has sovereign rights under international law or agreements

[1820] The task also includes a national tracking capacity

[1821] It is important that Norway has an independent ability to conduct intelligence in its own immediate areas

[1822] This is crucial both for being able to formulate our own national policy in our immediate areas, and for being able to communicate our own assessment of the situation in the area to allies and cooperation partners

[1823] Effective monitoring of Norwegian areas of interest is also a prerequisite for the Norwegian Defence Forces – on the basis of a smaller but more mobile force structure – to be able to carry out its other tasks in a satisfactory manner, including asserting sovereignty, exercising authority, national incident and crisis management and collective defence

[1824] In all cases, the main goal of the Armed Forces' surveillance and intelligence activities is to provide a good situational picture, as a contribution to the best possible decision-making basis for political authorities and the Armed Forces' operational management

[1825] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values

[1826] In general, the Armed Forces must have the ability to continuously monitor Norwegian airspace and adjacent areas, within the framework of NATO's integrated air defense

[1827] The Armed Forces must also have the ability to monitor selected activities in territorial waters and selected geographical areas at sea where Norway has jurisdiction

[1828] The Navy contributes here with, among other things, Coast Guard vessels, supported by, among other things, the Air Force's maritime surveillance aircraft

[1829] The Armed Forces must also have the ability to continuously monitor parts of the country's territory, primarily along the border with Russia, where the Border Guard has an important task

[1830] During incident and crisis management, the entire Norwegian Defence operational structure will contribute by summarising, analysing and disseminating information

[1831] Furthermore, in connection with operations abroad, the Norwegian Armed Forces must have intelligence functions to support decision-makers at both strategic and tactical levels

[1832] To assert Norwegian sovereignty and sovereign rights

[1833] The Armed Forces have a main role in asserting Norwegian sovereignty and defending Norway's territorial integrity

[1834] Assertion of sovereignty means defending, if necessary with military force, Norwegian fundamental rights as a state against other states that directly or indirectly challenge Norwegian sovereignty on Norwegian territory, or Norwegian sovereign rights in Norwegian jurisdictional areas outside Norwegian territory

[1835] This includes deterrence and handling of limited incidents, as well as preventing unauthorized actors from accessing Norwegian territory and from harming vital societal interests

[1836] In today's international security landscape, non-state actors can also challenge or

[1837] carry out actions or attacks that represent a violation of Norwegian sovereignty

[1838] The task also includes, if necessary, securing Norwegian embassies and Norwegian shipping

[1839] The increasing challenges in our immediate vicinity mean that we must also place great emphasis in the years ahead on having an effective and credible ability to assert our sovereignty

[1840] The armed forces must therefore have sufficient resources to both monitor activity in Norwegian areas and to be able to be present at short notice with suitable units

[1841] The Armed Forces must have the ability to handle various types of violations of Norwegian sovereignty at short notice, including multiple simultaneous violations

[1842] The armed forces must generally have the ability to respond to violations across the entire territory, and be able to exercise coercive power at sea, in the air and on land

[1843] The most likely violations of Norwegian sovereignty will, however, take place at sea and in the air, and planning must in practice be differentiated in relation to which part of the territory is in question, based on the probability of where violations may occur

[1844] With regard to asserting sovereignty at sea, the Coast Guard, through its presence in priority areas including territorial waters, will have an important function

[1845] In the airspace, the task will be carried out within the framework of NATO's integrated air defense, where the Armed Forces contribute with radar surveillance and fighter aircraft that are on continuous alert

[1846] On the land side, the Border Guard will, through continuous presence and information gathering, have the ability to respond to violations of Norwegian sovereignty along the Norwegian-Russian border

[1847] His Majesty the King's Guard (HMKG) will provide routine guarding and security for the Royal House

[1849] The Armed Forces shall ensure the exercise of authority related to the protection of Norwegian sovereign rights and the enforcement of Norwegian law in the demarcated areas where parts of the Armed Forces have been granted special authority

[1852] The exercise of authority is a national task that is normally carried out by the police and other civilian authorities, but the Armed Forces are granted authority to carry out the task in limited areas

[1858] This exercise of authority must be sufficiently clear and consistent to have a preventive effect on actors who deliberately challenge Norwegian laws and regulations

[1859] In the fisheries sector, this involves the ability to exercise resource control through effective intelligence, relevant presence and regular inspections in all areas where fishing takes place

The Armed Forces shall contribute to handling incidents and security policy crises in Norway and Norwegian areas that are entirely handled by Norwegian political authorities, and which are not of such a scale that the government would want to involve NATO

[2070] Command and control

[2071] Purpose of command and control arrangement

[2072] The objectives are both to ensure political control over the use of military force and to ensure that the use of military force is effective and timely

[2073] The constitutional responsibility for any use of the Armed Forces lies with the government, through the Minister of Defence as parliamentarily responsible to the Storting, and with full authority to instruct the Chief of Defence

[2074] Effective command and control depends on close interaction between political leadership and the military chain of command

[2075] This requires short lines of command, continuous coordination and rapid decisions based on a unified decision-making basis

[2076] The Chief of Defence exercises general command over all parts of the Armed Forces

[2077] He delegates authority, or parts of it, to military commanders at various levels in the organization

[2078] Transfer of command of Norwegian forces to NATO command

[2079] The chain is based on the fact that NATO's military command apparatus is subject to full political control through the NATO Council, where Norwegian authorities are represented and decisions are made by consensus

[2080] When alliance members make forces available to NATO, they transfer a limited part of the command authority to NATO's military commanders, while the Chief of Defence retains general command, including the possibility of recalling the authority

[2081] In principle, Norway will never provide forces for missions that are not within the framework approved in advance by the Norwegian authorities

[2082] In a UN operation, the UN Secretary-General appoints a Special Representative or Head of Mission (SRSG) in consultation with the Security Council

[2083] The SRSG reports directly to the Secretary-General (via the Department of Peacekeeping Operations) and to the Security Council

[2084] The operation's Force Commander (FC) commands the military force

[2085] In most current UN operations, where military force is included as one of several instruments on the part of the UN, the force commander reports to the SRSG

[2086] In some operations, the Force Commander's powers can be expanded, and the FC can act as the leader of a primarily military operation and thereby be the Head of Mission himself

[2087] EU-led operations are in principle managed in the same way as in NATO

[2088] Norwegian forces conducting operations must always be under the leadership of a responsible commander

[2089] This person is assigned a suitable form of command authority, and may delegate this authority or parts of it to subordinate commanders

[2090] In operations under national command, the forces will be under the operational command of the supreme national operational commander, who is currently the commander of the Joint Operational Headquarters

[2091] He can in turn delegate parts of the authority to commanders at a lower level

[2092] The commander of a multinational force will usually be assigned operational control over Norwegian units, along with the authority to delegate authority to a greater or lesser extent

[2093] The authority that is not transferred to the force commander is exercised by Norwegian military commanders in accordance with the provisions of the Chief of Defence

[2094] Most often, this means that the commander of the Joint Operations Headquarters has operational command and administrative control

[2095] All delegation of command authority must be explicit and documented

[2096] The person who delegates command authority always retains the authority to revoke the authorization

[2097] Delegation of authority never relieves the superior of responsibility

[2098] Military information operations

[2099] Military information operations are used to support the political and military objectives of a given operation

[2100] Military information operations are not a capacity in themselves, but a strategy for coordinating military activities in the information area

[2101] This should help reduce an opponent's combat capability, and thereby contribute to increased protection and increased survivability for one's own forces

[2102] It is also important to be able to protect one's own military forces against information operations from the opposing party

[2103] Examples of military capabilities are operations in computer-generated space, electronic warfare and psychological operations

[2104] Military information operations must be seen in close connection with other operational activities and must be expected to play an even greater role in future military operations

[2105] This is due not least to the desire to minimize the need for physical destruction and reduce the risk of accidental damage

[2106] Military information operations are also crucial to ensuring a necessary degree of information 63 2007–2008 St.prop
