[2109] Use of special forces

[2110] Special operations are military activities carried out by specially designated, organized, trained and equipped forces

[2111] Special forces contribute a flexible, applicable and unique capacity, both when they are used as a supplement to other forces or in support of other agencies, and when they are used to achieve military strategic or operational objectives

[2112] The activities of special forces are carried out in peace, crisis and war, independently or in coordination with regular forces, to achieve political and military objectives

[2113] This may require covert, hidden or discreet methods, and a willingness to accept a degree of risk not associated with regular operations

[2114] Special forces are defined as strategic forces, and are linked in terms of command at the highest appropriate level

[2115] Due to the nature of special operations, it is very important that the chain of command is clear and unambiguous, and responds quickly, while having as few links as possible

[2116] Special operations can be conducted across the entire spectrum of military operations in peace, crisis, conflict and war

[2117] The special forces should not initially be used for operations where other forces can complete the mission

[2118] They are a limited resource that cannot be produced quickly

[2119] Nor will they normally operate according to the same principles as conventional forces

[2120] The special forces can solve three principal missions

[2121] Special reconnaissance, direct action and military assistance

[2122] Support for operations Logistics is an integral part of all defense planning, and in the context of an alliance, responsibility is shared between the nations and NATO

[2123] Nations have the primary responsibility for ensuring access to the necessary logistics capacities during the implementation of an operation

[2124] NATO's primary responsibility is to coordinate activities to ensure that the Alliance's overall logistics needs are met

[2125] NATO also disposes of the common resources that nations have provided to NATO

[2126] In UN operations, responsibilities may vary from one operation to another

[2127] Strategic transport, that is, transport between the home country and an area of ​​operations, is a purely national responsibility

[2128] If national resources are insufficient, this can also be resolved by entering into bilateral and multinational agreements or by signing contracts with civilian suppliers

[2129] During operations abroad, the Armed Forces will most often establish a national logistics base or a national support element (NSE

[2130] Such departments must be flexible enough to be adapted to any operation in which Norway participates

[2131] During allied operations and exercises in Norway, Norway will have a responsibility to support foreign units

[2132] This responsibility is set out in detail in agreements and operational plans

[2133] In order to provide the necessary support, logistics units must have at least the same readiness as the departments they are to support. In addition, they must have flexibility, mobility, protection and deployability that are commensurate with the department they are to support

[2134] NATO is working to introduce the "Fair Share" principle, which states that nations that participate with combat forces should provide the same percentage of logistics in a common NATO logistics pool

[2135] This pool consists of logistics capabilities that, after a transfer of command, are available to NATO's chain of command

[2136] Such contributions will be in addition to the department's own built-in logistics

[2137] Norway must take this requirement into account when we offer forces for operations

[2138] The requirement can be met by providing the units yourself or by purchasing the service from other countries

[2139] Readiness Operational units are placed on readiness to be able to carry out the Armed Forces' overall tasks

[2140] It is a goal that the largest possible proportion of the Armed Forces' operational units should be usable both nationally and abroad

[2141] The emergency response should take care of this to the greatest extent possible

[2142] This means that efforts must be made to build up force contributions to operations abroad that are based on units that are on national alert

[2143] Furthermore, it must be assumed that the personnel serving in the operational units should normally be able to be used both nationally and in operations abroad

[2144] When the force contribution has completed its mission and is back on standby in Norway, this will also provide added value in terms of readiness for the Armed Forces

[2145] The preparedness of the Armed Forces is built up by giving operational units readiness times

[2146] The readiness time is a readiness requirement that regulates how quickly the individual units must be ready for deployment or movement from their main base

[2147] The readiness times are thus decisive for the departments' level of preparation and readiness

[2148] The readiness times for the various operational units are adapted to national needs for response capability, crisis management and commitments made to the UN, NATO and the EU

[2238] There is also a risk that Norwegian forces abroad may be exposed to such threat agents, either in the form of weapons or in the form of pollution

[2239] This entails a need for effective and coordinated protection

[2347] There is also a clear need to further develop staff service exercises between the various departments

[2348] This is necessary to ensure responsiveness and cooperation both in a national crisis situation and in connection with international crises

[2349] The Armed Forces will therefore emphasize participation in national and NATO crisis management exercises at the strategic level

[2350] This also includes participation in exercises related to the Proliferation Security Initiative (PSI), where the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is the coordinator for the cooperation on the Norwegian side

[2351] Exercises as an arena for experimentation and development Military concept development and experimentation (CD&E) has become an important tool for development in NATO and the Armed Forces

[2352] Exercises are a suitable arena for experimentation, and this should therefore be incorporated as part of the exercise activities when it is natural

[2353] Military experiences from exercises and/or operations constitute an important basis for further developing operational concepts

[2354] Norwegian Battle Lab Experimentation (NOBLE), the Centre for Military Experience (SME) and the Allied Competence Centre for Operations under Winter Conditions (AKOV) will contribute as key players in this work

[2355] The goal is to further develop the use of simulator technology in training contexts, to increase the ability to collaborate across departments and branches of defense

[2356] In this context, emphasis will also be placed on investigating the potential and opportunities for further developing the simulator technology that Forsvaret has today

[2367] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values Structure and organization

[2368] Development towards a balanced defense

[2369] In the further development of the Armed Forces, the best possible match must be created between the expectations placed on the Armed Forces and what the Armed Forces can do

[2370] As the risk landscape and security challenges are changing, the Armed Forces must be structured so that it can adapt to changes in the environment

[2371] The basis for such an adaptation is defense policy, including the defense policy goals, the defense concept and the tasks of the Armed Forces

[2372] Defence policy links the overall political ambitions for the Armed Forces with the specific design of the Armed Forces' structure, organisation and activities

[2373] The starting point for the changes in the structure and organization of the Armed Forces that the government recommends is the range of challenges that Norway may face

[2374] In sum, these changes will provide a defense that is well suited to carrying out its tasks in an effective and credible manner

[2375] While the proposed structure is geared towards meeting current tasks and needs, it is also the foundation for the modernization and development of the Norwegian Defence Forces in the longer term

[2376] The following overarching considerations should therefore form the basis for the further design and modernization of the defense structure

[2377] – Relevance to the tasks that must be solved at any given time, both alone and in collaboration with allies and partners

[2378] – Ability for good management and continuous renewal and improvement

[2379] – Continued close ties between the defense sector and civil society, based on trust that the sector's resources are managed for the best interests of the community

[2380] – Long-term balance between resource access, operational structure, force production, bases and support activities

[2381] The basis for developing the defense structure In today's changing security landscape, a modern and flexible responsive defense is required that has high operational quality, sufficient responsiveness, endurance, mobility and deployability, its own protection and training standards to be able to meet the full range of challenges both at home and abroad

[2382] The design of the Armed Forces must also ensure, to the greatest extent possible, that our forces can operate together with allies and partners

[2383] These principles have been central to the development of the defense structure throughout the two previous long-term periods

[2384] This has contributed to a renewal process that has been absolutely necessary to ensure that Norway has a modern and flexible defense that can meet today's main challenges

[2385] However, a fundamentally balanced defense requires continuous development and improvement

[2386] Both the Defence Policy Committee and the Chief of Defence are therefore clear in their recommendations and maintain the need to continue the development of the Armed Forces along the above-mentioned lines

[2387] The Armed Forces must have the ability to handle national tasks – both ongoing and those that may arise quickly – while also being engaged in operations abroad

[2388] The challenges at home and abroad emphasize the importance of having a defense that is capable of responding at short notice with relevant forces so that unforeseen events that threaten Norwegian interests at home or abroad can be handled

[2389] In such situations, early intervention is crucial both to signal political will and to provide the best possible basis for decision-making

[2390] For this reason, the Armed Forces must have available forces ready for action at all times

[2391] Experience from the Balkans, the Middle East, Africa and Afghanistan shows that military efforts and presence over time are important in order to prevent, manage and end conflicts, as well as to achieve lasting stability

[2392] In nearby Norwegian areas, the Armed Forces' daily presence signals political will to promote their own interests in a long-term perspective

[2393] It cannot be ruled out that episodes and crises at home will continue over time

[2394] Our forces must therefore also have sufficient endurance, both as a prerequisite for being able to contribute fully together with allies and partners in peace-support operations under the auspices of NATO and the UN, and in consideration of potential challenges in our immediate areas

[2395] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values. The Government places emphasis on developing an operational structure with the best possible balance between responsiveness and endurance in the structure

[2396] This balance requires a certain volume in the force structure to make it possible to solve long-term missions at home and abroad

[2397] The issue is particularly relevant in relation to smaller and vulnerable professional environments that are in demand internationally, but is also a challenge in other parts of the structure

[2398] The relationship between responsiveness, persistence and volume are therefore the central dimensions in the simultaneity problem that Norway may risk facing, cf

[2399] This – and in particular the consideration of sustainability – has been one of the most weighty considerations underlying the further development that the government is planning in the recommended operational structure

[2400] Further development of operational structure and capabilities The security picture and the sum of the tasks that arise from the defence policy basis, set the direction for the future response

[2401] The development of the structure is based on the capacities necessary to resolve the gifts

[2402] In this context, capacity means the ability to solve a limited part of the Armed Forces' overall tasks

[2403] A structural element is a platform, unit or department that contributes to providing one or more such capacities

[2404] Based on the discussion in chapter 6.2, the following assessments have been central to the design of the operational structure

[2405] – The armed forces must be equipped to carry out the tasks that political authorities have set

[2406] Analyzing both national and NATO scenarios, we consistently see a need for high-quality forces that can be quickly deployed where needed

[2407] The Armed Forces' operational structure will never be large enough to handle all challenges alone, but the range of possible challenges we face is nevertheless significant

[2408] This means that our forces must be very flexible, have a high level of training and be robust so that they can handle a wide range of challenges

[2409] – Norway still has purely national security challenges that are initially expected to be handled without support from allies

[2410] For Norway to have a credible defense capability, the operational structure must have a sufficient breadth of capabilities

[2411] This places clear limitations on how the defense structure can be further developed and requires that we ourselves be able to produce capabilities, both in the air, at sea, and on land

[2412] These capabilities must also be equipped and trained so that they are capable of conducting high-intensity combat operations

[2413] – The Armed Forces must be able to participate in the full range of NATO operations and thus contribute to burden sharing between the countries

[2414] The development in the operational pattern means that the Armed Forces will continue to be involved in conflict management and stabilization operations, also together with civilian actors

[2415] This type of operation also requires the Armed Forces to be able to conduct high-intensity combat operations

[2416] Such a capability is a consequence of the Armed Forces' tasks and Norway's alliance commitments, and constitutes an important premise for the Armed Forces' further development

[2417] – The complexity of today's operations, and the fact that Norway's defense structure is relatively limited, means that it is necessary to look at opportunities for cooperation with other nations in order to make the best possible use of resources

[2418] Norway already cooperates with a number of NATO and partner countries in many areas and aims to further develop this

[2419] The ability to operate in networks is today very important for carrying out operations, and will influence the further development of the Armed Forces

[2420] Great emphasis is placed on being at the forefront of the development of a network-based defense to create the best possible operational effect and ability for military cooperation within and between the defense branches, and with allies and partners

[2421] The further modernization of the Armed Forces is closely linked to an active attitude towards and conscious prioritization of technology, knowledge and attitudes

[2422] In summary, emphasis has therefore been placed on the fact that the Armed Forces must possess the necessary breadth of basic military capabilities to be able to handle a broad and unpredictable threat landscape in both a national and international context

[2423] To ensure this, it has also been necessary to avoid overlapping capacities

[2424] For national tasks, emphasis has been placed on balancing surveillance capabilities and the ability to maintain routine presence with the ability to quickly assemble sufficient military combat power on land, at sea and in the air

[2425] For international assignments, emphasis has been placed on developing a structure that can provide substantial and sought-after contributions, and where quality is prioritized through, among other things, facilitating good training standards for the contributions

[2426] Logistics and support functions are primarily adapted to the need for support of own combat units

[2433] The organization of the defense sector

[2434] The defense sector is organized with four agencies under the Ministry of Defense

[2435] The Norwegian Defence Force is the largest subordinate agency of the Ministry of Defence and primarily encompasses military activities, including responsibility for conducting military operations, force production and logistics

[2436] The Norwegian Defence Research Institute (FFI) is an interdisciplinary research institute, organized as an administrative body with special powers and its own board and statutes

[2437] The institute's purpose is to conduct research and development for the needs of the Armed Forces

[2438] FFI shall be an advisor on professional issues within the institute's area of work, cf. chapter 7.14.1. Forsvarsbygg (FB) is an administrative body under the Ministry of Defence organized as a separate entity with its own board and statutes

[2439] Defence Construction builds, manages and sells property for the defence sector and has the Norwegian Defence Agency as its largest and most important customer, cf. chapter 7.15.3. The National Security Authority (NSM) is an agency administratively subordinate to the Ministry of Defence

[2440] NSM reports to the Ministry of Justice for task resolution in the civilian sector and to the Ministry of Defense for the military sector

[2441] The Directorate's main tasks are to coordinate security measures and monitor security-related matters in the businesses covered by the Security Act, cf. chapter

[2442] NSM also has other tasks in both the civilian and military sectors, including the task of being the national alert and handling body for computer-generated attacks against socially critical ICT infrastructure

[2481] The changes are a further development and strengthening of the conditions that have worked well in the current management model, while at the same time initiating certain measures to improve the management apparatus in areas where challenges have currently been identified

[2482] The further development of strategic management along the lines described above aims to provide necessary improvements in terms of management and performance monitoring, strategic cross-prioritization and implementation capacity

[2483] Through such clarification of responsibility and authority, it is expected that each level and each manager can be held accountable and followed up in a clearer way than today

[2484] The armed forces' operational command structure

[2485] The operational command structure is the tool the Chief of Defence uses to exercise command over military departments in carrying out the Defence's tasks, both nationally and internationally

[2486] The main tasks of the command structure are the management of operations nationally and the monitoring of forces in operations abroad, as well as preparing for the use of operational forces in line with national requirements and NATO commitments

[2487] Another important function is facilitating allied training in Norway, as well as leading and coordinating joint operational and allied exercises

[2488] The Norwegian Armed Forces' operational command structure today consists of the Norwegian Armed Forces Joint Operational Headquarters (FOHK) at Jåtta in Stavanger with the Northern Norway Regional Command (LDKN) at Reitan near Bodø as a subordinate crisis management command

[2489] LDKN handles individual incidents and daily situations in the highlands, which are basically 74 St.prop

[2491] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values is not expected to have extensive security policy implications

[2492] The operational command structure must, like the rest of the Armed Forces, have the continuous ability to adapt its structure and working methods to prevailing framework conditions

[2493] Future management structure must be based on a network-based concept and be adapted to the operational structure

[2494] At the same time, the command apparatus must provide real opportunities to lead joint operations at a high pace, while also possessing great flexibility in meeting changing situations

[2495] This requires the shortest possible distance between strategic, joint operational and tactical command levels and the operational units

[2496] The operational command structure must be designed both with regard to it being robust enough to ensure timely decisions, but not larger than it can be staffed over time through recruitment from the recommended defense structure

[2497] The government believes that there is a need to adjust the command structure, so that there is better correspondence between the apparatus that will lead and the departments that will be led

[2498] The need to clarify responsibilities and authority relationships in management and command functions further reinforces the need for adjustment

[2499] The Government therefore recommends that the activities currently carried out by FOHK and LDKN be combined, and that a single operational headquarters for the Armed Forces be established

[2500] The establishment of one operational headquarters will provide robust professional environments and improved ability for 24/7 continuous management of operations

[2501] With fewer levels of coordination between strategic management and tactical departments, the exercise of responsibility and authority will also become clearer

[2502] Such a merger will simplify the lines of command, and at the same time be positive for cooperation with civilian actors and other partners in connection with crisis management

[2503] With this model, Norway will have a robust headquarters that can handle and follow up on all Norwegian forces in national operations and operations abroad, as well as lead and conduct major national joint operations and major multinational exercises

[2504] The Armed Forces' operational headquarters is recommended to be located at Reitan near Bodø, primarily due to the central importance of the northern regions in the future

[2529] The Army Overall tasks and operational activities

[2530] Active efforts and presence on land will continue to be one of the basic prerequisites for preventing, managing and ending conflicts in the future

[2531] The ability to seize and hold all or part of a territory will continue to be central, both in terms of being able to achieve purely military goals, but also as a prerequisite for being able to fulfill key political goals related to the maintenance of security, human rights, civil-military cooperation and the broader political and economic development of an area

[2532] It is therefore necessary for Norway to have forces that, through presence and efforts on land, can handle situations that arise, either nationally or as part of a multinational effort

[2533] The Army's task is to produce peace-operational and combat-ready units for use both nationally and internationally in peace, crisis and war

[2534] Our armed forces perform daily tasks related to border guarding and guarding the royal residences

[2535] The Army's international contribution is aimed at everything from regular combat missions to guard and security, surveillance and stabilization missions

[2536] The armed forces are continuously engaged in missions nationally, in addition to providing the largest share of our contributions to operations abroad

[2537] The sum of the tasks that the armed forces must cover is demanding, and the emphasis on these has increased

[2538] The need for land forces that can contribute to operations over time – especially in operations abroad – remains high

[2539] At the same time, the current country contribution to operations abroad is at a level that is too high to be continued, both in the short and long term

[2540] There is also a growing need for well-trained forces available for national and international preparedness

[2541] The Government therefore plans – based on the fundamental role of conscription in the defense concept – to strengthen the Army, through increased staffing in the structure, as well as longer training and education periods

[2542] This strengthening will develop the Army's ability, both to provide force contributions over time, and to have well-trained forces available for deployment nationally and internationally

[2543] The Army's forces and operational capabilities The core of the Army's capacity is the ability to conduct tactical joint operations

[2544] Tactical joint operations refer to the ability to plan, lead and execute a coordinated effort with resources from the Army's own troop types, and possibly joint capabilities, throughout the conflict

[2545] The coordinated interaction in the Army takes place between instruments that are divided into leadership support elements, maneuver units, tactical support units and logistics units

[2546] The brigade is the most important level where the overall effort can be integrated and coordinated in an appropriate manner

[2547] The brigade has the capacity to conduct independent land operations and will be able to conduct high-intensity combat for a limited period

[2548] The brigade level therefore constitutes the Army's operational and competence-based basis

[2549] This means that the brigade becomes the framework for solving two of the Army's main tasks, delivering contributions to ongoing operations abroad and at the same time educating and making well-trained forces available for national and international efforts

[2550] The government's overall objective in developing the Army's structure is to ensure and realize a robust brigade structure, where units with enlisted personnel and units where the majority are personnel for initial service form the basis for both national preparedness and contributions to operations abroad

[2551] Departments with crews ready for first duty will, after six months of education, reach a level of training that makes them fit to be on standby for simpler tasks nationally

[2552] It is therefore proposed to strengthen and improve the Army's performance in relation to tasks both at home and abroad

[2553] Plans are underway to strengthen the brigade structure in Northern Norway in terms of staffing

[2554] The Telemark Battalion will continue as a standing unit with enlisted personnel on high alert

[2555] The Telemark Battalion and the one battalion in Northern Norway will be mechanized battalions, and in the coming years will be equipped with, among other things, Leopard tanks and CV 90 armored personnel carriers

[2556] The last maneuver battalion in Northern Norway will be equipped with lightly armored wheeled and tracked vehicles

[2557] This battalion will be suitable for lighter tasks than mechanized combat against a conventional opponent, as the two mechanized battalions are equipped for

[2558] The brigade's leadership support elements (the Intelligence Battalion, the Liaison Battalion and the Military Police Company), the tactical support units (the Engineer Battalion and the Artillery Battalion), and the logistics support (the Logistics Battalion and the Medical Battalion) are being somewhat strengthened in terms of personnel

[2559] This increase, combined with an extended training period for international contributions, will provide improved operational capability and endurance in the Army

[2602] The Navy 6.6.1 Overall tasks and operational activities With Norway's long coastline and extensive area of ​​responsibility and interests at sea, the Navy has a central role in handling the challenges we may encounter in our immediate areas

[2603] At the same time, the Navy will continue to be an important contributor to operations abroad in the future, and will regularly contribute both to NATO's standing naval forces and to operations under the auspices of the UN and NATO

[2604] Maritime operations most often involve denying access to the use of sea areas (denial of access) or securing the use of sea areas for one's own purposes (sea control

[2605] The ability to establish limited maritime control and denial of access will continue to be the basis for the Navy's organization, equipment and operations in the future

[2606] The Navy must therefore continue to be able to meet maritime challenges in peace, crisis and war, in its own and foreign waters

[2607] The Navy's most central contribution to solving national tasks lies in its ability to be present with relevant capabilities over time

[2608] The ability for national crisis management and assertion of sovereignty requires independent Norwegian efforts with relevant maritime capabilities for this ability to be credible

[2609] Therefore, the ongoing modernization of the naval defense structure is absolutely necessary

[2610] With the proposed structure, the government intends to further develop a naval defense structure that emphasizes

[2611] The Navy's operational capacities are undergoing qualitative, technological and competence-related improvements

[2612] A robust ability to respond to national maritime security challenges will be maintained, while contributions can also be made to operations abroad

[2613] The Navy's forces and operational capacities are organized into the Coastal Squadron and the Coast Guard

[2614] For the Coast Guard, the government recommends a continuation of a modern and efficient vessel structure supported by new NH-90 helicopters

[2615] With the recommended structure, the Coastal Squadron will be able to strengthen, produce and provide complete naval forces for the conduct of naval denial and maritime control operations throughout the conflict

[2694] The Air Force is characterized by flexible forces that can be deployed at short notice and cover large areas

[2695] The air force's missions will normally be surveillance, information gathering, air control, combat of land or sea targets, sovereignty enforcement and air transport, primarily in support of other branches of defense

[2696] What the missions have in common is that they are often part of a joint operational framework

[2697] In such contexts, air forces contribute by supporting or creating conditions for the ability of other air, land and naval forces to carry out their missions

[2698] In addition to contributions in connection with operations abroad, the Air Force contributes to continuous and routine missions related to surveillance, assertion of sovereignty and exercise of authority

[2699] This is done, among other things, through air surveillance, fighter aircraft readiness and maritime patrol aircraft in support of the Coast Guard and the Navy

[2700] The Air Force also regularly supports special forces and land forces with, among other things, helicopters, transport aircraft and fighter jets

[2701] The Air Force also has its own missions within resource and environmental monitoring, as well as search and rescue operations

[2709] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values

[2710] New fighter aircraft capability With the wide range of roles, functions and tasks a fighter aircraft can perform, fighter aircraft are one of the cornerstones of a modern defense structure

[2711] Combat aircraft are important for the ability to assert national sovereignty and to establish and maintain the necessary degree of control in one's own airspace

[2712] Air control is a prerequisite for the protection and freedom of operation of one's own forces

[2713] The fighter jets also constitute a key capability related to fire support, information gathering and long-range precision-delivered fire

[2714] The flexibility of fighter aircraft, combined with responsiveness and range, makes fighter aircraft relevant in crisis situations, whether the challenge is in the air, on land or at sea

[2715] In addition to having an independent ability to resolve conflicts, fighter jets are a prerequisite for being able to fully utilize naval and land forces

[2716] The fighter jets thus represent a very central component in the Norwegian Armed Forces' total operational cooperation system

[2717] This is a system that must function satisfactorily for the Armed Forces to be able to handle the scenarios, intensity levels, conflicts and tasks that the Armed Forces are required to solve

[2718] It is therefore important to establish a fighter aircraft structure with flexibility and development potential in order to be relevant, and to provide political and military operational freedom of action also in a longer term perspective

[2719] Today's F-16 fighter aircraft, with planned upgrades, will have an expected operational life of

[2720] By that time, it will not be realistic to find alternative solutions to combat aircraft, such as unmanned systems or other technologies, that can replace combat aircraft in their tasks and roles at a lower cost

[2721] Based on this, it is planned to continue the current F-16 fighter aircraft structure, and that new fighter aircraft to replace the F-16 be acquired at the most optimal time after approximately 2015. The expected lifespan of a new fighter aircraft structure could be as long as 40 years

[2722] Tasks for the fighter structure

[2723] The multi-role capability of the fighter aircraft is important for a numerically small combat air force

[2724] The ability to assert sovereignty and handle incidents and crises that include the use of air weapons requires the ability to maintain a high level of air military readiness over time

[2725] In a larger alliance context, Norway implements this by maintaining fighter aircraft on NATO readiness in Northern Norway (Quick Reaction Alert - QRA

[2726] The new fighter aircraft structure must continue this capability, and in addition be able to establish similar readiness, but with lower endurance, to cover other areas of the country

[2727] In the event of a further heightened emergency situation, the combat air force must also be able to maintain a continuous air patrol over a prioritized area for some time

[2728] The future fighter aircraft structure must maintain the Armed Forces' ability to deliver fire against surface and land targets in support of naval and land operations, and as an independent capacity in offensive air operations

[2729] The new combat aircraft structure with multi-role capacity must also have the ability to establish an international contribution of squadron size, in accordance with NATO requirements and standards, while at the same time meeting the national need for air control and preparedness

[2869] Joint departments and capacities 6.9.1 Overall tasks and operational activities

[2870] The Norwegian Armed Forces' joint departments consist of structural elements and departments designed to support units from all branches of defence

[2871] These units can also be used as independent national contributions in multinational force structures, or as dedicated support for national contributions in operations at home and abroad

[2872] The units are designed flexibly and can be adapted in volume and configuration to the units or operations they are intended to support

[2873] The main objective of further developing the joint capabilities has been to improve their response capabilities, so that the support does not limit the Armed Forces' operational capabilities, either nationally or in operations abroad

[2874] In the further implementation work, the organizational structure of, and the responsibility for, the joint departments' strength production will be considered in more detail

[2875] Joint logistics

[2876] All joint logistics and support departments shall be dimensioned to support the national structure, but shall be able to be included in multinational associations

[2877] Today's deployable logistics and support units are partly based on mobilization units, while the forces to be supported are largely standing units

[2878] This creates imbalance

[2879] To increase the responsiveness and availability of these units, there is a need to increase the proportion of permanent personnel and civilian/military personnel with emergency contracts

[2880] In addition, it is a goal to be able to use a larger proportion of the personnel in the logistics and support structure also in the operational support structure

[2881] The deployable logistics that will support the primary response units will be strengthened

[2882] The logistics bases are part of the operational deliveries and will be further developed and strengthened

[2883] Overall, the logistics support is designed to be able to establish up to three logistics bases simultaneously, in support of national operations and operations abroad

[3030] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values ​​89 2007–2008 St.prop

[3031] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values as a result of defense and security policy

[3032] This requires a defense structure that has the ability to cooperate with allies, good responsiveness, endurance, mobility and deployability, self-protection and the necessary training standards to meet the spectrum of challenges both at home and abroad

[3033] The proposed operational structure contributes significantly in this direction

[3034] To ensure our sovereignty and contribute to stability in our areas of interest in the North, the ability to monitor and control the situation is central

[3035] In the recommended structure, the ability to monitor the sea and air area is prioritized, as the security challenges with potential military missions are considered to be greatest here

[3036] The structure has the ability to periodically monitor the sea areas with vessels and aircraft

[3037] If necessary, elements from the structure can be combined for continuous, real-time monitoring of delimited ocean areas

[3038] Furthermore, maritime surveillance capabilities are being strengthened with new frigates, MTBs, modernization of Coast Guard vessels and new NH-90 helicopters

[3039] The ability to monitor underwater is being strengthened with the new frigates and the upgrade of mine sweepers with autonomous underwater vehicles

[3040] The ability to continuously monitor national and adjacent airspace is maintained through a modernization of the sensor structure

[3041] The planned introduction of NATO's unified air command and control system (ACCS) improves command and control capabilities

[3042] The Army maintains surveillance capabilities, primarily along the border with Russia

[3043] In general, the ability to build a picture, establish situational awareness and effective command and control is strengthened

[3044] The Armed Forces' contribution to the exercise of authority remains a priority

[3045] The exercise of authority is primarily aimed at controlling resources at sea, presence in Norwegian territorial waters and border control with Russia

[3046] With its presence and regular monitoring, the Armed Forces support an administrative regime in line with Norwegian interests and international agreements

[3047] The recommended structure increases the ability to exercise authority at sea

[3048] Border control capabilities in territorial waters and on the border with Russia are maintained

[3049] Through continuous, relevant naval military to

[3050] presence of coast guard, naval and air units, violations and crises can be prevented, and to a certain level handled quickly without the need for further force buildup and escalation

[3051] With the recommended structure, presence in Norway's areas of interest at sea will be strengthened compared to the current structure, including through the phasing in of new frigates with NH-90 helicopters

[3052] Considered together with the recommended fighter structure, the recommended naval structure will have the capability for naval denial in confined areas

[3053] The structure also has the capacity to establish maritime control, in a limited area and time period

[3054] In airspace, sovereignty assertion and crisis management are closely linked to the ability to maintain a high level of air military readiness over time

[3055] Both the high priority given to operational capability in the northern regions and Norway's obligations in the alliance context require fighter aircraft to be on standby in northern Norway (Quick Reaction Alert - QRA

[3056] With the recommended fighter aircraft structure, the ability to intercept, identify, repel and possibly neutralize foreign aircraft is maintained at least at the current level

[3057] In addition, the fighter aircraft structure is capable of maintaining continuous air patrol in an area, as well as establishing and maintaining high air military readiness at an additional base

[3058] The ability to establish air defense capacity will be continued

[3059] With the recommended fighter aircraft structure, the Armed Forces' ability to deliver fire against surface and land targets in support of sea and land operations is maintained

[3060] On land, routine assertion of sovereignty will coincide with the exercise of authority, and mainly includes guarding the border with Russia

[3061] This capability is maintained at the current level through the continuation of the Border Guard

[3062] Supported by joint operational resources, the recommended army structure possesses the basic capabilities necessary for crisis management and sovereignty assertion

[3063] The ability to protect prioritized national objects is maintained with the operational structure of the Home Guard, His Majesty the King's Guard and a strengthened Armed Forces Special Command

[3064] Against a limited military or an asymmetric threat, the recommended structure is considered to have the ability to handle the challenges within a national framework

[3065] Overall, the structure's flexibility, robustness and operational capacity are increased somewhat to strengthen the ability to assert sovereignty

[3066] Within the framework of a UN-led world order, an effective NATO, based on the collective security guarantee and adapted to new security challenges, remains a cornerstone of Norwegian security policy

[3067] In the event of collective defense on or outside Norwegian territory, the Norwegian forces will form part of a larger NATO force

[3068] In such operations, cooperation and interoperability with allies will be crucial

[3069] The recommended structure strengthens the ability to collaborate through a general qualitative upgrade of the structure and a focus on network-based information and communication capacities

[3070] The recommended structure implies that the operational structural breadth is continued, which contributes to maintaining expertise, as well as 90 parliamentary proposals

[3071] No. 48 2007–

[3072] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values, contributing to NATO's force structure at a high level

[3073] The structural recommendation is based on the fact that the Armed Forces do not participate substantially in more than three operations or geographically separate operational areas simultaneously

[3074] Military participation abroad will continue to constitute a central element in Norwegian security and defense policy, with the UN and NATO as the primary frameworks

[3075] Participation in operations abroad may require both rapid deployment in multinational crisis management and participation in long-term stabilization operations

[3076] The Navy will be able to contribute with a mission-adapted maritime force for a period of up to six months

[3077] The Navy can also continuously contribute one frigate and one mine clearance vessel to standing maritime NRF forces, including occasionally taking command of these forces

[3078] In addition, the Navy can contribute individual vessels to maritime operations, for example related to surveillance and patrolling

[3079] Naval hunters, coastal hunters and mine divers can also contribute to operations on land

[3080] With the recommended structure, the Air Force is able to establish a contribution of up to one fighter squadron for a period of up to three months, or with a reduced number of fighter aircraft with longer endurance

[3081] In addition, the Air Force can contribute units or individual platforms from the entire air structure

[3082] With the planned strengthening of tactical transport helicopter capacity in the long term, the operational effectiveness of land forces will increase

[3083] The ability to contribute to international peace and stability depends to a significant extent on the ability of land forces to sustain contributions to international operations over time

[3084] The army will have the ability to contribute with a battalion-level battle group periodically or a company-level battle group continuously

[3085] Depending on the nature of the operational area and the nature of the mission

[3086] The Army, together with individual contributions from other parts of the Armed Forces, especially joint departments, and by utilizing the Home Guard as a source of strength for operations abroad, will be able to contribute further

[3087] The joint departments, including logistics and support, are designed to support the forces as described above, in up to three geographically separate operational areas of varying extent

[3088] The aim is to further develop a modern and flexible emergency defense force that has the responsiveness, endurance, mobility and deployability, self-protection and training standards to meet the breadth of challenges both at home and abroad

[3089] Particular emphasis is placed on designing the forces in a way that will, to the greatest extent possible, contribute to ensuring that they can operate together with allies and partners, both at home and abroad

[3090] The sum of the recommended measures, changes and frameworks described in this and the following chapters will bring the Armed Forces an important step in this direction and create a good starting point for the continuous further development of the Armed Forces where the balance between ambitions, resources and structure is ultimately sustainable

[3091] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values Support activities and base structure 7.1 Principles and goals

[3092] The defense sector must be organized so that operational activities are supported in the best possible way

[3093] At the same time, operations must be holistic, rational and efficient

[3094] The operational structure thus forms the basis for how the overall business will be organized and further developed

[3095] At the same time, the Armed Forces must be considered holistically, where the operational structure and support activities are in reality two sides of the same coin

[3096] The armed forces' operational activities entail a great need for logistics and support activities

[3097] Without sufficient support activities, operational capability is affected

[3098] There must therefore be a balance between the level of ambition associated with the operational structure and the performance of the support activities

[3099] A functional balance between these parts is necessary so that the resources available to the sector are consumed and managed for the best interests of the community

[3100] This balance must be reflected in the organization's structure

[3101] Force production and logistics and support activities lay the foundation for the operational capability created by personnel and materiel through education, training and exercises

[3102] The production of expertise, the production of services and the infrastructure that logistics and support activities represent will also have to be closely linked to the operational structure in the future

[3103] Both so that the operational activities can perform in the short term, and be further developed in the longer term

[3104] In the extensive restructuring of the defense sector, which has been carried out based on the reforms initiated by the Stoltenberg I government, a number of important and correct steps have been taken that have made the Defense Forces both better in terms of quality and significantly more cost-effective

[3105] Continued improvements related to both overall force production, and logistics and support activities, will free up additional resources for positive and necessary further development

[3106] The foundation for achieving the overall and long-term goals for the defense sector must be laid, not least through continued renewal and streamlining of the Armed Forces' support activities and base structure

[3107] Where it is possible and appropriate to streamline internally within the Armed Forces organization, this will be prioritized rather than outsourcing the activities to external actors

[3108] At the same time, it will always be a challenge to find the balance between optimizing the overall business and considering the details

[3109] This applies not least in relation to support activities and the base structure

[3110] The recommended measures and the development of future support activities will help to facilitate a long-term balance between the Armed Forces' operational structure, force production, bases and support activities

[3111] In line with the recommendations from the Defence Policy Committee and Defence Study 07, the government emphasizes that support activities and base structures must be developed based on overall operational needs

[3112] The recommended operational structure is thus the starting point for how the support activities and base structure will be renewed and streamlined

[3113] The defense structure must also be seen in the context of challenges, opportunities and measures related to ensuring sufficient personnel with the right expertise

[3114] The availability and relevance of support for the Armed Forces' operational activities must also be further developed

[3115] Logistics and operational support, which must work together with other operational units, must be prioritized in the same way as these, both in terms of materiel, preparedness and training, within a holistic framework and with the necessary focus on economically rational operations

[3116] The development of support activities and the base structure will contribute to more cost-effective solutions for the defense sector's overall activity

[3117] Overall, it is expected that the recommended measures related to the base structure will release approximately 375 million kroner annually when the measures are implemented – of which approximately 275 million kroner annually is expected to be released for prioritized activities and necessary investments by the end of the year

[3118] This will be a very important contribution to ensuring long-term financial balance in defense

[3119] The renewal of the Armed Forces will also include a number of initiatives and measures to make operations more efficient, without necessarily entailing fundamental reorganizations, relocations or closures of operations

[3120] The Armed Forces' activities are being concentrated to a somewhat greater extent than today, both to reduce operating costs and to create more robust professional environments

[3121] Together with 92 St.prop

[3122] No. 48 2007–

[3123] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values, it is important that the Armed Forces maintain a visible presence in various parts of the country

[3124] This is also important in some cases for emergency preparedness reasons

[3125] Bases for all branches of defense and the Home Guard are maintained in both Southern and Northern Norway

[3126] It is recommended to close some of the Armed Forces' current bases, including the Joint Operational Headquarters at Jåtta, Olavsvern, Bømoen and Madla

[3127] Furthermore, Sola will be discontinued as an air station and the Home Guard's educational activities at Værnes will be discontinued

[3128] Four home protection districts are being closed and replaced by two new ones with district headquarters and adjusted geographical boundaries

[3129] These measures will help free up over 185,000 square meters of building space

[3130] Changes in support activities and the base structure must take into account long-term flexibility, also in relation to changes in operational structure

[3131] This means, among other things, that the bases where the Armed Forces' activities are to be located must be able to be further developed in line with future needs

[3132] Consideration for flexibility must also be balanced against the fact that measures must be implemented at a sufficient pace and with the necessary degree of predictability for affected personnel, the Armed Forces as such and external partners

[3133] Not least, it is, among other things

[3134] The Defence Policy Committee has pointed out that it is important to identify connections between the plans for the replacement of infrastructure-intensive material systems and the plans for new investments and maintenance of bases, which are also correctly phased in time

[3135] This can help clarify natural decision points for location choices and promote efficient utilization of resources both in the short term and in a long term perspective

[3136] Key factors for further development As both the Defence Policy Committee and Defence Study 07 point out, the further development of the Armed Forces' support activities and base structure is affected by a number of important and partly conflicting considerations

[3137] This applies not least to localization issues

[3138] Various alternative solutions have therefore been assessed based on a broad spectrum of different conditions and from a holistic and overall approach

[3139] Developing and demonstrating a credible ability to use military force is the core function of the Defence Force

[3140] The ability to conduct operations, and the activities required to maintain a necessary level of force production and operational capability, are therefore given considerable importance

[3141] Suitable military units must be able to be deployed to solve various tasks under varying conditions, on Norwegian territory and in any area under Norwegian jurisdiction

[3142] This substantiates the need for bases for all branches of defense and the Home Guard in both Southern and Northern Norway

[3143] Operational forces and military bases in Northern Norway are an important part of the government's High North initiative

[3144] This has consequences for the Armed Forces' presence and base structure in the north

[3145] The importance of different solutions for distance to operational areas and appropriate training and exercise areas, including considerations for safety and climatic conditions, has been central to the assessments

[3146] Emphasis is placed on national and allied training and exercises in the North, also as a basis for participation in operations abroad

[3147] The need for effective cooperation between operational units may thus indicate that different parts of the Armed Forces' activities should be located together or near each other, and in connection with training and exercise areas

[3148] Safeguarding Norwegian security interests within an allied and international framework also places demands on Norwegian support activities and base structures

[3149] The Armed Forces must have sufficient capacity to receive and cooperate with allies and partners, both for training, exercises and operations

[3150] Various solutions and measures have been considered in relation to the consequences for meeting obligations towards allies and partners that Norway has through membership in NATO and various agreements

[3151] A number of the Armed Forces' expertise environments are currently small and vulnerable, even though they often have good networks, both internally and externally

[3152] Concentration of the Armed Forces' activities will strengthen the opportunities to create larger and more viable expertise environments, and facilitate closer contact and cooperation between them

[3153] Concentration of bases will help develop attractive service locations and local communities

[3154] The ability to recruit and retain the right personnel is a crucial factor for the continued successful renewal of the Armed Forces, and can contribute to cost savings

[3155] Fewer duty stations will, over time, lead to greater predictability, both for employees, their families and the host municipalities for the Armed Forces' activities

[3156] Any negative consequences for personnel and the Armed Forces of various measures, including uncertainty about job situations and declining productivity during a transitional period, have been assessed against the benefits that a possible greater concentration provides in the long term, not least through better opportunities for a lifelong career in the same area and increased stability

[3157] At the same time, the government's regional and district policy goals are also included in a comprehensive assessment, cf. chapter

[3158] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values Although location choices are about more than effective leadership, support for operational forces and military education, changes in support activities and base structure must not least be assessed in terms of the possibility of more rational operation of the Armed Forces. All activities should, as far as possible, be dimensioned in relation to a soberly defined need in the operational activities

[3159] The focus has been on truly cost-saving and cost-effective solutions

[3160] Not least, it will be important to be able to organize the activities at the individual base so that the Defence can use mobile logistics solutions in a cost-effective and rational manner and avoid unnecessary duplication of activities in the two regions of the country

[3161] The activities of the armed forces entail a great need for support activities

[3162] Successful renewal and change, however, requires sustained focus and sufficient resources

[3163] It is important that this resource requirement can be minimized through good planning and sufficient attention to possible challenges

[3164] The activities of the armed forces have consequences for noise, pollution and biodiversity

[3165] These consequences are largely linked to air stations and firing and training ranges

[3166] The Armed Forces place great emphasis on protecting environmental and natural interests from the stresses that necessary activities entail

[3167] Negative consequences can be limited by implementing environmental measures, but these come at a cost

[3168] Concentration of the Armed Forces' activities could ultimately result in more cost-effective environmental management

[3169] With regard to shooting and training ranges, the environmental impact will

[3170] nationally be less from a few fields with a higher level of activity, rather than many fields with moderate to low capacity utilization

[3171] At the same time, greater concentration could result in a higher environmental impact in affected areas, so these factors must also be assessed against each other

[3172] Increased concentration frees up areas, and it will be easier to both plan and implement good and effective mitigation measures and establish good environmental management systems

[3173] This is important in the current situation, but could be even more important in the future with expected increasing environmental requirements

[3174] The Armed Forces cannot rely on extensive new establishment of firing ranges in the future

[3175] Assessment of alternative measures

[3176] Assessments of alternative organizational and geographical measures have been made based on the need to conduct a comprehensive assessment of various factors that are important for the further development of the Armed Forces' support activities and base structure

[3177] These conditions are explained in chapter

[3178] An attempt has thus been made to balance a number of important and partly conflicting considerations, within the framework of the needs derived from the recommended operational structure and so that the Armed Forces will be able to carry out its tasks in an effective manner in a long-term perspective

[3179] The government has not least emphasized that different measures must be viewed as a whole

[3180] This means that analyses of organizational and geographical measures within force production, education and support activities have been carried out using both quantitative calculations and qualitative assessments

[3181] The quantitative profitability calculations of organizational and geographical measures have been carried out using the present value method

[3182] This is so that potential expenses and savings associated with the various alternatives, both with regard to operations and investments, can be taken into account in a realistic and systematic manner

[3183] The present value method provides a basis for comparing alternative solutions with different future receipts and payments

[3184] The highest management of the armed forces

[3185] Changes in strategic management

[3186] The strategic leadership of the Armed Forces is comprised of the Ministry of Defence, where the Chief of Defence and the military strategic functions are integrated, as well as the Defence Staff

[3187] The Government plans to further develop the adopted management model for the strategic management of the Armed Forces, with the aim of facilitating better strategic management and control of the sector

[3188] The Ministry of Defence's role as a government office remains unchanged, but the ministry is being further developed to better assume overall responsibility for strategic planning and management of the sector

[3189] The Defence Staff will be further developed into a dedicated staff apparatus to support the Chief of Defence in his role as head of agency

[3190] The new Defence Staff, together with the Ministry of Defence, will then constitute the Chief of Defence's staff apparatus to support him in the performance of both of his functions – as the highest-ranking military advisor in the ministry, and as head of the agency

[3191] The most significant change is the establishment of a clear management level where the inspectors general and their staff functions are organized outside the Defence Staff as a subordinate level to it

[3194] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values

[3195] More about economic calculations of changes in the base structure

[3196] The considered alternatives are first adapted to proposed changes and adjustments in operational structure

[3197] The present value of alternative organization and/or location of the business is then calculated against the current adapted solution

[3198] Future cash flows are discounted at a four percent real required rate of return

[3199] A 20-year time horizon has been used and the expected residual value of property, buildings and structures has been added

[3200] The calculations mainly include receipts and disbursements (cash flows) for personnel and infrastructure

[3201] Personnel-related costs are categorized with assistance from the Norwegian Defence Research Institute

[3202] Infrastructure expenses are divided into investments, disposal and operating costs, and are processed based on data from, among others, the Norwegian Defence Agency

[3203] In cases where alternatives are considered to result in significant differences in material costs or other operating costs, this is calculated separately

[3204] Material-related costs for the total structure are mainly captured in the overall financial calculations

[3205] To take into account the overall infrastructure-related uncertainty, a mark-up has been added to the investment basis calculations

[3206] In addition, general uncertainty has been taken into account in the calculation of present values

[3207] As part of the preparation of the proposal, a preliminary investment profile has been designed for the recommended measures

[3208] The investments are thus spread over several years

[3209] The results from the calculations have been assessed and prioritized with regard to the need to realize necessary investments within the financial planning assumptions

[3210] The calculations are supplemented with sensitivity analyses, the purpose of which has been to reveal how sensitive the various alternatives are to changes in the various cost elements

[3211] Furthermore, it has been assessed how the alternatives are affected by changes in return requirements and time horizons

[3212] These analyses have not provided grounds for changing the recommendations

[3213] External consulting support has been used to quality assure the method and financial calculations that form the basis for recommended changes to the Armed Forces' base structure

[3214] A main conclusion is that the methodological approach, assumptions, data basis and uncertainty management used in the calculations have been satisfactorily handled overall

[3215] The external review has shown that the conclusions drawn regarding the economic consequences of the individual measures are robust, and that the calculations have been carried out with good consistency

[3216] This means that the measures collectively and individually have a positive present value, and will contribute to reducing the Armed Forces' operating expenses in the short and long term

[3229] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values 7.4.2 Changes in operational leadership The government believes that there is a need to adjust the command structure so that there is better correspondence between the apparatus that will lead and the departments that will be led

[3230] The need to clarify responsibilities and authority relationships in management and command functions further reinforces the need for adjustment

[3231] The Government therefore recommends that the activities currently handled by the Armed Forces Joint Operational Headquarters (FOHK) and the Regional Command Northern Norway (LDKN) be combined, and that a single Armed Forces Operational Headquarters be established

[3232] The establishment of one operational headquarters will provide robust professional environments and improved ability for 24/7 continuous management of operations

[3233] With fewer levels of coordination between strategic management and tactical departments, the exercise of responsibility and authority will also become clearer

[3234] Such a merger will simplify the lines of command, and at the same time be positive for cooperation with civilian actors and other partners in connection with crisis management

[3235] With this model, Norway will have a robust headquarters that can lead all Norwegian forces in national operations and follow up operations abroad, as well as lead and conduct major national joint operations and major multinational exercises

[3236] Reference is made to a more detailed discussion of this measure in Chapter 6. It is recommended that the Armed Forces' operational headquarters be located at Reitan near Bodø, not least in view of the central importance of the highlands in the future

[3237] In addition to providing operational savings primarily through reducing the number of mountain facilities in operation, the measure will also entail a robust capacity to lead operations and major exercises nationally, as well as follow up on force contributions to operations abroad

[3238] The move will not have any consequences for the continuation of the Joint Warfare Center (JWC) as NATO's command structure is currently organized

[3239] Norway's host country obligations to the JWC will be fully respected

[3240] The consolidation into one headquarters in Bodø is estimated to provide annual operational savings of approximately NOK 91 million

[3526] The Norwegian Armed Forces' Logistics and Support Concept The Chief of Defence's Logistics and Support Concept currently provides guidance on how logistics in support of operations and other support activities should be implemented

[3527] Central elements of the concept are clarification of interfaces between, for example, operational and stationary logistics, assessment of what minimum targets should be set for the Armed Forces' own maintenance capacity, and how the Armed Forces' materiel and systems should be safeguarded

[3528] In this context, reference is made, among other things, to the

[3529] No. 30 (2007–2008), cf. St.prp

[3531] The Ministry of Defence will establish new overall guidelines for logistics and support activities, which will guide the Chief of Defence's future directives in this area

[3532] The directives must, among other things, clarify the responsibilities, tasks and authority of the various actors, including the boundaries between logistics and support activities and users

[3533] This is important because the complexity of logistics and support activities requires significant collaboration both internally and with various external actors

[3534] requires, in addition to will and ability, a clear and agreed understanding of the roles and responsibilities of the various actors, and also that the various users have sufficient competence to be able to define their own needs and clarify requirements

[3535] These directives will also provide further delineations regarding which functions the sector must perform itself

[3536] In this context, thorough fundamental assessments and analyses must be made

[3537] Security policy and operational conditions, including flexibility, access to necessary expertise and delivery security, will always be given considerable importance

[3538] Logistics and support functions that directly support operational activities will be crucial for operational capability

[3539] The directly supporting logistics should therefore, regardless of the area, be continued under the sector's own management

[3540] The Norwegian Armed Forces Logistics Organisation The overall tasks of the Norwegian Armed Forces Logistics Organisation (FLO) are to procure, maintain and deliver materiel and supplies at the right place and time, and at the agreed price and quality within set limits

[3541] In addition, FLO is responsible for its own operational deliveries, both in the form of operational units and through various operational support functions

[3542] Logistics in the Armed Forces is governed by the operational structure and organizational units' need for support

[3543] In this way, the activities of FLO are inextricably linked to the operational structure

[3544] A functional balance between these parts of the business is necessary so that the resources available to the sector are consumed and managed for the best interests of the community

[3545] The further development and organization of the activities in FLO must be resource-efficient in a holistic perspective

[3546] At the same time, there are currently challenges related to cooperation in the logistics and support area in the Armed Forces

[3547] A very central challenge is to further develop the Armed Forces' ability and capacity to further adapt logistics and support contributions to the needs and requirements of the response organization for enhanced and flexible support

[3548] Based on the Armed Forces' further development, the need for a logistics and support operation that is organized with a view to great adaptability to continuous changes in needs is increasing

[3549] In this context, the Government considers that there are two main challenges related to the further development of the St.prop

[3550] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values, and the development of FLO

[3551] Firstly, FLO is a very large organization with very complex activities

[3552] Secondly, FLO handles functions across the entire service spectrum, from local support functions at the individual base/department to strategically important and often very resource-intensive and complicated investment projects

[3553] In light of the strategic importance of the logistics support activities in the Forsvar, the government considers that it would be appropriate to conduct a comprehensive review of FLO's facilities and activities

[3554] In parallel with this review, FLO will be adapted to the changed operational structure and base structure, increase the scope of international cooperation and be organized in accordance with the Armed Forces' approach to network-based defense

[3555] It is likely within the logistics area that the greatest positive effects of network-based defense can be achieved in the short term, as much of the technology has already been developed and is in civilian use

[3556] The primary focus in the review of FLO will be governance, as well as management and competence aspects related to such a large and complex organization

[3557] The Government will therefore return to the Storting in an appropriate manner after such a review

[3558] In this context, reference is also made to the consideration of Recommendation

[3559] P. no. 234 (2003–

[3560] No. 42 (2003–2004), in which the Storting asked the government to investigate a new agency under the Ministry of Defence with overall responsibility for the executive part of the Defence's investment and procurement activities, where procurement and material purchases have been taken out of FLO
