[3605] Other agencies under the Ministry of Defence 7.15.1 The Norwegian Defence Research Institute The Norwegian Defence Research Institute (FFI) is organised as an administrative body with special powers

[3606] FFI's board is responsible for efficient and targeted operations and for ensuring that there is consistency between the number of employees, expertise, appropriations and assignments

[3607] FFI is the largest research unit in the Norwegian Defence Force

[3608] FFI will provide advice with the aim of assisting the Ministry of Defence and the defence sector in the development of materiel and investment programmes, as well as contributing to restructuring and rational operations

[3609] The institute will have a special focus on features of scientific and military-technical development that may affect the implications for defense planning on the materiel and technology side

[3610] Furthermore, FFI will assist the top management in the defense sector in providing the best possible basis for decision-making with a view to the further development of the Armed Forces

[3611] FFI will face a number of challenges in the coming years

[3612] Technological development is rapid, and development is increasingly taking place in sectors outside of defense research

[3613] At the same time, developments are occurring very rapidly both in relation to the geographical areas in which units from the Armed Forces are deployed and in terms of the nature of the various operations

[3614] FFI must be able to meet emerging challenges much more quickly than the traditional three-year perspective that projects at FFI have tended to have

[3615] FFI must therefore increasingly be able to contribute to concept development and experimentation processes, as well as have the capacity to handle emerging individual cases

[3616] FFI's role as an independent scientific and technological advisor to the Ministry of Defense and the defense sector is important

[3617] Research is the basis for this advice

[3618] The close contact with clients and users in the sector, and the access to operational and specialist military knowledge this provides, is important for the quality of FFI's research and consultancy

[3619] However, the consideration of concentrating efforts on core activities dictates that the institute's involvement in security policy research and development be limited to topics that are of 105 2007–2008 St.prop

[3620] A defense that protects Norway's security, interests and values, directly relevant to the Armed Forces' structural planning, or in selected thematic areas where the institute possesses particular expertise in a national context, such as in terrorism and societal security

[3621] FFI is well positioned to conduct research on societal vulnerability, particularly in areas where the Armed Forces' and civilian interests overlap

[3622] The focus of such research should therefore be on scientific and technological developments, and their consequences for societal security and preparedness

[3623] Responsibility for research on civil security lies with the responsible sector ministries, and the Ministry of Justice has overall coordinating responsibility for this research in the civilian sector

[3624] The Ministry of Defence will ensure the best possible coordination of its own efforts with the resource efforts of other ministries in this area

[3625] FFI's contact and collaboration with national and international research institutions and environments, both military and civilian, is important in order to gain access to complementary knowledge and thereby increase the quality and efficiency of its own research

[3626] An increasing degree of Norwegian military effort will occur through participation in operations abroad

[3627] It is important that Norwegian military capabilities can interact as best as possible with the capabilities of cooperating countries, and as a whole contribute to mutually reinforcing defense structures

[3628] International cooperation is therefore an important consideration when organizing research activities

[3629] Competence and knowledge must also contribute to the research-based teaching at bachelor's and master's level at the Armed Forces' schools, and build on the good collaboration that has been established between FFI and the Armed Forces' Schools Centre

[3630] Considerations for resource utilization and the desire to avoid duplicating efforts mean that FFI must continue to prioritize research in areas that are not covered by the Armed Forces Education Center or others and draw on resources from these other professional environments rather than building up its own professional environments

[3631] There is significant potential for mutual development and deepening of teaching and research activities between FFI and the Norwegian Armed Forces School Centre, for example through observation and participation in specific work assignments

[3632] FFI will continue to maintain and further develop its analytical capacity to support long-term planning work in the defense sector

[3633] Including conceptual studies, long-term cost calculations and performance assessments of military capabilities and the overall defense structure

[3634] National Security Authority

[3635] The National Security Authority (NSM) is responsible for the executive functions of the preventive security service, which includes, among other things, obtaining and assessing relevant information, supervising the security situation and providing information, advice and guidance to the agencies

[3636] This is done on behalf of the Minister of Justice and the Minister of Defense, where the Minister of Justice has overall responsibility for security in the civilian sector, while the Minister of Defense has a corresponding responsibility in the military sector

[3637] NSM has no function in the actual management of the preventive security service within the individual enterprises

[3638] In the Armed Forces, the Chief of Defence, within the framework of the regulations and with the authority of instruction, is responsible for managing the preventive security service

[3639] The Defence Security Department (FSA) is the department that, on behalf of the Chief of Defence, assumes this responsibility

[3640] The Ministry of Defence is assigned administrative responsibility for NSM, with budgetary and agency management responsibility

[3641] State management takes place in close collaboration with the Ministry of Justice

[3642] When establishing NSM, it was decided that a review of the new agency would be conducted after a certain period of time

[3643] A working group consisting of representatives from the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Defence has been established to conduct a closer review of the agency management of NSM and the directorate's task portfolio

[3644] Although NSM fulfills its responsibilities within both the civilian and military sectors in a consistently good manner, there is a need to look at, among other things, how agency management functions

[3645] The Infrastructure Committee states in its report, the question arises as to whether it is possible in practice to clearly distinguish between agency management responsibility and professional responsibility

[3646] The committee has also pointed out that the responsibilities and tasks assigned to NSM, the Police Security Service (PST) and the Directorate for Civil Protection and Emergency Preparedness (DSB) can be perceived as partially overlapping

[3647] It is therefore natural that, in connection with the review, NSM's task portfolio and interfaces with other actors, including the FSA, be taken into account

[3648] At a time of sometimes major changes in society with regard to security threatening activities and an increasingly rapid pace of change in relation to technological innovations, it would also be natural to take a closer look at the balance in the overall tasks for NSM within the civilian and military sectors, respectively

[3662] P. No. 343 (2000–

[3663] no. 77 (2000–2001), that no depreciation should be introduced on national operational

[3664] EBA and NATO infrastructure

[3666] During the Storting's consideration of the Budget proposal

[3667] No. 7 (2002–2003), cf. St.prp

[3669] No. 1 Supplement No. 6 (2002–2003), where, among other things, it was postponed that rental income should fully cover costs, it was also decided that all investments in property, buildings and facilities should be financed by appropriations

[3670] As a result of the assumptions that formed the basis for St.prop

[3671] No. 77 (2000–2001) has changed and there is further emphasis on the principle of cost-covering rent, the government believes that the depreciation basis should be expanded to include all EBA, including infrastructure, national operational EBA and NATO infrastructure

[3672] Changing the capital element by expanding the depreciation basis will ensure a more complete cost-covering rent, which is the underlying principle in the horizontal trade between the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces

[3673] The actual capital wear and tear resulting from the Armed Forces' EBA use will be made more visible by introducing depreciation in the rent on infrastructure, national operational EBA and NATO infrastructure

[3674] The change means that all EBA will be treated uniformly, which simplifies the rental model

[3675] This will also eliminate unintended negative effects that may arise from different treatment of depreciation within the EBA pool. The change will facilitate a more correct decision-making basis with regard to demand for EBA since all real costs will be visible

[3676] In addition, it will ensure that decisions are based on real costs, which could help prevent overspending or misuse of EBA resources in the defence sector

[3677] The change will also contribute to a better alignment with the real costs at the portfolio level

[3678] Today, annual depreciation amounts to approximately NOK 500 million

[3679] This depreciation element is too low in relation to the need for replacement of the defense sector's EBA over a depreciation period of 60 years

[3680] The change in the rent model has no budgetary consequences and does not affect the defense budget beyond the fact that the respective operating chapters must be allocated an increased allocation corresponding to the increase in the capital element

[3681] This is financed by reducing the amount in chapter 1710, item 47 to the corresponding amount

[3682] Cultural heritage protection – national fortifications

[3683] The national fortifications have significance as national cultural monuments

[3684] The fortresses' history, distinctive architecture and environment make them well suited as a gathering point for artistic and cultural development

[3685] The government's goal is that the national fortifications will be safeguarded through value-preserving and condition-based maintenance and investments

[3686] In 2006, common overall guidelines for the management of cultural and historical state properties were prepared and established

[3687] The guidelines make sectoral responsibility applicable

[3688] This means that each ministry is responsible for ensuring that the guidelines are complied with within its own sector

[3689] The management responsibility for the national fortifications is handled by the Ministry of Defence on behalf of the Ministry of Defence

[3690] The guidelines oblige each property manager to prepare a national conservation plan and management plans

[3691] The defense sector is one of the sectors with the longest experience in managing listed buildings and facilities

[3692] Landsver 107 2007–2008 St.prp

[3693] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values The defense plan for the Armed Forces was completed

[3694] The plans for the 14 national fortifications, which were completed in 2007, provide comprehensive documentation of various conditions at the fortresses, and form the basis for preservation in accordance with the Cultural Heritage Act, or the basis for protection in other ways

[3695] To ensure that the cultural, historical and architectural quality of the buildings is preserved and made visible, long-term and predictable management is necessary

[3696] The fortifications are maintained through condition-based maintenance and are financed by leasing to actors outside the Armed Forces, in addition to annual operating subsidies from the state budget

[3697] Today, rental income constitutes a significant source of operating the facilities

[3698] The long-term goal is to achieve a satisfactory condition level by 2020. A condition assessment carried out by the Ministry of Environment in 2007 will form the basis for prioritizing funds

[3700] The Armed Forces' activities and the environment

[3701] Environmental considerations should be a major consideration in all activities. For the answer is driving, and the most gentle use of the environment should be facilitated

[3702] As a follow-up to the government's environmental policy, climate policy and commitment to a toxic-free environment, the Armed Forces will have increased attention to the following areas

[3703] The business shall systematically seek to reduce emissions of greenhouse gases and nitrogen oxides, emphasis shall be placed on energy efficiency and conversion to heating based on renewable energy sources, work on reducing the use of chemicals hazardous to health and the environment and substituting environmental toxins shall be intensified, and environmental and social responsibility shall be taken into account in all procurements

[3704] Consideration for biological diversity in the Armed Forces' management areas will be further developed

[3705] Central to the Armed Forces' systematic environmental protection efforts is the introduction of environmental management

[3706] Environmental management shall be further developed and contribute to making environmental considerations an integrated part of all planning and decision-making processes

[3707] By having a good environmental management system, the Armed Forces will be able to achieve, among other things, a reduction in environmental impacts in relation to combat capability and activity level (increased degree of environmental efficiency), financial savings through reduced future costs associated with operation and disposal, and a reduction in operational limitations based on environmentally justified restrictions

[3708] The Armed Forces must at all times have an overview and control of its activities, including its input factors and products, which may have a significant impact on the environment

[3709] The Norwegian Armed Forces' environmental database shall be used as a basis for monitoring and systematic improvement of the sector's environmental impacts

[3710] At military airports, the aim is to introduce a system for more active planning, management and documentation of operations to ensure more noise-optimized flight patterns and departure procedures as well as predictability of the activity

[3711] Noise pollution from aircraft is regulated through guidelines from the Ministry of the Environment on land use at airports and through the Pollution Regulations with regard to indoor noise conditions in homes

[3712] Fighter aircraft produce high maximum noise levels during takeoff and represent the main challenge related to aircraft noise for the Armed Forces

[3779] Regional political conditions

[3780] The government will give people real freedom of choice in where they want to live and will lay the foundation for using the entire country

[3781] The Government has a strong desire that all people throughout the country should be able to develop their abilities and live good and meaningful lives

[3782] An active and targeted district and regional policy should contribute to value creation, jobs and welfare where people live

[3783] The government's overall goal in district and regional policy is to facilitate equal living conditions throughout the country and maintain the main features of the settlement pattern

[3790] The armed forces, with their traditionally nationwide activities, have had an impact on settlement, employment and other activities in a number of local communities and regions

[3791] Restructuring and renewal may lead to fewer jobs directly associated with the Armed Forces, and reduced demand for goods and services, both locally and centrally

[3792] In other places, an increased concentration of the Armed Forces' activities will lead to more activity and ripple effects in affected local communities

[3793] Military facilities and infrastructure that the Armed Forces no longer need may also have potential for further development for civilian purposes and thus represent a positive opportunity for the development of individual local communities

[3794] Good and effective disposal processes will be important in this context

[3797] It is therefore important that the Armed Forces maintain a sufficiently decentralized presence in different parts of the country within the framework of what is operationally and socioeconomically appropriate, and so that the Armed Forces can carry out their tasks in the most efficient way possible

[3798] The Government will, insofar as it is consistent with the overall goals for the development of the Armed Forces, seek to ensure that further renewal builds on the district and regional policy goals

[3812] In recent years, the Norwegian Armed Forces have changed from being a mobilization defense force to a defense force that is used at home and abroad every single day – with operations abroad as a natural part of the service

[3813] The same departments are mainly responsible for solving tasks both nationally and internationally – which places very high demands on the employees

[3814] The complexity and dynamics of today's military operations, combined with a continuing need for development and efficiency, place high demands on individual knowledge, skills and attitudes

[3903] Organizational culture, diversity and workload 8.2.1 Organizational culture

[3904] Organizational culture is a foundation for supporting the sector's development, task solving and results, and for influencing individual attitudes and values

[3905] This is an important starting point for the Ministry of Defence's organizational culture

[3906] The military role encompasses a wide range of tasks that ultimately involve sharp operations and a balance between the necessity of using weapons in given situations and the desire to avoid the use of violence

[3907] Culturally, the Armed Forces have over time developed a valuable sense of unity and pride that provides motivation and belonging for the individual, with significant effort and personal commitment involved

[3908] This culture will be an important contribution to the further development of the Armed Forces

[3909] The armed forces' leaders as role models will be an important factor in influencing the organizational culture

[3910] The defense sector shall be further developed as a value-based and learning organization, with an organizational culture characterized by integrity, openness and high ethical standards

[3911] Management, ethics and working environment

[3912] In recent years, the Norwegian Armed Forces have carried out one of the largest restructurings in the public sector, and are still in constant development

[3913] Clear management communication and broad involvement are particularly important in restructuring processes, to provide opportunities for influence, create understanding of and support for the Armed Forces' tasks, organization and challenges, and hold personnel accountable towards achieving the goals

[3914] Transformations require solid foundations and require strong, visible and coordinated leadership as well as good communication of goals and direction

[3915] In the future, there will therefore be a continued strong focus on a good culture of leadership and management

[3916] In this context, it is important that experiences from previous restructurings are utilized and translated into renewed insight

[3917] There is a need for greater transparency regarding management and decision-making processes, as well as the best possible utilization of the organization's overall expertise, to create commitment and involvement, both externally and internally

[3918] Different competencies increase the ability for innovative thinking, and a constantly evolving defense requires an organization with a good culture for sharing knowledge and expertise

[3919] The Armed Forces will continue their work to further develop an organizational culture characterized by responsibility, the ability to learn and the willingness to complete missions

[3920] The follow-up of the measures in the Action Plan for Relations, Ethics and Leadership (HEL) is a key instrument in this context

[3921] The goal is for this work to increase the individual's ethical awareness and integrity

[3922] Participation and dialogue are crucial in all ethics work

[3923] Regular dialogue conferences are one of the measures in the Action Plan

[3924] The purpose is to create greater awareness in the defense sector about employees' own attitudes and their own contributions to a good work culture and a good climate for expression

[3925] The Action Plan further describes measures that include, among other things, the development of e-learning programs for attitudes and ethics and measures aimed at providing managers with knowledge about improving internal and external communication

[3926] Collaboration with external actors and other nations is also a key means of gathering experience and expertise that can contribute to further developing the organizational culture in these areas

[3927] Emphasis will be placed on further developing a working environment where employees thrive and gain motivation

[3928] This will be measured, among other things, through regular employee surveys and followed up through appropriate measures

[3929] There will also be a continuous focus on providing the best possible facilities for reporting objectionable matters

[3932] Diversity and equality

[3943] Workload and family policy The Armed Forces have an uneven distribution of workload between different departments and personnel categories

[3944] The heaviest burden naturally falls on many of the operational units, as well as the functions that provide direct support to them

[3945] Armed Forces personnel also have a special work situation, with relatively long and frequent absences from home, including during naval service, exercises and overseas operations

[3946] In this context, reference is also made to the Regulations on Service in International Operations

[3947] It is a challenge for the Armed Forces to find a good balance between tasks and the individual's needs for leisure and family life

[3948] Violations of AML or other regulations should not, under any circumstances, be permitted

[3952] Furthermore, measures must be considered to train more employees within the personnel categories that are most in demand in relation to such services

[3953] The Armed Forces shall facilitate the provision of services to meet the needs of personnel as far as possible, in various phases of life

[4043] Strengthened compensation protection

[4044] Personnel who are injured in international service receive, in addition to social security benefits, compensation under the Occupational Injury Insurance Act if they have been exposed to an occupational injury or occupational disease that is equivalent to an occupational injury

[4045] Personnel participating in operations abroad also have extended protection against occupational injuries, 24 hours a day

[4046] Employees who fall outside the protection of the Occupational Injury Insurance Act may be entitled to compensation under other grounds of liability, including non-statutory strict liability

[4047] In addition, regulations have been introduced regarding compensation for psychological strain injuries resulting from service in operations abroad

[4048] A working group that assessed compensation protection and submitted a report in 2007, however, pointed out that certain types of damage, including particularly psychological sequelae, did not have sufficient compensation protection under these regulations, and put forward several proposals for measures

[4059] Competence management and personnel administration. 8.4.1 The Armed Forces' competence needs

[4060] The combined competence of the individual employee, the departments and the Defence are key factors in ensuring good task performance at all levels

[4061] The Armed Forces must therefore spend significant resources on developing and managing personnel competence, and on ensuring that the right person is deployed in the right place at the right time

[4062] The extensive restructuring the Armed Forces have undergone has meant that the Armed Forces today have fewer employees to carry out increasingly demanding tasks

[4063] In combination with, among other things, service in foreign operations, this places great pressure on the Armed Forces' ability to maintain robust professional environments

[4064] With a relatively small operational structure, the Armed Forces also face challenges related to staffing demanding functions, including in the Armed Forces' management and support structure as well as in international staffs and departments

[4065] The extensive rotation system creates challenges in terms of continuity, maintenance and development of both the personnel's and the organization's overall competence

[4066] The goal of better competence management is to ensure that the Armed Forces' competence needs can be met at all times - both in the short and long term

[4078] Arrangement of the Armed Forces' personnel structure In order for the Armed Forces to be able to meet future challenges in the best possible way, the personnel structure must be arranged so that an appropriate balance is created between the different personnel categories in relation to the Armed Forces' needs

[4079] A comprehensive modernization of personnel management has been underway for some time

[4080] This has occurred through the introduction of a better adapted command system, adjustments related to the practice of initial service, the introduction of general command access to foreign operations, and the beginning of harmonization of the rank level and personnel composition

[4081] Overall, this contributes to a competence, degree and age structure that is more closely aligned with the organization's needs

[4082] It is planned to continue this work in the coming long-term period

[4083] However, changes to the personnel structure are time- and resource-intensive processes that can take 10-15 years to complete

[4084] When changing structural elements, it must be taken into account that adding the necessary expertise can often take longer than the actual system procurement

[4085] It is therefore essential that changes in the personnel structure are implemented early, preferably before the system acquisitions that create the need for new expertise

[4086] In the case of major system changes, additional personnel costs must be calculated because it usually takes a long time to change and further develop the skills of employees

[4087] This means that during such periods of change, the Armed Forces must have more personnel than the ongoing operations require at any given time

[4088] A more long-term perspective in personnel planning will reduce the need for major staff reductions by encouraging employees to leave before reaching retirement age

[4089] High job rotation poses challenges in terms of planning and managing personnel resources and expertise

[4090] The rotation of military personnel in various service positions should thus be reduced

[4091] This includes the need for stronger management from the employer, increased focus on horizontal careers, a reduction in the number of fixed-term positions and greater emphasis on continuity and tenure

[4092] The degree may also be an indication that the Armed Forces have had too strong a focus on vertical careers

[4093] Personnel management The Act of 2 July 2004 on personnel in the Armed Forces and the introduction of a new command system (BO) entailed a change in the personnel management system

[4094] In this connection, a unified management system was established where all commands were subject to an application system

[4095] This unified management system ensures equal rights and obligations for the entire commanding corps, but has also had some unintended consequences

[4096] The current practice of the application system results in an inappropriately high personnel rotation, which has also been pointed out by the Defence Policy Committee

[4097] The committee writes in its report, among other things, that “the current extensive rotation of military personnel in various positions should be greatly reduced

[4098] This will involve a greater element of ordering than the current application system

[4099] Experience has shown that the rate of rotation among lower-ranking officers in particular is a challenge

[4100] These are in a phase where they are building their competence and career, and an application system can often tempt individuals to apply for positions that seem attractive in the short term, but which do not necessarily provide the long-term competence that the command needs or the continuity that the Armed Forces need

[4101] In addition, the system creates challenges in relation to the use of service plans, which is an important management instrument in the follow-up of personnel

[4102] There is thus a need for greater focus on continuity in position and opportunities for horizontal careers, as well as a more flexible allocation system, adapted to both the needs of the Armed Forces and the individual

[4103] It is therefore planned to adjust the command system, so that the disposition of commanders at the rank of ensign and below has a greater element of command

[4104] This means that they are allocated according to service needs, consideration for competence development and the individual's prior learning

[4105] Such an adaptation of the deployment system for the lower-grade levels requires the Armed Forces to ensure a thorough review of local employer obligations

[4106] For mandatory service plans, they should be prepared through dialogue, so that the assigned commander has a predictable and competence-building assignment period

[4107] To ensure a certain degree of predictability for personnel, the adaptation of the disposition system should be followed by normal advancement from sergeant/quartermaster to ensign

[4108] Normal advancement means that personnel are automatically promoted to the next grade after a set period of time in the grade

[4226] The Norwegian Armed Forces' salary policy

[4227] Salary is one of several important components of a comprehensive personnel policy

[4228] The wage and salary system must be appropriate in terms of recruiting and retaining qualified personnel

[4229] The armed forces must be perceived as an attractive and competitive workplace, also in terms of salary levels and opportunities for salary development

[4230] The main collective agreement will form the basis for work on reforms in wage policy in the Armed Forces

[4231] The Armed Forces shall seek to develop long-term strategies that are independent of economic cycles in cooperation with employee organizations

[4232] Average basic salary growth in the Armed Forces shall follow salary developments in the rest of the state, and Armed Forces employees shall, as a general rule, be given the same conditions as other state employees

[4233] Civilian and military employees in the Armed Forces are treated equally as long as the fundamental characteristics of the position, including rights and obligations, are essentially the same

[4234] It is further assumed that employees in the defense sector should have equal pay for work of equal value, regardless of gender, ethnic background or functional ability

[4235] The salary system must be set up so that it enables acceptable salary development in a horizontal career path, not least to ensure salary development for department commanders and enlisted personnel who are employed on a temporary basis

[4248] Session, conscription and initial service

[4249] Session Through the session scheme, the Armed Forces have a unique opportunity to meet and market themselves to a large proportion of each cohort

[4250] In a recruitment context, this puts the Armed Forces in a special position, and the Armed Forces must use this opportunity in an optimal way

[4251] Today's session process is characterized by challenges in getting the right person in the right place, by high dropout rates upon induction, and by the fact that the period between session and service is too long

[4252] There is also too little follow-up and dialogue with the individual conscript during this period

[4253] Further development of the session scheme The Government wants to make the session a better selection and recruitment tool, and plans for future sessions to be conducted in two parts

[4254] Part I will be a self-declaration, primarily online, where the purpose is to obtain basic information about the individual's health, conditions and interests, and the goal is to use this as a basis for further selection and follow-up

[4255] Part II will involve the best suited and most motivated meeting for a session in one of the Armed Forces' session rooms

[4256] The focus will be on targeted recruitment activities, including information about the branches of defense and service positions, classification and testing of the individual

[4257] To increase quality, it is planned to abolish the ambulatory session and introduce a number of permanent session locations in different parts of the country

[4258] However, this must be practiced in a flexible manner, so that geographical distances do not impair the individual's ability to attend a session

[4259] Such a measure means that fewer people are called to session part II, thus freeing up both time and resources, in addition to increasing the quality of the session as a whole

[4260] It also creates space for the most suitable individuals to be identified as early as possible, and for session part II to be held as close to the start date as possible, which will contribute positively to the follow-up of the individual during this period

[4261] Targeted, online follow-up of those in military service is planned for the period from session part

[4275] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values ​​Box 8.1 What is general conscription

[4276] General conscription today means that all men who are deemed capable of military service are liable for military service

[4277] The essence of conscription is that all able-bodied Norwegian male citizens shall be at the disposal of the nation from the age of 18 to the age of 44, i.e. a total of 25 years

[4278] Military service is not the same as first-time service

[4279] Eligible persons who are not called up for service in the first instance are still subject to conscription and can be called up if the need arises

[4280] In other words, conscripts perform their duty even if they are not called up and complete their initial service

[4281] General conscription is thus a national emergency plan, in case there should be times when the population must be mobilized to protect our country

[4282] Military defense is a fundamental task that citizens should stand together for

[4283] Conscription is the fundamental element in the Armed Forces' recruitment

[4284] The use of conscripts who are in their first year of service works well for many types of national operations and as a basis for and preparation for operations abroad

[4285] Through conscription, the Armed Forces have the opportunity to recruit the employees they need

[4589] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values Goals, measures and implementation

[4590] Targeted implementation

[4591] The entirety of the measures proposed in this proposal will ensure a relevant defense, prepared to handle a wide range of different tasks both nationally and internationally

[4592] For the government, the central objective has been to lay the foundation for sustainability in the defense sector by continuing and further developing what has been achieved through modernization

[4593] The Armed Forces must have military capabilities with the necessary reaction capability, operational capability, availability and endurance, with conscription forming a foundation, while at the same time cooperating effectively with allies

[4594] This long-term proposition lays this foundation

[4595] At the same time, these are ambitious goals that place high demands on the sector in their implementation

[4596] It is essential that the sector, through both planning and implementation work, is able to adhere to overall goals and develop towards them through a balance between continuing and improving existing solutions and adding new ones, in the most efficient and appropriate way possible

[4597] The foundation for the implementation work is continuous improvement and development within the framework of established restructuring goals and the specified overall financial framework for the defense sector

[4598] The defense sector manages significant resources on behalf of society

[4599] There are strict requirements for these resources to be managed efficiently and in line with political decisions

[4600] It is very important that the defense sector maintains good cost control and prudent management of personnel and materiel

[4601] This requires management skills, but is also dependent on attitudes, ethics and management that support this

[4602] In addition, it requires expertise and an organization of the business that makes it manageable and intention-driven

[4603] Good incentive structures and clear priorities must support the overall goals that have been set

[4604] These are matters that will be given special emphasis both in the preparations for the implementation – and also in the implementation – of this long-term plan

[4605] The focus on further developing attitudes, leadership and organizational culture is central in this context

[4606] An ongoing challenge has been to ensure predictability in the sector's framework factors, and a balance between tasks, structure and access to resources

[4607] The level of funding is a crucial factor for this balance

[4608] In addition, the business's own ability to manage and implement is also crucial to ensuring sustainable development of the sector

[4609] The Government places particular emphasis on ensuring that the further development of the sector takes place in a holistic manner

[4610] It is important that the processes within the sector, and the communication between the sector and its surroundings, function well

[4611] This is essential so that the defense sector can continue to be – and also appear to be – a relevant security policy instrument for Norway

[4612] The foundation for the further development of the Armed Forces

[4613] The government is primarily concerned with facilitating sustainable development that ensures that the sector can fulfill its tasks nationally and internationally, both in the short and long term

[4688] Investments in materials and equipment

[4689] One of the most significant measures to ensure a better balance between economic conditions and the structure recommended in this proposal has been a significant reduction in the level of new procurement of equipment

[4690] This has contributed to reducing the average annual level of material investment by approximately NOK 1.6 billion compared to continuing the structure adopted for the period 2005-2008 in the period

[4691] This reduction is partly a result of a critical review of all investment plans to prioritize and reduce the level of ambition within a number of capacities, and partly through reductions and closures of individual capacities, as well as very sober investment assumptions related to new initiatives in this plan

[4692] The recommended structure thus contains a total of 135 2007–2008 St.proposals

[4693] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values based on very sober investment assumptions

[4694] Therefore, during implementation, special emphasis must be placed on ensuring that this sober approach is also used as a basis for planning material investments overall and individual projects

[4695] To ensure that the investment conditions are realized, there are two factors in particular that will be emphasized

[4696] The first will be to ensure that all investments that are planned and implemented are based on a sober “good enough” approach that is based on the basic and primary requirements for the material systems

[4697] Alternative ways of procuring materials – for example by joining forces with other countries, particularly in purchasing off-the-shelf products and/or materials produced on a large scale – will also need to receive increased attention within such an approach

[4698] Secondly, priority will be given consistently to projects where the purpose is to put in place basic capacities linked to the adopted structure

[4699] Projects where the main purpose is to increase capacity and improve existing capacity will have to be given lower priority

[4700] Investments in real estate, buildings and structures

[4701] The organizational changes resulting from the proposals in this plan will require significant investments in property, buildings and facilities

[4702] Renewal of the operational structure, increase in the number of man-years in the Norwegian Defence Force, concentration on fewer bases, as well as a continued significant need for renewal of the EBA stock in the defence sector, means that the sector will carry out significant upgrades of existing property stock and investments in new buildings and facilities in the coming years

[4703] Investments in the existing building stock have in recent years been at a somewhat lower level than what is necessary in the long term to continue and maintain the values inherent in the building stock managed by the sector

[4704] An important explanation is the sharp increase in costs within construction

[4705] Sufficient progress on the renewal and restructuring, where not least the consolidation of the operational headquarters to Reitan near Bodø constitutes an important initiative, will be crucial because the operational savings associated with the relevant EBA constitute an important part of the financial assumptions on which the long-term plan is based

[4706] There is therefore a close connection between how quickly the sector will be able to implement EBA investments that are critical to the transition, and how quickly the operational savings on which this plan is based can be realized

[4707] A balanced approach is therefore planned in prioritizing EBA investments

[4708] In addition to EBA investments related to the working environment and HSE requirements, restructuring-related projects related to realizing operational savings and increasing operational capability will be given priority in implementation

[4709] At the same time, special emphasis will be placed on ensuring that the EBA investments that are planned and implemented are based on and maintain sober needs assessments and ambitions

[4710] It will be important that a sober level of ambition is reflected in the detailing of the EBA investments, both in the design and implementation of the individual investment projects

[4765] Predictability with regard to economic development

[4766] Implementing long-term plans is challenging

[4767] The basis for the long-term plan is based on a number of assumptions, some of which are assumptions that the sector itself can only influence to a limited extent

[4768] This includes externally imposed costs, budget levels, wage growth, price growth, equipment service lives, operational ambition levels and, to some extent, feasibility of equipment procurement and infrastructure measures

[4769] The recommended structure and associated level of ambition are based on the economic assumptions discussed in Chapter

[4770] If this structure is to be continued and further developed beyond 2012, these financial conditions must be met and continued

[4771] Economic development within this long-term period, and beyond, that does not correspond to the assumptions in this proposition will have long-term structural consequences

[4772] At the same time, necessary structural measures, aimed at restoring the balance between budget and costs and thereby ensuring ongoing sustainability, often do not have sufficient economic effect in the short term

[4773] Structural measures must therefore be supplemented with short-term and operational ad hoc measures to ensure coverage in the near term

[4774] This means that if the economic conditions change and the structure is once again put under pressure, the government will have to return to the Storting within the planning period with further proposed changes of a structural nature, both related to the operational structure, support activities and the base structure

[4775] The Government considers it crucial that the consequences of any changes in economic conditions are assessed and handled in a long-term perspective

[4776] Any financial changes in the annual perspective must be handled structurally and in a multi-year perspective

[4777] Cost control and sound management

[4778] The restructuring from 2001 to the present day has largely been followed up in accordance with the assumptions

[4779] The overall operational capabilities of the Armed Forces have been strengthened during the period

[4780] A key basis for this is structural renewal, management reform and relatively stable budget development, where the defense sector's overall spending over a number of years has been close to the projected level

[4781] As part of this restructuring, the defense sector has improved control over cost developments, particularly in the area of operations

[4782] In the coming period, efforts in this area will be further strengthened, with particular focus on continuous improvements and good incentive structures for cost control

[4783] Administration, including business management, constitutes a main function in the sector's overall operation and development

[4784] The Government emphasizes that sound management is given high priority in the defense sector

[4785] This requires that the sector, among other things, adapts its personnel structure, advancement and allocation system so that a long-term stable personnel and competence balance is established within the administrative area

[4786] A strong prioritization of overall management will result in better utilization of management expertise, and ensure an area of expertise that is better aligned with the other main functions in the sector

[4787] The defense sector will therefore make greater use of civilian expertise within administration, financial functions, logistics and support systems

[4788] Positions that primarily require civilian expertise should preferably be filled by civilian personnel

[4789] Management and governance

[4790] The establishment of integrated strategic management in 2003 has contributed to creating better strategic management and control of the sector, and the reform has given the sector a better basis for effective management and leadership

[4791] Similar to the Defence Policy Committee

[4792] No. 48 2007–

[4793] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values. The government also believes that this reform has given strategic management better conditions for good and effective management

[4794] The Government believes that the main features of the chosen model should be continued and further developed, cf. the proposed changes in chapter

[4795] There are, however, several issues and dilemmas related to management and governance in the sector that cannot be addressed solely through structural changes

[4796] It will be just as important to further develop and improve both management processes, organizational culture and management execution

[4797] In this context, there are certain areas that will receive particular emphasis in the coming years

[4798] It is, and will continue to be, a continuous challenge for the sector to find a good balance between focusing on challenges that should be solved in a long-term perspective, and focusing on achieving operational goals and results in the short term

[4799] In this context, the government is planning two measures in particular that are expected to improve this balance in the future

[4800] Firstly, the recommended changes in strategic management will provide a clearer division of responsibilities and tasks at the highest levels, and in this way lay the foundation for clearer management of responsibilities and division of roles

[4801] This is essential to avoid overlapping work, not least ambiguity about which issues are handled at different levels in the organization

[4802] The fundamental thing in this context – which is also the central premise of today's management model – is that responsibility for the overall strategic and long-term planning and management is assigned to the integrated ministry

[4803] Secondly, a more continuous approach to long-term planning is taken as the basis, as the government has taken the initiative to do, cf. chapter

[4804] This will also help to strengthen the focus on implementation and continuous improvement, by addressing the need for change when it arises rather than creating uncertainty about the consequences for adopted goals and choices

[4805] The two measures mentioned above will help to facilitate a better balance between long-term challenges and short-term goal achievement

[4806] A final crucial element in this is also open, predictable and involving processes between the different levels of the organization, employee organizations and other partners

[4807] Furthermore, it is absolutely crucial that a sector undergoing continuous modernization and restructuring has leadership that steers in one common direction

[4808] It is important to have a good and open dialogue about the development of the sector and about key choices

[4809] Once the decision has been made, targeted work must be done to achieve the agreed goals and implement the decided measures

[4810] In this context, a special responsibility rests on all levels of management in the sector, but especially on the highest levels, which must take the lead and lead the work towards adopted plans and goals

[4811] In this area, the sector faces certain challenges today

[4812] To ensure goal achievement, necessary safety for the sector's employees and the environment, and the sector's reputation, this will therefore be an area that will be focused on going forward

[4813] Among other things, greater emphasis will be placed on change management and implementation of restructuring as criteria for evaluation and further development of both managers and employees

[4814] In order to build trust in the organization, establish a management based restructuring and stronger organizational affiliation, the government wants to emphasize increased continuity in leadership positions, as well as clearer performance requirements for individual leaders

[5000] No. 48 2007–

[5001] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values The development of the defense in the long term

[5002] A defense capable of change and adaptation

[5003] A changeable and adaptable defense – which can meet a broad spectrum of possible security challenges and continuously adapt to changes in the environment – will be the best guarantee that Norway can meet future defense and security policy challenges

[5004] In order for this ability to change to be present, a long-term and broad perspective must be taken on the further development of the Armed Forces

[5005] The Government places emphasis on creating and maintaining the best possible balance between the tasks

[5006] The defense is required to resolve the framework conditions that the sector receives

[5007] Long-term and predictable frameworks as well as continuous processes should form the defense sector’s basis for comprehensive long-term planning

[5008] Given the long lead times associated with the Ministry of Defence's material investments and the production of military expertise, it is neither possible, appropriate nor desirable to adopt an approach where sweeping changes are implemented in the defence sector based on short-term priorities

[5009] While the Armed Forces must have the necessary flexibility and the greatest possible robustness to handle continuous changes and new challenges, it is important to create predictability around the overall political objectives and framework for the Armed Forces' activities

[5010] This part of the proposal outlines some of the main assumptions that the government believes should be the basis for the further development of the Armed Forces in a more long-term perspective, and the opportunities and potential choices that follow from these

[5011] In addition, the lines and trade-offs outlined here will form part of the basis for a more continuous and comprehensive further development of the Armed Forces, where both short-term needs and long-term goals are prioritized against each other

[5012] The goal of establishing such an approach to further developing the defense sector is to ensure that consideration of the long-term perspective and the long-term consequences of the choices made are given greater weight

[5013] At the same time, this approach will facilitate the necessary prioritization and choices being made, based on needs and challenges as they arise, so that long-term challenges do not accumulate

[5014] The recommended defense structure, and the framework factors that are the basis for this proposition, form a good starting point for the continuous further development of the Armed Forces, where the balance between ambitions, resources and structure will overall remain sustainable

[5015] The Armed Forces will thus be able to continue the current modernization line, in a more rational and cost-effective manner

[5016] Stability and uncertainty

[5017] Long-term defence development will be driven by the interaction between developments in the sector's key framework conditions, the defence policy goals that are set and the consequences of the choices and priorities that have already been made

[5018] In this way, the long-term development of the response will be characterized by both predictability and unpredictability at the same time

[5019] Unpredictability is largely created by the uncertainty and complexity associated with developments in the overall framework conditions, such as security policy and socio-economic developments both globally and in our local areas, as well as technological developments

[5020] The consequences of the choices and priorities that have already been made in relation to the sector will in themselves represent a relatively large degree of stability, as the consequences of these choices largely form the premises for the further development of the Response

[5021] This predictability constitutes a significant feature of the defense sector, in that it is both specialized, personnel-intensive and investment-intensive

[5022] The long-term development of the armed forces will therefore be associated with a significant degree of unpredictability, while the sector has a fundamentally stable character

[5023] A number of dilemmas and challenges will arise at the intersection between the requirement for the ability to change, which is driven by unpredictable 145 2007–2008 St.prop

[5024] A defense that protects Norway's security, interests and values and the more fundamental stability that lies in the sector's unique nature

[5025] The key to further defense planning lies in meeting these challenges through a holistic and targeted approach based on the current security policy goals and the current defense policy basis

[5026] Framework for further development

[5027] Security policy goals and ambitions

[5028] As part of the state's power apparatus, the Armed Forces shall be a modern and flexible security policy instrument

[5029] The security policy objectives and political ambitions guide the development of the Armed Forces

[5030] – To prevent war and the emergence of various threats to Norwegian and collective security

[5031] – To contribute to peace, stability and the further development of a UN-led international legal order

[5032] – To safeguard Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights, interests and values and protect Norwegian freedom of action against political, military and other pressure

[5033] – Together with our allies, defend Norway and NATO against attacks and threats

[5034] – To secure society against attacks and threats from state and non-state actors

[5035] At the same time, defense planning is of such a nature that changes in strategic or security policy framework factors that may impact Norway may occur faster than the Armed Forces' ability to adapt

[5036] The external threat situation may change as a result of external conditions - such as changes in the security policy environment or technological developments among potential adversaries

[5037] The changes could have consequences for defense development or the organization of the defense structure, either in the form of capacity expansion in certain areas or capacity reductions in others

[5038] Possible security policy developments in the longer term Norway's security policy challenges beyond the planning period will be a result of developments globally and in our immediate areas, and it is expected that global developments will increasingly affect the situation in Norway's immediate areas

[5039] Norway is today facing new geopolitical developments with potentially major consequences for the future global pattern

[5040] However, the world is changing and developments can take several directions

[5041] The next few years may be decisive for the direction the development actually takes, and it will therefore be important to monitor and analyze this

[5042] Depending on the direction of development, this could have significant consequences for Norway, both in terms of security and defense policy

[5043] That Norway should be able to play an active and constructive security policy role internationally is a long-term goal that is based on broad consensus in the Storting

[5044] Norway must be a clear peace nation, and supranational and global challenges must be resolved through joint efforts and commitments

[5045] The values ​​that we wish to protect require a broad and long-term approach to defence development

[5046] The requirement for Norwegian military engagement, both nationally and internationally, could be significant, both to safeguard our national interests, for humanitarian reasons and to contribute to international security

[5047] There is great uncertainty in predicting how developments will be in the medium or long term

[5048] However, a number of development directions can be outlined, all of which are possible, but with varying degrees of probability

[5049] On a general and overall basis, it may be possible to envision both a positive, a gloomy, and a more challenging development

[5050] A predominantly positive development could be characterized by the gradual reduction of the extent of risks and threats to collective security and international peace and stability

[5051] Such a development would require that the relationship between the largest international actors is characterized by fundamental cooperation and a world order based on stability, which could be expressed in a greater degree of cooperation in dealing with common challenges such as international terrorism, the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, global environmental challenges and regional conflicts

[5052] The absence of great power conflicts in such a situation would contribute to giving multilateral security systems, such as the UN, room for manoeuvre

[5053] Also in our immediate areas, one could imagine that the line of cooperation would prevail, based on common Norwegian-Russian interests in the resource area

[5054] Such a development could be assumed to contribute to reducing the overall challenges in our immediate areas, and provide an opportunity to turn an even greater part of our attention to the challenges internationally, including participation in peace-support operations

[5055] At the other end of the spectrum, a possible bleak direction of development can be described, based on an antagonistic world order characterized by increasing fundamental contradictions

[5056] In the worst case, 146 St.prop

[5057] No. 48 2007–

[5058] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values could once again face a conventional or nuclear threat that could require the build-up of larger military forces to ensure military deterrence and collective defense

[5059] This would leave less room for multilateral security arrangements

[5060] The same could apply to the possibilities for jointly addressing global challenges such as the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, terrorism and the environment

[5061] The state perspective and symmetrical threats could once again become dominant, with negative consequences also in nearby Norwegian areas

[5062] This in turn could have consequences for safeguarding Norwegian interests, the development of the Armed Forces and what tasks NATO should undertake related to collective defense and security

[5063] Our ability to engage internationally could be reduced, despite ongoing challenges in this area

[5064] The third possible development direction could represent a continuation and strengthening of the current development direction towards a more multipolar world, but without this culminating in open contradiction or confrontation between the most important international actors

[5065] However, the tendency towards increased rivalry would, in such a situation, be clear, with consequences for relations between the great powers, for smaller states, and potentially also for the Western security system

[5066] Multilateralism could, as it does today, play an important role in providing legitimacy for the use of military force and in solving a number of global challenges

[5067] The state perspective would have to be expected to be central, something we are already seeing in our own immediate areas, and a deterioration in the international situation could have an impact on the situation in the north

[5068] The further development of the defense structure must take into account a development that may be characterized by threats such as global environmental challenges, increased competition for strategic raw materials, international terrorism and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction

[5069] Future challenges in the North are linked to, among other things, resource management, unresolved jurisdictional issues in areas characterized by significant fisheries and petroleum resources, as well as climate change and environmental challenges

[5070] New opportunities in the north have resulted in increased shipping traffic, which will lead to increased demands for maritime safety and emergency preparedness

[5071] Long-term investment in the High North, a strengthened role for the UN in the international community, and increased focus on societal security are fundamental elements of Norwegian security policy

[5072] The global era is characterized by a number of internal and cross-border conflicts, which have serious consequences for human rights and regional stability, often with consequences far beyond the regional level

[5073] The most characteristic feature of today's international picture is gradual, but nonetheless fundamental, changes over a relatively short period of time

[5074] This must be expected to continue, which means that international developments going forward will be characterized more than anything else by uncertainty and ongoing challenges

[5075] This underlines the importance, for smaller countries like Norway, of being able to act within an alliance framework that safeguards our common security interests, as well as the need to have a credible national capability to be able to carry out the tasks that follow from being a sovereign state

[5076] Combined with increased challenges in our immediate vicinity, Norway must also be able to contribute to international peace and stability, including through contributions to peace-support operations

[5077] The overall challenges at home and abroad could be significant, with the Armed Forces playing a central role

[5078] In developing the Armed Forces, we must take into account that the challenges we may face in the longer term may be different from those we face and are able to see today

[5079] In such a perspective, it becomes more important to focus on what we should defend than what we should defend ourselves against

[5080] The consequence of this is that the Armed Forces must be organized to safeguard our fundamental security, and the values and interests we as a nation wish to protect

[5081] A long-term and robust defense and security policy must have this as its starting point

[5082] It is therefore important that the defense structure is developed in a long-term perspective, and that it is at the same time scenario-robust in order to be able to take into account various developments, where uncertainty and ongoing challenges both internationally and in our immediate vicinity will very likely shape the security picture

[5083] Technological development

[5086] This makes it possible to provide relatively precise estimates regarding what military equipment will be available in the next 10-15 years

[5088] Norway, as a small country with limited resources, will normally acquire ready-made equipment, or alternatively develop modern technology and capacities through collaboration with others

[5164] Key factors in longer-term defense development

[5165] A broader approach to desired instruments A comprehensive security policy, increased focus on societal security and a good balance between military and civil preparedness will strengthen Norway's ability to meet both traditional and new security challenges

[5166] It is increasingly expected that the Armed Forces can use force with coordinated, precise and situation-adapted means

[5167] Effects-based thinking sees military operations in a larger context, where efforts are coordinated with other military units and civilian agencies and are subject to an overall political strategy

[5263] Further development of long-term planning After the Cold War, the framework conditions for the defense sector have changed significantly

[5264] A more uncertain and complex threat landscape with great dynamics characterizes Norway's security policy environment both globally and in our own immediate areas

[5265] The defense sector has also experienced a greater degree of unpredictability related to the economic framework conditions

[5266] In sum, this has led to the need for change arising more quickly and more continuously

[5267] Strategic defense planning cannot therefore be based exclusively on a projection of the current situation

[5268] It must also create a robust basis for change and adaptation to the unexpected, both in the short and long term

[5269] This places increased demands on strategic long-term planning in the defense sector

[5270] This must be able to continuously absorb changes and handle them in a sufficiently long-term and holistic perspective

[5271] Today, we are experiencing that the framework and conditions for the Defence Sector's activities are changing so rapidly that choices and priorities made in certain areas must be adjusted after only a short time

[5272] Furthermore, it is a challenge that early in each new planning period we must restart work on comprehensive and far-reaching reforms in which large parts of the defense sector are "thrown up into the air

[5273] This contributes both to weakening the long-term perspective of political decisions that have just been made and to removing focus from the implementation of adopted plans

[5274] It also creates unnecessary uncertainty and insecurity in the organization, among individual employees, and in the local communities affected by the Armed Forces' activities

[5275] In municipalities and regions where the Armed Forces are a key player, this often creates a recurring uncertainty, with consequences for jobs, business development, housing prices and other conditions

[5276] These challenges must be met by finding a good and correct balance between the need for stability and sustainability in the long term and the necessary ability to adapt in the shorter term

[5277] On the one hand, this means that the development of the defense sector must be based on specific and long-term goals that are fixed over time

[5278] Both the planning and implementation work must have a sufficient time horizon

[5279] Key objectives and priorities cannot be changed continuously

[5280] This would lead to a loss of control and to ad hoc development, where comprehensive priorities are replaced by short-term, changing and random considerations

[5281] At the same time, long-term planning must be designed so that the sector is able to respond to changes to a greater extent than today, and so that the course can be adjusted if necessary

[5282] The goal is to create the most robust possible basis for the long-term development of the Armed Forces, where necessary changes can be handled within the framework of established overall goals and priorities

[5283] The Government therefore proposes that the future development of the defense sector should take place through more continuous strategic and long-term development work within the framework of the integrated ministry

[5284] This should be a natural, clear and more permanent activity in the strategic management of the defence sector, and appear less like extraordinary and all-encompassing executive actions

[5285] This will help to

[5286] – Ensure increased predictability and less insecurity for the Armed Forces, its employees and partners

[5287] – Create a better match between planning and implementation

[5288] – Ensure that short-term priorities are made in a long-term perspective and in a holistic manner

[5289] – Establish a more robust planning basis and better documented traceability in the planning work

[5290] – Strengthen the long-term perspective in all parts of the business

[5291] Such an approach follows up on key assumptions that were made when today's integrated strategic management in the defense sector was established

[5292] This is about strengthening the ability to strategically 153 2007–2008 St.prop
