[5340] The professional military input to this proposition is based on the proposals in the Chief of Defence's Defence Study 2007 (FS 07), which was presented in November. The Chief of Defence's recommended force structure with associated base and support structure and adapted personnel structure represents his view of how the Armed Forces should be organised for the future, based on the tasks and the study's financial framework

[5341] The recommendation places considerable emphasis on establishing a functional balance between the operational structure and the associated base and support structure, as well as a corresponding balance between the structure's total resource requirements and the financial framework

[5342] The main focus has been on ensuring the greatest possible operational capability and establishing a long-term balanced defence through a holistic approach to developing the Defence structure in the period 2009 to 2028, with a focus on the period

[5343] The long-term proposition that is now being presented continues the main lines of the Armed Forces' development from recent years, and will provide Norway with a modern and qualitatively good defense with the ability to solve both national tasks and tasks that we must solve in cooperation with others - nationally and internationally

[5344] The answer will thus continue to be a flexible security policy tool for our authorities, with the ability to operate both within and outside the country's borders

[5345] Economic assumptions The Chief of Defence's recommendation in Defence Study 07 is based on an assumption that the defence budget will continue in real terms at the 2008 level in the period

[5346] In this context, real continuation means that the budget development follows the wage and price development in the defense sector

[5347] This assumption is central to the possibility of the Norwegian Defence Forces being able to maintain and develop their operational capabilities and establish and maintain a defence structure in long-term balance

[5348] If the ongoing loss of purchasing power continues, it will quickly undermine the defense structure

[5349] This must then be expected to have an accelerating attrition effect in the years ahead, because it is no longer possible to exploit the remnants of a redundant mobilization defense, as we have been able to do until now

[5350] The long-term proposal sets out a future budget level that is kroner 800 million per year above the financial planning assumption in the response study

[5351] The Chief of Defence is satisfied with the prioritization of the Defence Forces that this entails, but at the same time emphasises the necessity for this budget level to be followed up in future years' budgets

[5352] Otherwise, such an increase would be directly detrimental to structural development

[5353] because in such a situation the Armed Forces will begin building up a defense that in the long term it turns out that they will not be able to maintain, resulting in an increasing imbalance

[5354] This would then entail the risk of major misinvestments and represent a very poor use of society's resources

[5355] A budget development in which the Armed Forces' purchasing power is maintained from year to year is therefore of greater importance for the stability of the structure than the initial budget level

[5356] The Chief of Defence has no comment on the further development of the strategic leadership of the Armed Forces, other than strongly advising against the relocation of the Inspectors General and their staffs out of the Defence Staff

[5357] This will significantly complicate the daily management of the agency, and in particular weaken the possibilities for ongoing financial management by separating very important capital owners from the central financial management

[5358] The long-term proposal continues the Chief of Defence's recommendation to establish a joint operational headquarters in the Armed Forces

[5359] This will bring greater consistency between the command structure and the departments to be managed, provide more robust professional environments and improve the ability for 24/7 management of operations

[5360] No. 48 2007–

[5361] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values

[5362] Furthermore, such a solution will simplify the lines of command and cooperation with civilian actors, while ensuring the ability to manage national operations, monitor Norwegian forces in operations abroad and conduct major joint operational exercises in Norway

[5363] The measure also contributes to a general streamlining of the Armed Forces' operations by reducing infrastructure and support needs in the long term

[5364] The operational structure that the long-term proposal proposes is a modern, high-quality structure that ensures the ability for joint operations and the necessary interoperability

[5365] Of particular importance in this respect is the increase in mobility and deployment capability, combined with an increased ability to operate in networks, both between own land, sea and air forces and with allies and partners

[5366] The operational structure is available to a limited extent for operations both at home and abroad, especially for the Army

[5367] This is due to the focus on continuing the current army model, where a significant portion of resources is tied to conscription-based education departments

[5368] Given the increasing complexity of modern materiel and rising competence requirements, these units have national operational readiness value only in the final months of their service, and at the same time they cannot be sent abroad

[5369] Their most important function is therefore as a recruitment well for short-term recruitment of crews for international operations

[5370] The structure nevertheless has limited depth and robustness in several areas, which reduces the ability to sustain operations

[5371] With the recommended force structure, the Armed Forces' contribution to operations abroad should therefore be based to a greater extent than to date on the use of the entire structural breadth, i.e. the use of operational units and departments from all branches of defence to provide endurance internationally

[5372] The desire to stand out over time with a substantial force contribution from the Army, ideally a battalion, will not be feasible, but in the Chief of Defence's assessment this should not be a limiting ambition either

[5373] The structure is thus in most areas in line with the Chief of Defence's recommendations, but deviates from this primarily in relation to the design and organisation of the land forces

[5374] Continuation of the Skjold-class MTB will, subject to financial coverage, strengthen the Norwegian Navy's ability to conduct coastal operations

[5375] The question of which operational bases and installations should be continued beyond those for which there is a strict need must be expected to arise again during the period, if economic priorities make it necessary

[5376] Base and support structure

[5377] To ensure both economic and structural balance, and thereby maintain and develop the Armed Forces' operational capability in the long term, the Chief of Defence in Defence Study 07 recommended a significant concentration of similar activities and the closure of a larger number of bases

[5378] The Chief of Defence is satisfied that the long-term proposal, with some exceptions, has based this recommendation on this

[5379] With the uncertainty that characterized the problem of noise from new combat aircraft after the presentation of FS 07, the Chief of Defence therefore supports an approach in which the future location of combat aircraft, air defence and base sets are assessed in light of the process associated with the procurement of new combat aircraft

[5380] It is nevertheless emphasized that the establishment of a unified base for the fighter aircraft will be a key strategic measure to contribute to long-term financial balance and major operational synergies

[5381] This measure should therefore be implemented as soon as possible after remaining uncertainties have been clarified

[5382] However, in light of the possible consequences of the noise issue for the location, the possibility of a third location alternative should still be kept open

[5383] The Chief of Defence is also of the opinion that there is still untapped potential

[5384] for further concentration of bases and activities which, if realised, will further improve the functional balance and thereby contribute to ensuring the maintenance and further development of the Armed Forces' operational capability

[5385] Assessments should therefore be carried out with the aim of identifying how the Armed Forces' base and support structure can best be further developed in this respect

[5386] A personnel corps with the right composition in terms of rank, category, age and competence is central to ensuring good task performance and continuing and further developing the Armed Forces as a usable and relevant security policy tool

[5387] The Chief of Defence has therefore placed great emphasis on this area in his recommendation

[5388] The further development of the allocation scheme with a focus on precise competence management, service needs, increased local influence and increased

[5389] Continuity, especially at lower degree levels, will be important measures to ensure that the Armed Forces have the right expertise at all levels of the organization

[5390] Of particular importance is the work to further develop departmental 157 7 2007–2008 St.prop

[5391] A defence to protect Norway's security, interests and values, the system is designed to ensure increased continuity and experience at the lower levels

[5392] The long-term budget proposal's emphasis on the need to increase the number of department commanders is thus entirely in line with the Chief of Defence's priorities

[5393] Strengthening the department commander system and increasing the number of department commanders is of great importance for increasing safety in both the implementation of operations and exercises, and will increase the efficiency of the Armed Forces' departments

[5394] The Norwegian Armed Forces' education system is initially of very high quality and functions well

[5395] Therefore, no major changes are recommended in this area

[5396] The adjustments being made will clarify the inspectors general's responsibility and authority for education from the recruit school level up to and including the war school level, and are in line with the Chief of Defence's recommendation

[5397] The Chief of Defence also supports the comprehensive and effective utilisation of the Defence Forces' overall competence environments as proposed in the proposal, including by strengthening cooperation between schools that provide accredited university education

[5398] In addition to cooperation between the Armed Forces' own schools, cooperation with both civilian educational institutions in Norway and with foreign expertise environments should be strengthened

[5399] In this context, the Chief of Defence will particularly highlight the potential he believes lies in further developing cooperation between Sweden and Norway within advanced officer education

[5400] Conscription

[5401] In addition, the Home Guard will continue to be completely dependent on conscripts in the future

[5402] Furthermore, conscription plays a crucial role in relation to the Defence's recruitment capacity

[5403] It is therefore crucial that conscription is retained and practiced in line with the needs of the Armed Forces

[5404] To ensure the continued legitimacy of military service, it is crucial that those subject to military service themselves perceive their initial service as meaningful

[5405] The Chief of Defence would like to emphasize that the right approach to the practice of military service, according to the conscripts' own assessment, is not about as many people as possible serving, but about those who are called up being compensated in a financially and status-wise reasonable manner

[5406] Focus on the content and quality of the service must therefore be maintained and the work to raise the status of conscripts who are completing their first-time service must be continued

[5407] The long-term proposal proposes a change to the session scheme that is largely in line with the Chief of Defence's recommendation, but goes one step further by recommending that both part 1 and part 2 of the new session scheme be made mandatory for women

[5408] The Chief of Defence wishes to continue and intensify the work of increasing the proportion of women in the Defence Forces, and sees mandatory sessions for women as part of this work

[5409] The Home Guard The long-term proposal aims to continue and follow up on the quality reform in the Home Guard, with particular emphasis on equipment, training level and response capability

[5410] As a basis for continuing the quality reform, a reduction in the number of districts is planned

[5411] This is in line with the Chief of Defence's recommendation

[5412] In addition, the proposal calls for a reduction in the force structure by 5,000 personnel and a continuation of the current three categories of Homeland Security forces

[5413] The Chief of Defence considers that the Home Guard is one of the few parts of the defence structure that is still scalable and yet financially and competence-wise sustainable

[5414] The recommended arrangement will largely continue the Home Guard's ability to protect important infrastructure, support national crisis management, reinforce military presence as needed, and provide support to civil society, although with somewhat reduced endurance or lower ambition in relation to the number of security targets

[5415] In the longer term, it would be appropriate to assess whether there is potential for developing greater synergy and increased operational capability through closer cooperation, a division of functions or a merger of the Army and the Home Guard

[5416] Cooperation with allies and partners For small nations, it is increasingly a challenge to be able to maintain a defense structure with all the units and capabilities that such a structure has traditionally encompassed

[5417] Reduced defense appropriations, combined with rising prices for defense equipment and rising operating costs, have led to certain operational elements in the structure, both in Norway and in other small countries, being at or rapidly approaching critical mass, that is, a level that is neither financially nor competencewise sustainable

[5418] In order to retain more of the capacities that small countries cannot in reality retain individually, it will be crucial to increasingly establish multinational cooperative solutions, particularly within logistics and force production

[5419] In this context, the Chief of Defence has, as part of Defence Policy 158 St.prop

[5420] No. 48 2007–

[5421] A defense to protect Norway's security, interests and values. In 2007, a feasibility study was conducted together with the Swedish Defense Forces

[5422] The study shows that there is significant potential for cooperation with Sweden, both in logistics, training, exercises, education and a number of other areas

[5423] Any closer cooperation with Sweden should not hinder, or replace, already established or potential cooperation solutions with allies or other nations, but should supplement them

[5424] There is a growing trend towards closer European defense cooperation and integration

[5425] Norwegian-Swedish cooperation in this area would therefore be forward-looking and in line with such developments

[5426] The long-term proposal's mention of these possibilities is thus in line with the Chief of Defence's recommendation, and the work of concretising and operationalising collaborative solutions within this framework should be given priority. Conclusion

[5427] The Chief of Defence has had two main objectives with his military-technical recommendation for the further development of the Armed Forces

[5428] Firstly, to further develop a standing military force with up-to-date military capabilities to provide the political authorities with a security policy tool that provides freedom of action to meet crises and challenges both nationally and internationally

[5429] Secondly, to develop a defense in long-term structural and economic balance within a budget that is continued at the 2008 level plus annual wage and price compensation

[5430] The main measures identified to establish a long-term balanced defence structure are a significant rationalisation of the base structure and the concentration of the Armed Forces' activities in fewer locations to reduce operating costs, an increased focus on multinational cooperation, particularly within logistics and strengthening production, to reduce costs within these areas and a necessary reduction of the operational structure through the removal of the relatively least critical and important capacities

[5431] Considered overall and overall, the recommendations of the long-term proposal are largely in line with the development that the Chief of Defence believes is necessary for the Defence to ensure the greatest possible operational capability, while establishing a structure that is functionally and financially balanced in the long term

[5432] However, the proposal assumes a higher budget level than that which was the basis for the Chief of Defence's recommendation

[5433] This implies a prioritization of the Armed Forces that the Chief of Defence welcomes

[5434] If such an increase is to have the intended effect, however, a long-term perspective must be established for future budgets by following up the proposed increase in coming years with budgets at a minimum equivalent level, plus wage and price compensation

[5435] Predictable budget frameworks are therefore more important for the Armed Forces than a short-term increase in budgets for one or a few years

[5436] Stable and predictable resource allocation

[5437] combined with a continuous focus on shielding operational capability by exploiting the potential that still exists in the base and support structure

[5438] will be able to ensure a defense in long-term financial and structural balance, with sufficient ability to solve the Defense's future tasks
